                '<td class="mnum">'+int(d.clicks)+'</td><td class="mnum">'+int(d.conversions)+'</td>'+
                '<td class="mnum">'+dec(d.frequency,2)+'</td><td class="mnum">'+pctv(d.ctr)+'</td>'+
                '<td class="mnum">'+cents(d.cpa_cents)+'</td><td class="mnum">'+dec(d.roas,2)+'</td></tr>';
            }).join('') +
          '</tbody></table></div></div>'
        : '') +
    '</div>' +

    '<div class="dw-sec"><div class="eyebrow" style="margin-bottom:8px">RECENT ACTIONS</div>' +
      '<div class="dw-tbl"><div class="tblscroll"><table class="grid"><thead><tr><th>When</th><th>Actor</th><th>Rule</th><th>Reason</th><th>Change</th><th>Outcome</th><th>Revert</th></tr></thead>' +
      '<tbody>'+actRows+'</tbody></table></div></div>' +
      '<p class="note" style="margin-top:7px">This campaign and its ad sets only. Newest 50.</p>' +
    '</div>';

  var ds = document.getElementById('dwDays');
  /* days= is a SERVER parameter — the window is applied by the endpoint's
     `m.date > CURRENT_DATE - $2 days`, so it has to be re-read. There is no
     client-side series to narrow instead: until /detail answers there are no
     days on this screen at all. */
  if(ds) ds.addEventListener('change', function(){
    DW.days = Number(ds.value);
    if(DW.detail) loadDetail(DW.id); else renderDrawerBody();
  });
  document.querySelectorAll('#dwMetrics button').forEach(function(b){
    b.addEventListener('click', function(){ DW.metric = b.dataset.m; renderDrawerBody(); });
  });
  hookChart(series, DW.metric);
  host.querySelectorAll('[data-cw]').forEach(function(btn){
    btn.addEventListener('click', function(){
      var action = btn.getAttribute('data-cw');
      var msg = document.getElementById('cwMsg');
      /* re-checked here as well as on the disabled attribute above: nothing may
         be sent when this screen has no partner at all. partner_id is sent only
         when the address names one — a partner login is pinned server-side and
         sending a null would be worse than sending nothing. */
      if (!hasPartnerScope()) {
        if (msg) msg.textContent = 'Nothing was sent. Pick a partner first.';
        return;
      }
      var sendPid = partnerParam();
      var body = { campaign_id: c.id, action: action, reason: 'campaign-manager drawer' };
      if (sendPid) body.partner_id = sendPid;
      if (action === 'update_budget') {
        var el = document.getElementById('cwBudget');
        var n = el ? Number(el.value) : NaN;
        if (!Number.isFinite(n) || n < 100) {
          if (msg) msg.textContent = 'Enter a daily budget of at least 100 cents.';
          return;
        }
        body.budget_cents = Math.round(n);
      }
      /* UI-STANDARDS §5: these three spend a partner's real money on Meta, so
         each names its consequence and waits for a yes. The campaign is named
         in the question because the drawer opens on whichever row was clicked,
         and all three buttons sit together inside it. */
      var name = c.name || 'this campaign';
      var money = function (v) {
        return (Number(v) / 100).toLocaleString('en-US', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });
      };
      var ask =
        action === 'pause'
          ? 'Stop spending on “' + name + '” on Meta?\n\nIts ads stop being shown and it stops spending. It stays stopped until somebody starts it again.'
        : action === 'resume'
          ? 'Start spending on “' + name + '” again on Meta?\n\nIts ads start being shown again and it starts spending against its daily budget straight away.'
        : action === 'update_budget'
          ? 'Change the daily budget for “' + name + '” to ' + money(body.budget_cents) + '?\n\n' +
            'That is what this partner’s ad account is allowed to spend on this campaign every day, from now on. ' +
            'It is now ' + (c.budget_cents == null ? 'not set' : money(c.budget_cents)) + '.'
          : 'Send “' + action + '” for “' + name + '” to Meta?';
      if (!window.confirm(ask)) {
        if (msg) msg.textContent = 'Nothing was sent — you cancelled.';
        return;
      }
      if (msg) msg.textContent = 'Sending to Meta…';
      var t = '';
      try { t = localStorage.getItem('fh_token') || ''; } catch (e) { t = ''; }
      fetch('/api/campaigns/write', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: {
          accept: 'application/json',
          'content-type': 'application/json',
          ...(t && t !== 'demo' ? { authorization: 'Bearer ' + t } : {})
        },
        body: JSON.stringify(body)
      }).then(function (r) { return r.json().catch(function () { return { ok: false }; }); })
        .then(function (res) {
          if (!res.ok) {
            /* Nothing changed. Say so first, then whatever reason came back in
               words — the guardrail reasons carry their own message, so no
               error code has to be shown to explain this (UI-STANDARDS §6). */
            var why = res.message ||
              (res.reasons || []).map(function (r) { return r && r.message; })
                .filter(function (s) { return !!s; }).join(' · ');
            if (msg) msg.textContent = 'Nothing changed on Meta. ' +
              (why || 'No reason was given. Try again in a moment.');
            return;
          }
          /* only reached on ok:true — nothing here reports a success Meta did
             not confirm */
          if (msg) msg.textContent =
            action === 'pause' ? 'Meta has stopped spending on this campaign.'
            : action === 'resume' ? 'Meta is spending on this campaign again.'
            : action === 'update_budget' ? 'Meta has the new daily budget.'
            : 'Meta accepted the change.';
          if (typeof wireAll === 'function') wireAll();
          loadDetail(DW.id);
        });
    });
  });
}

/* hover layer — crosshair + tooltip, the default for any plotted chart here */
function hookChart(series, mk){
  var wrap = document.getElementById('dwChart');
  if(!wrap || !series.length) return;
  var svg = wrap.querySelector('svg'), tip = document.getElementById('dwTip'),
      cur = wrap.querySelector('#dwCursor'), m = metricDef(mk);
  /* chartSVG returns a plain empty-state div when every value for this metric is
     null — cpa_cents on days with no conversions, for instance — so there is
     nothing to hover. */
  if(!svg || !tip) return;
  var L = 52, R = 14, W = 720;
  function move(e){
    var r = svg.getBoundingClientRect();
    var vx = (e.clientX - r.left) / r.width * W;
    var t = (vx - L) / (W - L - R);
    var i = Math.round(t * (series.length - 1));
    if(i < 0) i = 0; if(i > series.length - 1) i = series.length - 1;
    var d = series[i];
    var px = L + (W - L - R) * (series.length === 1 ? 0.5 : i/(series.length-1));
    if(cur){ cur.setAttribute('x1', px); cur.setAttribute('x2', px); cur.style.opacity = 1; }
    tip.innerHTML = esc(d.date) + '<br>' + esc(m.label) + ' &nbsp;<b>' + m.fmt(d[mk]) + '</b>';
    tip.classList.add('on');
    var left = (px / W) * r.width;
    tip.style.left = Math.max(4, Math.min(r.width - tip.offsetWidth - 4, left - tip.offsetWidth/2)) + 'px';
    tip.style.top = '6px';
  }
  svg.addEventListener('mousemove', move);
  svg.addEventListener('mouseleave', function(){ tip.classList.remove('on'); if(cur) cur.style.opacity = 0; });
}

/* loadDetail — the CM-05 read. Fires on open and on a window change, and is the
   reason the detail row in CM-01 has a source at all. A stale response (the user
   opened another campaign while this one was in flight) is dropped on the seq
   check rather than painting the wrong campaign. */
function loadDetail(id){
  var seq = ++DW.seq;
  SRC.detail = { source:'…', note:'', rows:null };
  renderSources();
  return apiGet(scoped('/api/campaigns/detail?id=' + encodeURIComponent(id) + '&days=' + DW.days))
    .then(function(res){
      if(seq !== DW.seq) return res;                 /* a newer open won */
      if(res.ok && res.data && res.data.id){
        DW.detail = res.data;
        SRC.detail = { source:'api', rows:1,
          note:'loaded · ' + ((res.data.ad_sets||[]).length) + ' ad sets · ' +
               ((res.data.metrics_daily||[]).length) + ' days · ' +
               ((res.data.recent_actions||[]).length) + ' actions' };
      } else {
        DW.detail = null;                            /* nothing to show, not a guess */
        /* the same plain sentence the panels use — no status code and no raw
           API string in the note (UI-STANDARDS §6) */
        SRC.detail = { source: res.ok ? 'api' : res.source, rows: res.ok ? 0 : null,
          note: res.ok ? 'loaded, but no campaign came back' : readFailureText(res) };
      }
      renderDrawerBody();
      renderSources();
      return res;
    });
}

function openDrawer(id){
  DW.id = id; DW.days = 30; DW.metric = 'spend_cents'; DW.detail = null;
  var c = CAMP_BY_ID[id];
  document.getElementById('dwTitle').textContent = c ? c.name : 'not_found';
  renderDrawerBody();
  document.getElementById('drawer').classList.add('on');
  document.getElementById('drawer').setAttribute('aria-hidden','false');
  document.getElementById('scrim').classList.add('on');
  document.getElementById('dwClose').focus();
  loadDetail(id);
}
function closeDrawer(){
  DW.seq++;                       /* anything still in flight no longer applies */
  if(SRC.detail && SRC.detail.source === '…'){
    SRC.detail = { source:'…', note:'', rows:null };
    renderSources();
  }
  document.getElementById('drawer').classList.remove('on');
  document.getElementById('drawer').setAttribute('aria-hidden','true');
  document.getElementById('scrim').classList.remove('on');
}
document.getElementById('dwClose').addEventListener('click', closeDrawer);
document.getElementById('scrim').addEventListener('click', closeDrawer);
document.addEventListener('keydown', function(e){ if(e.key === 'Escape') closeDrawer(); });

/* ══ CM-01 · SCOPE + PER-PANEL STATUS ════════════════════════════════════ */
var PANELS = [
  { key:'spend',    label:'spend vs limits'  },
  { key:'list',     label:'campaigns'        },
  { key:'detail',   label:'campaign detail'  },
  { key:'fatigue',  label:'creative fatigue' },
  { key:'conn',     label:'connections'      },
  { key:'log',      label:'action log'       }
];
var SRC = {};
PANELS.forEach(function(p){ SRC[p.key] = { source:'…', note:'', rows:null }; });
/* CM-09 ad performance is NOT one of the five PANELS above — it is org-wide
   (no partner_id on the endpoint), not part of the "pick a partner" gate below,
   and not part of the "X of 5 panels loaded" count. It gets its own SRC entry
   so panelUnread('adbooks') and panelRow() work exactly like every other panel. */
SRC.adbooks = { source:'…', note:'', rows:null };
/* CM-10 funnel pages is the same shape as CM-09 just above: org-wide, staff-
   only, its own SRC entry, not one of the five and not in the loadWarn banner. */
SRC.funnelPages = { source:'…', note:'', rows:null };
/* CM-11 the label spine is the same shape again: org-wide, staff-only, its own
   SRC entry, not one of the five and not in the loadWarn banner. */
SRC.adspine = { source:'…', note:'', rows:null };
/* '…' is the in-flight marker wireAll seeds every panel with, not an outcome —
   painting it like a failure reports six errors while nothing has failed yet. */
function tone(src){ return src==='api' ? 'real' : src==='…' ? 'reading'
  : (src==='demo'||src==='notfound'||src==='badrequest'||src==='nodata') ? 'sample' : 'error'; }
/* The Panel / Status / Rows table this used to paint is gone (owner call,
   2026-08-17): it was repair-shop wording at the top of a customer screen.
   The honesty it carried is kept in three cheaper places — this one line, the
   plain sentence each panel prints in its own body, and the footer count.
   SILENT unless a panel was actually turned down. '…' is the in-flight marker,
   never a failure, so a screen still reading says nothing at all. */
function renderSources(){
  var el = document.getElementById('loadWarn');
  if(!el) return;
  var bad = PANELS.filter(function(p){
    var src = SRC[p.key].source;
    return src !== 'api' && src !== '…';
  });
  if(!bad.length){ el.hidden = true; el.textContent = ''; return; }
  /* The reason shown is the panel's own sentence — the same words its body
     shows, never a status code (UI-STANDARDS §6). */
  var names = bad.map(function(p){ return p.label; });
  var list = names.length === 1 ? names[0]
    : names.slice(0,-1).join(', ') + ' and ' + names[names.length-1];
  var why = '';
  for(var i=0;i<bad.length;i++){ if(SRC[bad[i].key].note){ why = SRC[bad[i].key].note; break; } }
  el.innerHTML = '<b>' + esc(list.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + list.slice(1)) +
    ' did not load.</b> ' + esc(why);
  el.hidden = false;
}
/* Partner names come only from GET /api/read/partners (FHData.partners).
   Empty or failed → honest empty. Never a built-in roster. */
var PARTNER_LIST = [];
function partnerNameFor(id){
  if(!id) return null;
  for(var i=0;i<PARTNER_LIST.length;i++){
    if(PARTNER_LIST[i].id === id) return PARTNER_LIST[i].name || null;
  }
  return null;
}
function renderScope(){
  var scoped = hasPartnerScope();
  var name = partnerNameFor(partnerParam());
  document.getElementById('scopeName').textContent = name || (scoped ? 'Your partner' : 'No partner selected');
  document.getElementById('scopeHow').textContent = scoped
    ? 'Spend is this partner’s ads today. One partner at a time.'
    : 'Pick a partner from the list to see their ads.';
  renderSources();
}
function loadPartnerPicker(){
  var sel = document.getElementById('partnerSel');
  if(!sel) return;
  /* data.js is deferred. This block used to run during parse, before
     FHData existed, and lock the list on "Could not load partners"
     even when the partner read itself was fine. Wait until the data
     script is ready, then ask. */
  if(!window.FHData || typeof FHData.partners !== 'function'){
    if(document.readyState === 'loading'){
      document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', loadPartnerPicker, { once: true });
      return;
    }
    sel.innerHTML = '<option value="">Could not load partners</option>';
    sel.disabled = true;
    return;
  }
  FHData.partners({ limit: 200 }).then(function(res){
    if(!res.ok){
      PARTNER_LIST = [];
      sel.innerHTML = '<option value="">Could not load partners</option>';
      sel.disabled = true;
      renderScope();
      return;
    }
    var items = (res.data && res.data.items) || [];
    PARTNER_LIST = items;
    if(!items.length){
      sel.innerHTML = '<option value="">No partners on file</option>';
      sel.disabled = true;
      renderScope();
      return;
    }
    var cur = partnerParam() || '';
    sel.disabled = false;
    sel.innerHTML = '<option value="">Choose a partner</option>' +
      items.map(function(p){
        return '<option value="'+esc(p.id)+'">'+esc(p.name || p.slug || '')+'</option>';
      }).join('');
    if(cur) sel.value = cur;
    renderScope();
  });
}
/* ══ FILTER CONTROLS ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
document.getElementById('partnerSel').addEventListener('change', function(){
  var id = this.value;
  var url = new URL(location.href);
  if(id) url.searchParams.set('partner_id', id);
  else url.searchParams.delete('partner_id');
  location.assign(url.pathname + url.search + url.hash);
});
document.getElementById('fPlatform').addEventListener('change', function(){ UI.campPlatform = this.value; renderCampaigns(true); });
document.getElementById('fOffer').addEventListener('change',    function(){ UI.campOffer    = this.value; renderCampaigns(true); });
document.getElementById('fLimit').addEventListener('change',    function(){ UI.campLimit = Number(this.value); renderCampaigns(true); });
/* days= is applied by the endpoint (`d.date > CURRENT_DATE - $3 days`, capped at
   30), so changing the window has to re-read it. Re-rendering the rows already in
   memory would leave 7-day rows under a footer claiming 30 — the one caption on
   this screen that could assert something the data does not back. */
document.getElementById('fDays').addEventListener('change',     function(){ UI.fatDays = Number(this.value); renderFatigue(); readFatigue(); });
/* Same reason as fDays just above: days= is a SERVER window, so changing it has
   to re-read. Re-rendering would leave 7-day rows under a 30-day footer. */
document.getElementById('spineDays').addEventListener('change', function(){ UI.spineDays = Number(this.value); readAdSpine(); });
document.getElementById('fTarget').addEventListener('change',   function(){ UI.logTarget = this.value; renderLog(); });
document.getElementById('fRule').addEventListener('change',     function(){ UI.logRule = this.value; renderLog(); });

/* ══ API WIRING ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   The reader contract is public/app/data.js's: every call resolves, never
   rejects, and returns { ok, source, data, error }. FHData exposes readers for
   /api/read/* and /api/dashboard/*, not for /api/campaigns/*, so the same
   envelope is reproduced here rather than reaching into its private get().

   A panel that cannot be read SHOWS AN ERROR STATE saying what failed, and says
   so again per panel in CM-01. It never keeps furniture from a read that did not
   answer, and it never reports a bad filter as an outage.
   ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
function apiGet(path){
  var demo = false, tok = '';
  try { demo = localStorage.getItem('fh_demo') === '1'; tok = localStorage.getItem('fh_token') || ''; } catch(e){}
  if(demo) return Promise.resolve({ ok:false, source:'demo', data:null, error:'demo session — no backend read attempted' });
  var started;
  try {
    started = fetch(path, { headers: tok ? { accept:'application/json', authorization:'Bearer '+tok } : { accept:'application/json' } });
  } catch(e){
    return Promise.resolve({ ok:false, source:'offline', data:null, error:(e && e.message) || 'fetch unavailable' });
  }
  return Promise.resolve(started).then(function(r){
    if(r.status === 401 || r.status === 403) return { ok:false, source:'unauthorized', data:null, error:'not signed in' };
    if(r.status === 404){
      return r.json().then(function(d){
        return (d && d.error === 'not_found' && typeof d.path === 'string')
          ? { ok:false, source:'offline', data:null, error:'/api/* not deployed' }
          : { ok:false, source:'notfound', data:null, error:'no such record' };
      }).catch(function(){ return { ok:false, source:'offline', data:null, error:'/api/* not deployed' }; });
    }
    if(r.status === 400){
      return r.json().then(function(d){
        return { ok:false, source:'badrequest', data:null, error:(d && d.message) || 'That request was not accepted.' };
      }).catch(function(){ return { ok:false, source:'badrequest', data:null, error:'bad request' }; });
    }
    return r.json().then(function(d){
      if(r.status === 503 || (d && d.db === 'down')) return { ok:false, source:'nodb', data:null, error:(d && d.message) || 'The database is not reachable right now.' };
      /* 500 query_failed here is very often this screen's own bad ?state=, not a
         backend outage — stateFilter throws and the catch turns it into a 500. */
      if(!d || d.ok !== true) return { ok:false, source:'nodb', data:null, error:(d && d.message) || 'Something went wrong. Try again in a moment.' };
      return { ok:true, source:'api', data:d, error:null };
    }).catch(function(){ return { ok:false, source:'offline', data:null, error:'response was not JSON' }; });
  }).catch(function(e){
    return { ok:false, source:'offline', data:null, error:(e && e.message) || 'network error' };
  });
}

function scoped(path){
  var qp = partnerParam();
  return qp ? path + (path.indexOf('?') === -1 ? '?' : '&') + 'partner_id=' + encodeURIComponent(qp) : path;
}

/* One plain sentence for the panel body: what failed, and what to do next.
   Deliberately not the endpoint's own error string, which is never shown. */
function readFailureText(res){
  if(res.source === 'demo') return 'This is a demo session. Nothing was loaded.';
  if(res.source === 'unauthorized') return 'You are not signed in for this data, so nothing was read. Sign in and press Reload.';
  if(res.source === 'notfound') return 'There is nothing here to show.';
  if(res.source === 'badrequest'){
    return partnerParam()
      ? 'This could not load. Press Reload to try again.'
      : 'Pick a partner to see their ads.';
  }
  if(res.source === 'nodb') return 'We could not reach the data. Press Reload to try again.';
  return 'This could not be read right now. Press Reload to try again.';
}

function wirePanel(key, path, apply){
  return apiGet(scoped(path)).then(function(res){
    var s = SRC[key];
    /* THE OUTCOME IS RECORDED BEFORE apply() RUNS. apply() re-renders panels
       that read this panel's outcome (the tiles and the attention row read all
       five), so recording it afterwards leaves the last panel to resolve
       painting itself as still reading, for good. */
    if(res.ok){
      var items = (res.data && res.data.items) || [];
      delete PANEL_MSG[key];
      s.source = 'api';
      s.note = '';
      s.rows = items.length;
      /* apply() ALWAYS runs on a good read, including an empty one — otherwise
         rows from an earlier read would sit under a later "nothing there". */
      try { apply(items); }
      catch(e){
        PANEL_MSG[key] = 'This could not be shown. Press Reload to try again.';
        s.source = 'error'; s.note = 'This could not be shown. Press Reload to try again.'; s.rows = null;
        try { apply([]); } catch(e2){}
      }
    } else {
      /* a rejected read clears the panel and says why — it never leaves rows up.
         The note is the SAME plain sentence the panel body shows, so this table
         never prints a status code or the API's own error string beside it
         (UI-STANDARDS §6). */
      PANEL_MSG[key] = readFailureText(res);
      s.source = res.source;
      s.note = PANEL_MSG[key];
      s.rows = null;
      try { apply([]); } catch(e){}
    }
    renderSources();
    return res;
  });
}

/* The one place the fatigue window is sent, called by wireAll and again by the
   CM-06 Window select — a client-side re-render cannot change a server window. */
function readFatigue(){
  return wirePanel('fatigue', '/api/campaigns/fatigue?state=all&days=' + UI.fatDays, function(items){
    FATIGUE = items; renderFatigue();
  });
}

/* GET /api/read/ad-books. Reproduces wirePanel's outcome contract by hand
   rather than calling wirePanel itself: the response is { ok, groups, ... },
   not { ok, data:{ items } }, so wirePanel's items-only unwrap does not fit it.
   Not run through scoped() — the endpoint takes no partner_id, org comes off
   the session — so this never sends partner_id even when one is picked above. */
function readAdBooks(){
  return apiGet('/api/read/ad-books?group_by=' + encodeURIComponent(UI.adBooksGroupBy)).then(function(res){
    var s = SRC.adbooks;
    if(res.ok){
      delete PANEL_MSG.adbooks;
      s.source = 'api';
      s.note = '';
      s.rows = (res.data && res.data.groups) ? res.data.groups.length : 0;
      try { ADBOOKS = res.data; renderAdBooks(); }
      catch(e){
        PANEL_MSG.adbooks = 'This could not be shown. Press Reload to try again.';
        s.source = 'error'; s.note = PANEL_MSG.adbooks; s.rows = null;
        try { ADBOOKS = null; renderAdBooks(); } catch(e2){}
      }
    } else {
      PANEL_MSG.adbooks = readFailureText(res);
      s.source = res.source;
      s.note = PANEL_MSG.adbooks;
      s.rows = null;
      try { ADBOOKS = null; renderAdBooks(); } catch(e){}
    }
    return res;
  });
}

function isPartnerLogin(){
  try { return localStorage.getItem('fh_role') === 'partner'; } catch(e){ return false; }
}

function wireAll(){
  PANELS.forEach(function(p){ SRC[p.key] = { source:'…', note:'', rows:null }; });
  SRC.detail = { source:'…', note:'', rows:null };
  SRC.adbooks = { source:'…', note:'', rows:null };
  SRC.funnelPages = { source:'…', note:'', rows:null };
  SRC.adspine = { source:'…', note:'', rows:null };
  renderSources();

  /* Ad performance (CM-09) is org-wide, not this partner book — the endpoint
     takes no partner_id — so it reads here regardless of which branch below
     runs, and is not one of the "0 of 5 panels loaded" five.

     STAFF ONLY. Found by adversarial review 2026-09-07: this used to fire
     for every session, but /api/read/ad-books gates on ROLE_SETS.STAFF,
     which a partner login is never in — the request always 403s for one.
     Firing it anyway showed "you are not signed in for this data," which is
     false; a partner IS signed in, just not staff. A partner never sees this
     card long enough to matter (this screen redirects them home), but the
     message should still be true for the moment it is visible. */
  if (isPartnerLogin()) {
    PANEL_MSG.adbooks = 'This report is for staff. It is not part of a partner login.';
    SRC.adbooks = { source:'forbidden', note:PANEL_MSG.adbooks, rows:null };
    try { renderAdBooks(); } catch(e){}
  } else {
    readAdBooks();
  }

  /* Funnel pages (CM-10) is the same shape: org-wide, staff-only, reads here
     regardless of the branch below. */
  if (isPartnerLogin()) {
    PANEL_MSG.funnelPages = 'This report is for staff. It is not part of a partner login.';
    SRC.funnelPages = { source:'forbidden', note:PANEL_MSG.funnelPages, rows:null };
    try { renderFunnelPages(); } catch(e){}
  } else {
    readFunnelPages();
  }

  /* Label spine (CM-11) is the same shape a third time: org-wide, staff-only, and
     /api/read/ad-spine gates on ROLE_SETS.STAFF (api/read/ad-spine.mjs:605), which
     a partner login is never in. Firing it for one would show "you are not signed
     in", which is false — they are signed in, just not staff. */
  if (isPartnerLogin()) {
    PANEL_MSG.adspine = 'This report is for staff. It is not part of a partner login.';
    SRC.adspine = { source:'forbidden', note:PANEL_MSG.adspine, rows:null };
    try { renderAdSpine(); } catch(e){}
  } else {
    readAdSpine();
  }
  funnelScopeUi();

  /* Staff with no partner in the address: do not call the five reads.
     They answer 400 and the panels used to look like a broken book.
     A partner login has no partner_id in the address — the server pins
     their book — so they still read. */
  if (!partnerParam() && !isPartnerLogin()) {
    var pick = 'Pick a partner to see their ads.';
    PANELS.forEach(function(p){
      PANEL_MSG[p.key] = pick;
      SRC[p.key] = { source:'badrequest', note:pick, rows:null };
    });
    try { renderSpend(); } catch(e){}
    try { renderCampaigns(true); } catch(e){}
    try { renderFatigue(); } catch(e){}
    try { renderConn(); } catch(e){}
    try { renderLog(); } catch(e){}
    try { renderAdBooks(); } catch(e){}
    try { renderFunnelPages(); } catch(e){}
    try { renderAdSpine(); } catch(e){}
    try { renderTiles(); } catch(e){}
    try { renderAttention(); } catch(e){}
    renderSources();
    renderScope();
    syncScopeUi();
    funnelScopeUi();
    document.getElementById('footNote').textContent = '0 of 5 panels loaded';
    if (window.FHData && FHData.banner) FHData.banner('sample', 'Campaigns — pick a partner to load their ads.', 'campaigns');
    return;
  }

  Promise.all([
    wirePanel('spend', '/api/campaigns/spend?state=all', function(items){
      CEILINGS = items.map(ceil_); renderSpend(); renderTiles(); renderAttention();
    }),
    wirePanel('list', '/api/campaigns/list?state=all&limit=200', function(items){
      CAMPAIGNS = items; reindex(); renderCampaigns(true); renderTiles(); renderAttention();
    }),
    readFatigue(),
    wirePanel('conn', '/api/campaigns/connections?state=all', function(items){
      CONNECTIONS = items; reindex(); renderConn(); renderAttention();
    }),
    wirePanel('log', '/api/campaigns/action-log?state=all&limit=200', function(items){
      ACTIONS = items; renderLog(); renderAttention();
    })
  ]).then(function(res){
    /* The bottom banner is the last thing a person reads before they believe the
       screen. It used to spell out reader codes — "spend:badrequest · list:
       badrequest" — which says nothing to whoever is looking at it. It now counts
       what answered and repeats the first plain reason, same words as the panel
       (UI-STANDARDS §6). */
    var worst = 'real', good = 0, bad = 0, first = '';
    PANELS.forEach(function(p){
      var s = SRC[p.key];
      if(s.source === '…') return;
      var t = tone(s.source);
      if(t === 'error') worst = 'error';
      else if(t === 'sample' && worst !== 'error') worst = 'sample';
      if(s.source === 'api') good++;
      else { bad++; if(!first) first = PANEL_MSG[p.key] || ''; }
    });
    var total = good + bad;
    var msg = !total ? 'Campaigns — nothing has been read yet'
      : bad ? 'Campaigns — ' + good + ' of ' + total + ' panels loaded. ' +
              (first || 'The rest could not be read. Press Reload to try again.')
      : 'Campaigns — everything loaded';
    /* the same count in the same words — no endpoint path, and no "read-only",
       which stopped being true when the Meta controls landed */
    document.getElementById('footNote').textContent =
      total ? good + ' of ' + total + ' panels loaded' : 'nothing loaded yet';
    if(window.FHData && FHData.banner) FHData.banner(worst === 'real' ? 'real' : worst, msg, 'campaigns');
    /* one settle pass now every panel's outcome is known — the tiles, the
       attention row and the ceiling chip each read more than one panel */
    renderSpend();
    renderTiles();
    renderAttention();
    /* the reads are the only proof a PARTNER login has a scope — re-decide the
       scope panel and the write control now that they have answered */
    renderScope();
    syncScopeUi();
    funnelScopeUi();
  });
}
document.getElementById('reloadBtn').addEventListener('click', wireAll);

/* A write may never be sent when this screen has no partner. The button is
   disabled in that state and says why, rather than looking live and failing on
   click. Re-run at the end of every wireAll, because a partner login only
   proves it has a scope once a read has answered. */
function syncScopeUi(){
  var btn = document.getElementById('syncMetaBtn');
  var msg = document.getElementById('syncMetaMsg');
  var ok = hasPartnerScope();
  btn.disabled = !ok;
  if(!ok) msg.textContent = 'Pick a partner first — this needs to know whose ad account to pull.';
  else if(msg.textContent === 'Pick a partner first — this needs to know whose ad account to pull.') msg.textContent = '';
}
syncScopeUi();

/* CM-10 / CONN-07 — ClickFunnels is org-wide, not partner-scoped, so there is
   no partner check here (unlike syncScopeUi above). The only gate is staff vs
   partner login, same as the ad performance panel. */
function funnelScopeUi(){
  var partner = isPartnerLogin();
  var syncBtn = document.getElementById('funnelSyncBtn');
  var connectBtn = document.getElementById('cfConnectBtn');
  if(syncBtn) syncBtn.disabled = partner;
  if(connectBtn) connectBtn.disabled = partner;
  var msg = document.getElementById('cfConnectMsg');
  if(msg){
    if(partner) msg.textContent = 'Staff only. Not part of a partner login.';
    else if(msg.textContent === 'Staff only. Not part of a partner login.') msg.textContent = '';
  }
}
funnelScopeUi();

function authHeaders(extra){
  var t = '';
  try { t = localStorage.getItem('fh_token') || ''; } catch(e){ t = ''; }
  var h = Object.assign({ accept:'application/json' }, extra || {});
  if(t && t !== 'demo') h.authorization = 'Bearer ' + t;
  return h;
}

document.getElementById('funnelSyncBtn').addEventListener('click', function () {
  var btn = this;
  var cap = document.getElementById('funnelConnCap');
  btn.disabled = true;
  var prev = btn.textContent;
  btn.textContent = 'Syncing…';
  fetch('/api/analytics/clickfunnels-sync', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: authHeaders({ 'content-type': 'application/json' }),
    body: '{}'
  }).then(function (r) { return r.json().catch(function () { return { ok: false }; }); })
    .then(function (res) {
      btn.disabled = isPartnerLogin();
      btn.textContent = prev;
      if (!res.ok) {
        if (cap) cap.innerHTML = '<b>Sync failed.</b> ' + esc(res.message || res.error || 'Press Sync now to try again.');
        return;
      }
      readFunnelPages();
    });
});

document.getElementById('cfConnectBtn').addEventListener('click', function () {
  var msg = document.getElementById('cfConnectMsg');
  var key = (document.getElementById('cfApiKey').value || '').trim();
  var sub = (document.getElementById('cfSubdomain').value || '').trim();
  if (!key || !sub) {
    msg.textContent = 'Enter both the API key and the subdomain first.';
    return;
  }
  msg.textContent = 'Connecting…';
  fetch('/api/analytics/clickfunnels-connect', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: authHeaders({ 'content-type': 'application/json' }),
    body: JSON.stringify({ api_key: key, subdomain: sub })
  }).then(function (r) { return r.json().catch(function () { return { ok: false }; }); })
    .then(function (res) {
      if (!res.ok) {
        /* ClickFunnels' own words, verbatim, per the contract other lanes build
           to — never reworded here (same rule as connRows' errbox above). */
        msg.textContent = res.message || res.error || 'Nothing was saved. Try again.';
        return;
      }
      document.getElementById('cfApiKey').value = '';
      msg.textContent = 'Connected. Syncing now…';
      return fetch('/api/analytics/clickfunnels-sync', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: authHeaders({ 'content-type': 'application/json' }),
        body: '{}'
      }).then(function (r) { return r.json().catch(function () { return { ok: false }; }); })
        .then(function (res2) {
          msg.textContent = res2.ok
            ? 'Connected and synced.'
            : 'Connected, but the first sync did not finish. ' + (res2.message || res2.error || 'Press Sync now above to try again.');
          readFunnelPages();
        });
    });
});

document.getElementById('syncMetaBtn').addEventListener('click', function () {
  var msg = document.getElementById('syncMetaMsg');
  if (!hasPartnerScope()) {
    msg.textContent = 'Nothing was sent. Pick a partner first.';
    return;
  }
  var pid = partnerParam();
  msg.textContent = 'Syncing from Meta…';
  var t = '';
  try { t = localStorage.getItem('fh_token') || ''; } catch (e) { t = ''; }
  fetch('/api/campaigns/sync', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      accept: 'application/json',
      'content-type': 'application/json',
      ...(t && t !== 'demo' ? { authorization: 'Bearer ' + t } : {})
    },
    /* partner_id only when the address names one — a partner login is pinned
       server-side and a null here would be worse than sending nothing. */
    body: JSON.stringify(pid ? { partner_id: pid } : {})
  }).then(function (r) { return r.json().catch(function () { return { ok: false }; }); })
    .then(function (res) {
      /* The server now says in words what it saved and what it did not. A run
         that saved some campaigns and lost others answers ok:false, so the old
         'Nothing was pulled from Meta' prefix would have been a lie here — it
         is only used when the server sent no sentence of its own. */
      if (!res.ok) {
        msg.textContent = res.message ||
          'Nothing was pulled from Meta. Press Sync Meta now to try again.';
        return;
      }
      /* THE SENTENCE IS THE SERVER'S, AND THE SERVER COUNTS ONLY WHAT SAVED.
         This line used to build its own sentence out of three of the four
         counts and drop the fourth — days of numbers, which is the only one
         that says whether any SPEND landed. So a run that pulled the shape of
         an account but saved no money at all read exactly like a run that
         saved everything.

         api/campaigns/sync.mjs adds to its insight count only after that
         campaign's transaction has committed (see buildSyncResponse and the
         stats.insights += written.insights line under it), so res.message is
         rows SAVED, never rows attempted. Rebuilding it here is how the two
         wordings drift apart; the fallback stays only for an answer with no
         sentence in it. */
      msg.textContent = (res.message ||
        'Pulled in ' + (res.campaigns || 0) + ' campaigns · ' +
        (res.ad_sets || 0) + ' ad sets · ' + (res.ads || 0) + ' ads' +
        ' · ' + (res.insights || 0) + ' days of numbers') +
        (res.note ? ' · ' + res.note : '');
      wireAll();
    });
});

document.getElementById('metaAgencyBtn').addEventListener('click', function () {
  var msg = document.getElementById('metaAgencyMsg');
  if (!hasPartnerScope()) {
    msg.textContent = 'Nothing was sent. Pick a partner first.';
    return;
  }
  var biz = (document.getElementById('metaBizId').value || '').trim();
  var act = (document.getElementById('metaActId').value || '').trim();
  if (!biz) {
    msg.textContent = 'Paste the partner Meta Business ID first.';
    return;
  }
  var pid = partnerParam();
  msg.textContent = 'Sending agency request…';
  var t = '';
  try { t = localStorage.getItem('fh_token') || ''; } catch (e) { t = ''; }
  var body = { meta_business_id: biz };
  if (pid) body.partner_id = pid;
  if (act) body.ad_account_id = act;
  fetch('/api/campaigns/meta-agency', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      accept: 'application/json',
      'content-type': 'application/json',
      ...(t && t !== 'demo' ? { authorization: 'Bearer ' + t } : {})
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body)
  }).then(function (r) { return r.json().catch(function () { return { ok: false }; }); })
    .then(function (res) {
      if (!res.ok) {
        msg.textContent = 'Nothing was saved. ' + (res.message || 'Try again.');
        return;
      }
      msg.textContent = res.message ||
        'Saved. Partner admin must Approve once in Meta Business Settings → Requests.';
      wireAll();
    });
});

/* ══ CM-06b · LINK AN AD TO A CREATIVE, AND GIVE IT OUR NUMBER ═══════════
   POST /api/campaigns/link-asset. Two things, set independently: which creative
   is running on this ad, and what our own number for it is.

   WHY THIS IS A PERSON PRESSING A BUTTON. Meta's pull never asks for a creative
   (api/campaigns/sync.mjs:229) and nothing has ever pushed one of ours to Meta,
   so the two sides share no identifier at all. There is nothing to match on. A
   human picking the row is slower and correct; a name guess is instant and
   cannot be checked.

   THE AD'S INTERNAL ID IS NEVER TYPED. It comes off the row's own button.

   A BLANK FIELD IS LEFT OUT OF THE REQUEST, NOT SENT AS "". On this endpoint a
   key that is present but blank means CLEAR, and clearing the creative turns an
   ad's labels back off with no error anywhere. Absent is the only thing that
   means "leave it alone" (api/campaigns/link-asset.mjs:44-54).
   ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
var LINK = { adId:null, adName:'', assetsLoaded:false, loading:false };

/* Refusals with no sentence of their own get one written here. The rest of this
   endpoint's refusals already carry a sentence meant for a person to read — the
   number is taken, that creative belongs to another partner, our ad number is
   one to nine digits — and those are shown exactly as they came back, the same
   way the ClickFunnels box above shows its provider's own words. */
function linkPlain(res){
  switch(String((res && res.error) || '')){
    case 'unauthorized':
      return 'You are signed out. Sign in again and try once more.';
    case 'forbidden':
      return 'Your sign-in is not allowed to change this ad.';
    case 'auth_unavailable':
      return 'The system could not check who you are just now. Try again in a moment.';
    case 'offline':
      return 'The screen could not reach the server, so nothing changed.';
    case 'partner_id_required':
      return 'The screen does not know which partner this is for. Pick a partner at the top and try again.';
    case 'ad_id_required': case 'ad_id_not_a_uuid':
      return 'The screen lost track of which ad this is. Reload the page and press Label again.';
    case 'asset_id_not_a_uuid':
      return 'The screen lost track of which creative that is. Reload the page and try again.';
    case 'method_not_allowed':
      return 'That request was made the wrong way, so nothing changed. Reload the page and try again.';
  }
  /* The endpoint's own sentence, with only its first letter raised so it does not
     read as a fragment after "Nothing was saved." NEVER when it opens with a
     field name: angle_key is a real column and Angle_key is not, so a sentence
     whose first word carries an underscore is left exactly as it came back. */
  if(res && typeof res.message === 'string' && res.message){
    var firstWord = res.message.split(' ')[0];
    return firstWord.indexOf('_') === -1
      ? res.message.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + res.message.slice(1)
      : res.message;
  }
  return 'The server would not do it, and nothing changed. Try again in a moment.';
}

/* The creatives this partner has, read once, the first time somebody opens the
   box. A read that fails is SAID OUT LOUD and leaves the ad number usable —
   an empty picker with no explanation reads as "there are none". */
function loadLinkAssets(){
  if(LINK.assetsLoaded || LINK.loading) return;
  LINK.loading = true;
  var sel = document.getElementById('linkAsset');
  var msg = document.getElementById('linkMsg');
  var pid = partnerParam();
  fetch('/api/creative/library?limit=100' + (pid ? '&partner_id=' + encodeURIComponent(pid) : ''),
        { headers: authHeaders() })
    .then(function(r){ return r.json().catch(function(){ return { ok:false, error:'offline' }; }); })
    .catch(function(){ return { ok:false, error:'offline' }; })
    .then(function(res){
      LINK.loading = false;
      if(!res || !res.ok){
        msg.textContent = 'The list of creatives could not be read, so only the ad number can be set here. '
          + linkPlain(res);
        return;
      }
      LINK.assetsLoaded = true;
      var items = res.items || [];
      items.forEach(function(a){
        var o = document.createElement('option');
        o.value = a.id;
        var words = a.copy_text ? String(a.copy_text).replace(/\s+/g,' ').trim().slice(0,40) : '';
        o.textContent = [a.kind, a.format, a.created_at ? dt(a.created_at) : '']
          .filter(Boolean).join(' · ')
          + (words ? ' · ' + words : '')
          + ' · ' + String(a.id).slice(0,8);
        sel.appendChild(o);
      });
      if(!items.length){
        msg.textContent = 'There are no creatives on file for this partner yet, so only the ad number can '
          + 'be set here. Creatives are made on the Creative Factory screen.';
      }
    });
}

/* Delegated, because renderFatigue() replaces every row in this table each time
   the window or the filter changes. The listener is on the tbody, which stays. */
document.getElementById('fatRows').addEventListener('click', function(e){
  var b = e.target && e.target.closest ? e.target.closest('[data-link-ad]') : null;
  if(!b) return;
  LINK.adId = b.getAttribute('data-link-ad');
  LINK.adName = b.getAttribute('data-link-name') || '';
  var box = document.getElementById('linkBox');
  box.style.display = '';
  document.getElementById('linkWho').innerHTML =
    'Setting the creative and our ad number for <b>' + esc(LINK.adName) + '</b>. ' +
    'The screen already knows which ad this is, so there is no id to look up.';
  document.getElementById('linkMsg').textContent = '';
  document.getElementById('linkNumber').value = '';
  document.getElementById('linkAsset').value = '';
  loadLinkAssets();
  try { box.scrollIntoView({ block:'nearest' }); } catch(err) {}
});

document.getElementById('linkCloseBtn').addEventListener('click', function(){
  document.getElementById('linkBox').style.display = 'none';
  LINK.adId = null;
});

document.getElementById('linkSaveBtn').addEventListener('click', function(){
  var btn = this;
  var msg = document.getElementById('linkMsg');
  if(!LINK.adId){
    msg.textContent = 'Nothing was sent. Press Label on one of the ads above first.';
    return;
  }
  var assetId = document.getElementById('linkAsset').value;
  var number = (document.getElementById('linkNumber').value || '').trim();
  if(!assetId && !number){
    msg.textContent = 'Nothing was sent. Pick a creative, type our ad number, or both.';
    return;
  }
  var body = { ad_id: LINK.adId };
  var pid = partnerParam();
  if(pid) body.partner_id = pid;
  if(assetId) body.asset_id = assetId;
  if(number) body.fundhub_ad_number = number;

  var prev = btn.textContent;
  btn.disabled = true;
  btn.textContent = 'Saving…';
  msg.textContent = 'Saving…';
  fetch('/api/campaigns/link-asset', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: authHeaders({ 'content-type':'application/json' }),
    body: JSON.stringify(body)
  }).then(function(r){ return r.json().catch(function(){ return { ok:false, error:'offline' }; }); })
    .catch(function(){ return { ok:false, error:'offline' }; })
    .then(function(res){
      btn.disabled = false;
      btn.textContent = prev;
      if(!res || !res.ok){
        msg.textContent = 'Nothing was saved. ' + linkPlain(res);
        return;
      }
      /* THE LABELS PRINTED HERE ARE READ BACK, NOT GUESSED. The endpoint selects
         the ad's row out of v_ad_label_spine after the write and returns it, so
         this says what the database now really holds — including "still none",
         which is the answer whenever the creative has no script on it. */
      var ad = res.ad || {};
      var sp = res.spine;
      var tail;
      if(!sp){
        tail = ' The labels could not be read back just now.';
      } else {
        var labels = ['script_type','lane','angle_key','hook_key','offer_key']
          .map(function(k){ return sp[k]; })
          .filter(function(v){ return !!v; });
        if(labels.length) tail = ' It now carries these labels: ' + labels.join(', ') + '.';
        else if(ad.asset_id) tail = ' It still carries no labels: the creative it points at has no script on it.';
        else tail = ' It still carries no labels: no creative is linked to it yet.';
      }
      msg.textContent = 'Saved.'
        + (ad.fundhub_ad_number ? ' Our number for this ad is ' + ad.fundhub_ad_number + '.' : '')
        + (ad.asset_id ? ' A creative is linked to it.' : '')
        + tail;
      wireAll();
    });
});

/* ══ BOOT ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
renderScope();
renderSpend();

renderAttention();
renderCampaigns(true);
renderFatigue();

renderConn();
renderLog();
loadPartnerPicker();
wireAll();
</script>
</body>

<script>
/* FH-CCP-OPENING. A client id in the address means a file is on its way, so
   the header shows the loading state, not "No client open" (hole 5). This runs
   before the first paint — the page script waits for DOMContentLoaded, which
   is too late to stop the no-client words flashing. Same four keys, same
   order, as the page script's `id`. The class comes off at the top of the
   FHData.client() callback, whatever the read says. */
(function () {
  try {
    var q = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
    if (q.get("id") || q.get("client_id") || q.get("client") || q.get("contact")) {
      document.documentElement.classList.add("ccp-opening");
    }
  } catch (e) { /* no class: the page keeps its no-client words, as before */ }
})();
</script>

        <div class="record-id">
          <div class="record-name" id="ccp-name">Loading…</div>
          <!-- Two sets of words, and CSS picks one before the first paint:
               .ccp-idle with no client id in the address, .ccp-wait while a
               file is on its way (html.ccp-opening — see the note in <head>).
               render() and every failure branch overwrite both with setText. -->
          <div class="record-key" id="ccp-key"><span class="ccp-idle">No client open — pick one below.</span><span class="ccp-wait">Opening this client’s file…</span></div>
        </div>
        <!-- THE ONE THING THE PERSON CAME FOR: what to do next on this file.
             Owner-set 2026-09-06 — the slot used to hold a count of bank answers
             missing a dollar amount, which is bookkeeping, not an instruction.
             That count now sits beside the bank rows it is about, in the
             Funding · Apply door card below.

             ONE ANSWER, NOT TWO. The step here is the one the system worked out.
             The stale string saved on the record used to sit right under it in a
             second line, and a paragraph under THAT explained why the two did
             not agree — three sentences where one was wanted. The saved string
             is still kept, quietly, under Details at the bottom of the column.

             GATE A still holds: this slot only ever shows a worked-out step,
             never the string typed onto the client record. See paintNextAction()
             and the FH-CCP block at the top of this file's script. -->
        <div class="na-step">
          <div class="eyebrow na-eyebrow">Do this next</div>
          <!-- NOT A DASH. With no file open this slot is the biggest text on the
               screen, and a lone dash there reads as a screen that failed rather
               than one waiting to be pointed at a client. paintNextAction()
               replaces this the moment a file is opened, and it is the ONLY
               thing allowed to write here (GATE A) — which is why this is
               static markup and not a setText() call. While a file is on its

<script>
/* Groups fold. */
document.querySelectorAll('.group-title.tog').forEach(function(t){
  t.addEventListener('click', function(){
    var body = document.getElementById(t.getAttribute('aria-controls'));
    var open = t.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true';
    t.setAttribute('aria-expanded', open ? 'false' : 'true');
    body.hidden = open;
    /* A header that names its state says the state it is in now (hole N21). */
    var state = t.querySelector('.tog-state');
    if (state) state.textContent = state.getAttribute(open ? 'data-shut' : 'data-open');
  });
});
</script>

<!-- Live file only. Missing fields stay a dash. Never a sample person. -->
<script defer src="data.js"></script>
<script src="proxy-apply.js"></script>
<script src="money-input.js"></script>
<script defer src="ccp-declines.js"></script>
<script>
/* FH-CCP-BEGIN
   THE TWO DECISIONS ON THIS SCREEN THAT CAN QUIETLY BECOME A LIE, kept pure
   and out of the DOM so they can be run with no browser by
   src/http/client-panel-screen.test.mjs — the same technique as
   pipeline.html's FH-LENS block. No DOM, no network, nothing that writes. */
(function () {
  "use strict";

  var UNKNOWN = "—";

  /* ── MONEY: THE UNIT IS WHOLE DOLLARS ────────────────────────────────────
     Every money value this screen shows is DOLLARS. Not cents. Traced, not
     assumed:

       funding_rounds.approved_amount and clients.funded_amount —
         numeric(14,2), db/schema/001_init.sql:58 and :127. node-postgres
         registers no parser for numeric (type 1700), so both arrive in
         JavaScript as a STRING: "50000.00" means $50,000. The demo seed
         writes funded_amount 47500.00 for a funded client
         (db/migrations/094_demo_logins.sql:227), which is $47,500.
       custom_fields.total_funding_estimate / analyzer_prequal_amount —
         written in dollars as a NUMBER by
         src/handlers/client-lifecycle.mjs:449, from crs.mjs's fundingEstimate;
         the fixture in src/adapters/crs.test.mjs:63 pins it at 80000 for an
         $80,000 pre-approval.

     THESE ARE EXCEPTIONS TO CLAUDE.md §12's "money is integer cents". §12
     describes src/commissions/money.mjs, and that module converts INTO cents
     at its own door: src/commissions/calculate.mjs:59 calls
     toCents(round.funded_amount), which multiplies by 100 — proof the column
     holds dollars. Cents never leave src/commissions/.

     ONE RULE, BOTH SCREENS. public/app/pipeline.html moneyText() applies
     exactly this rule and returns null where this returns the dash.
     src/http/client-panel-screen.test.mjs fails if the two ever format the
     same value differently again.

     Unknown — null, undefined, a blank, a word, a wrong type — is a dash.
     Never 0 for unknown: a zero would be a claim that the amount is nothing,
     and unknown is not nothing. A RECORDED zero is a fact and prints as $0. */
  function money(v) {
    try {
      if (v === null || v === undefined) return UNKNOWN;
      var dollars;
      if (typeof v === "number") {
        if (!isFinite(v)) return UNKNOWN;
        dollars = v;
      } else if (typeof v === "string") {
        var t = v.trim();
        if (!/^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$/.test(t)) return UNKNOWN;
        dollars = Number(t);
        if (!isFinite(dollars)) return UNKNOWN;
      } else {
        return UNKNOWN;
      }
      return "$" + Math.round(dollars).toLocaleString("en-US");
    } catch (e) {
      return UNKNOWN;
    }
  }

  /* ── THE TILES THAT WERE ALREADY HERE KEEP THE RULE THEY ALREADY HAD ──────
     Prequal, Total Approved and the two income-per-year lines are not part of
     this work. They shipped with the rule below and they keep it, byte for
     byte, so nothing on the screen moved that nobody asked to move:

       a recorded zero  → a dash (money() above prints "$0")
       a negative       → a dash (money() above printed "$-500", plainly wrong)

     Whether a recorded zero on those tiles ought to read "$0" or a dash is a
     real question and it is Chris's to answer, not this change's. Until he
     does, they read exactly as they read on main.

     money() above stays the single shared rule for the two NEW money values —
     this page's funding-round approved amount and pipeline.html's — and
     src/http/client-panel-screen.test.mjs pins both rules. */
  function tileMoney(n) {
    if (n == null || n === "") return UNKNOWN;
    var v = Number(n);
    if (!isFinite(v) || v <= 0) return UNKNOWN;
    return "$" + Math.round(v).toLocaleString("en-US");
  }

  /* ── ONE FACT, ONE DEFINITION ────────────────────────────────────────────
     "Is this bank yes worth anything yet?" was answered in three places in
     three slightly different ways, and they already disagreed:

       src/funding/success-fee.mjs   the biller   NULL or <= 0, not excluded
       api/dashboard/pipeline.mjs    the board    NULL only, exclusion ignored
       this file                     the screen   NULL or blank, not excluded

     The two SQL callers now share one string —
     unpricedApprovalConditions() in src/funding/success-fee.mjs. A screen
     cannot import a module, so this is still a copy; what stops it drifting is
     src/http/client-panel-screen.test.mjs, which reads that string and proves
     these two functions answer the same way on the same rows.

     They live up here, out of the DOM, for the same reason everything else in
     this block does: the number they produce leads the screen, and a number
     that leads a screen has to be provable with no browser.

     NULL IS UNKNOWN AND SURVIVES (CLAUDE.md §12). Nothing here turns an unknown
     amount into 0, and nothing here treats a 0 as an amount: a zero cannot be
     invoiced, so it is still waiting. */

  /* Somebody has recorded that this approval does not count — withdrawn, or the
     client never used it (db/migrations/272_approval_excluded.sql). A decision
     with a name and a time on it, not a dismissed warning. */
  function isExcluded(app) {
    return !!(app && app.approval_excluded_at);
  }

  /* A bank yes that cannot be billed yet: approved, not excluded, and no usable
     dollar amount. Unknown, blank, unreadable and non-positive all count as
     waiting — every one of them is a row the client would never be invoiced
     for, and guardFundedAmount refuses the Funded move on the same set. */
  function isWaitingOnAmount(app) {
    if (!app || String(app.status || "") !== "Approved") return false;
    if (isExcluded(app)) return false;
    var a = app.approved_amount;
    if (a === null || a === undefined || String(a).trim() === "") return true;
    var n = Number(String(a).trim());
    if (!isFinite(n)) return true;
    return n <= 0;
  }

  /* The mirror: a bank yes we HAVE confirmed a number for. This is the set the
     success fee is a percent of (owner-set 2026-08-30,
     docs/finance/CLOSEOUT-FEE-BASIS.md), so it is the only honest thing to put under a
     label that says "Approved". */
  function isConfirmedApproval(app) {
    if (!app || String(app.status || "") !== "Approved") return false;
    if (isExcluded(app)) return false;
    return approvalCents(app.approved_amount) > 0;
  }

  /* Dollars as the numeric(14,2) column holds them -> integer cents, or 0 for
     anything unreadable. Cents, not floats: 450.10 * 100 is
     45009.999999999996 in JavaScript, which is how a $450.10 approval becomes
     $450.09 in a total. The two halves of the string are read as whole numbers
     instead, exactly as public/app/money-input.js does — written out here
     rather than imported because this block is deliberately dependency-free so
     a test can run it with no browser and no other file. */
  function approvalCents(v) {
    if (v === null || v === undefined) return 0;
    var m = /^(\d+)(?:\.(\d{1,2}))?$/.exec(String(v).trim());
    if (!m) return 0;
    var frac = m[2] === undefined ? "00" : (m[2].length === 1 ? m[2] + "0" : m[2]);
    var cents = Number(m[1]) * 100 + Number(frac);
    return isFinite(cents) ? cents : 0;
  }

  /**
   * What this client's applications add up to.
   *
   * NEWEST ROW PER LENDER WINS, and rows with no lender at all are each counted
   * on their own. listClientApplications orders by updated_at DESC, so the
   * first row seen for a lender is the current one; an imported approval that
   * carries only a bank name has no lender id and no row on screen to chip, and
   * an approval nobody can see is exactly the one that rots. This is the rule
   * the screen already applied when it painted the rows — it is written down
   * here so the headline count and the row chips can never disagree.
   *
   * Returns { waiting, confirmed, confirmed_dollars }. confirmed_dollars is a
   * fixed 2dp string, or null when nothing is confirmed — never "0.00", because
   * "we have confirmed nothing" and "we have confirmed nothing at all" are the
   * same sentence and neither of them is a dollar total.
   */
  function summariseApprovals(rows) {
    var out = { waiting: 0, confirmed: 0, confirmed_dollars: null };
    var list = [];
    try { if (Array.isArray(rows)) list = rows; } catch (e) { list = []; }
    var seen = {};
    var cents = 0;
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var app = list[i];
      if (!app || typeof app !== "object") continue;
      try {
        if (app.lender_id) {
          if (seen[app.lender_id]) continue;
          seen[app.lender_id] = true;
        }
        if (isWaitingOnAmount(app)) out.waiting += 1;
        if (isConfirmedApproval(app)) {
          out.confirmed += 1;
          cents += approvalCents(app.approved_amount);
        }
      } catch (e) { /* one unreadable row must not lose the rest of the count */ }
    }
    if (out.confirmed > 0) {
      out.confirmed_dollars = String(Math.floor(cents / 100)) + "." +
        (cents % 100 < 10 ? "0" : "") + String(cents % 100);
    }
    return out;
  }

  /* ── NEXT ACTION: COMPLIANCE GATE A LIVES ON THIS LINE ───────────────────
     The big line may ONLY ever show a step the system worked out. It may
     never show custom_fields.employee_next_action.

     WHY. That stored string is written by workflows that never look at
     consent — src/workflows/s-06-post-call-funding-purchased.mjs:42 and
     src/workflows/c-05-pre-funding-review.mjs:44 both write the literal
     "Pull CRS". src/fulfillment/next-action.mjs refuses "Pull CRS" unless
     consent is KNOWN VALID (guardConsentBeforePull), and turns a refusal into
     degraded:true with next_action:null. Painting the stored string when the
     answer came back degraded therefore puts "Pull CRS" on screen for exactly
     the client whose consent could NOT be established. Degraded is the worst
     possible moment to trust stale text, not the moment to fall back to it.

     THE STORED VALUE IS NOT THROWN AWAY. It comes back as `saved`, for a
     quiet labelled line underneath, so staff keep the information and simply
     stop being told to act on it. It is returned only when it exists and
     differs from the worked-out line.

     THREE ANSWERS, ALL THREE IN WORDS. The big slot is never blank and never
     a bare dash. A bare dash beside a "Saved on the record: Pull CRS" line
     reads as though the dash were hiding the real instruction, which is the
     one impression this slot must never give.

     Returns { main, saved }. Never throws.
       main  — the worked-out step;
               or NONE_APPLIES when the answer WAS worked out and no step on
               the list applies to this file;
               or NOT_WORKED_OUT when nothing was worked out at all.
       saved — "" or the labelled saved line. */
  var NOT_WORKED_OUT = "Not worked out yet.";
  var NONE_APPLIES = "No step applies right now.";
  var SAVED_PREFIX = "Saved on the record: ";

  function nextAction(fx, cf) {
    var stored = "";
    var label = "";
    var workedOut = false;
    try {
      if (cf && cf.employee_next_action != null) stored = String(cf.employee_next_action).trim();
    } catch (e) { stored = ""; }
    try {
      // deriveNextAction() never returns a label alongside degraded:true, so a
      // label here is always an answer the gates already cleared.
      workedOut = !!(fx && fx.degraded !== true);
      if (workedOut && fx.next_action && fx.next_action.label != null) {
        label = String(fx.next_action.label).trim();
      }
    } catch (e) { label = ""; workedOut = false; }

    var main = label ? label : (workedOut ? NONE_APPLIES : NOT_WORKED_OUT);
    var saved = (stored && stored !== main) ? (SAVED_PREFIX + stored) : "";
    try {
      if (saved && fx && fx.scores_on_file === true && /^pull crs$/i.test(stored)) saved = "";
    } catch (e) { /* keep the labelled saved line */ }
    return { main: main, saved: saved };
  }

  function displayStatus(raw, fx) {
    var s = "";
    try { s = raw == null ? "" : String(raw).trim(); } catch (e) { s = ""; }
    var key = "";
    try { key = fx && fx.next_action && fx.next_action.key ? String(fx.next_action.key) : ""; } catch (e) { key = ""; }
    if (s === "New Lead" && key === "apply_for_funding") return "Apply Now";
    return s;
  }

  function displayHold(raw, fx) {
    var h = "";
    try { h = raw == null ? "" : String(raw).trim(); } catch (e) { h = ""; }
    try {
      if (h === "Awaiting CRS" && fx && fx.scores_on_file === true) return "";
    } catch (e) { /* keep */ }
    return h;
  }

  /* ── A SAMPLE REPORT SAYS IT IS A SAMPLE (live hole 23, 2026-09-18) ──────
     A walkthrough can load a SAMPLE credit report onto a file that nobody has
     pulled (scripts/sim/push-credit.mjs, src/demo/simulate-client.mjs). It is
     stamped environment "simulated" — and push-credit also sets
     simulated:true — on purpose, so the scores still paint and everything
     after a pull still runs. Those scripts say the stamp is there "so every
     screen can tell it was never a bureau pull". This screen did not tell.

     #13 Sim Thirteen-NoBook showed "EX 771 · EQ 778 · TU 766" and a Last
     Credit Pull date right beside "No written permission on file — we cannot
     pull their credit yet". The live rows had no permission and no pull, so
     the permission line was TRUE. The lie was the scores: sample data shown as
     real (UI-STANDARDS §6).

     One question: did the tri-merge scores come from a sample report? The
     report is found by tri_merge.asOf, which the server sets to that row's
     created_at (triMerge in src/http/client-detail.mjs). Anything unreadable
     answers false, which is how the screen read before this: it only ever ADDS
     a warning, it never hides a score. Never throws. */
  var SAMPLE_NOTE = "Sample scores. Not a real credit pull.";
  /* The same stamp covers every other figure this screen reads off that
     report — the inquiries list and count, Card Use and the income estimates
     (live hole N12, 2026-09-18). Each one is matched to its own report by the
     date the server or fileInquiries() says it came from. Prequal and Tier,
     which the decision on that report set, are matched by sampleDecision(). */
  var SAMPLE_FIGURE_NOTE = "From a sample report. Not a real credit pull.";

  function isSampleReport(crsResults, asOf) {
    try {
      if (!asOf) return false;
      var at = new Date(asOf).getTime();
      if (!isFinite(at)) return false;
      var list = Array.isArray(crsResults) ? crsResults : [];
      for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
        var row = list[i];
        if (!row || typeof row !== "object") continue;
        if (new Date(row.created_at).getTime() !== at) continue;
        var r = row.result;
        if (typeof r === "string") {
          try { r = JSON.parse(r); } catch (e) { r = null; }
        }
        if (!r || typeof r !== "object") continue;
        if (r.simulated === true) return true;
        if (String(r.environment || "").toLowerCase() === "simulated") return true;
      }
    } catch (e) { /* unreadable is not a sample */ }
    return false;
  }

  /* Prequal and Tier are not read off a report. decision.rendered stamps them
     on the client (onDecisionRendered in src/handlers/client-lifecycle.mjs)
     from the report that was just worked out, so they belong to the NEWEST
     stored report. Both sample loaders also keep that decision on the sample
     row itself: the pre-approval total as result.preapprovals.totalCombined
     and the tier as the row's outcome_tier. So a Prequal or a Tier is the
     sample's when the newest stored report is a sample AND carries that same
     figure (live hole N12). Returns { prequal, tier } — either may be null —
     for a sample, and null for a real pull, no report, or anything
     unreadable. Like isSampleReport() it only ever ADDS a warning. Never
     throws. */
  function sampleDecision(crsResults) {
    try {
      var list = (Array.isArray(crsResults) ? crsResults : []).filter(function (r) {
        return r && typeof r === "object";
      });
      if (!list.length) return null;
      list.sort(function (a, b) {
        return new Date(b.created_at || 0) - new Date(a.created_at || 0);
      });
      var row = list[0];
      if (!isSampleReport([row], row.created_at)) return null;
      var r = row.result;
      if (typeof r === "string") {
        try { r = JSON.parse(r); } catch (e) { r = null; }
      }
      var pre = r && r.preapprovals && typeof r.preapprovals === "object"
        ? r.preapprovals.totalCombined : null;
      var preNum = pre === null || pre === undefined || pre === "" ? NaN : Number(pre);
      return {
        prequal: isFinite(preNum) ? preNum : null,
        tier: row.outcome_tier ? String(row.outcome_tier) : null
      };
    } catch (e) { return null; }
  }

  window.FHClientPanel = {
    UNKNOWN: UNKNOWN,
    NOT_WORKED_OUT: NOT_WORKED_OUT,
    NONE_APPLIES: NONE_APPLIES,
    SAVED_PREFIX: SAVED_PREFIX,
    money: money,
    tileMoney: tileMoney,
    isExcluded: isExcluded,
    isWaitingOnAmount: isWaitingOnAmount,
    isConfirmedApproval: isConfirmedApproval,
    summariseApprovals: summariseApprovals,
    nextAction: nextAction,
    displayStatus: displayStatus,
    displayHold: displayHold,
    SAMPLE_NOTE: SAMPLE_NOTE,
    SAMPLE_FIGURE_NOTE: SAMPLE_FIGURE_NOTE,
    isSampleReport: isSampleReport,
    sampleDecision: sampleDecision
  };
})();
/* FH-CCP-END */

// data.js carries `defer` (see its tag above), so FHData does not exist yet
// while this script is being parsed — reading the client id from it here threw,
// and the throw killed the rest of this block before the client file was ever
// requested, leaving every tile on "loading…". Every deferred script runs
// before DOMContentLoaded, so this whole block waits for that event.
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  "use strict";

  function $(id) { return document.getElementById(id); }
  function dash(v) {
    if (v == null || v === "") return "—";
    var s = String(v).trim();
    return s ? s : "—";
  }
  function setText(id, v) {
    var node = $(id);
    if (node) node.textContent = dash(v);
  }
  // The money rule and the next-action rule both live in the FH-CCP block at
  // the top of this script, so a test can run them with no browser.
  var FHCP = window.FHClientPanel;
  // `money` is the rule the tiles on this page already had — unchanged from
  // main. `roundMoney` is the shared whole-dollars rule, and the ONLY thing it
  // paints is the new funding-round amount. See FH-CCP-BEGIN for both.
  var money = FHCP.tileMoney;
  var roundMoney = FHCP.money;
  function moneyYr(row) {
    if (!row || row.annual == null) return "—";
    var m = money(row.annual);
    return m === "—" ? "—" : m + "/yr";
  }
  function when(iso) {
    if (!iso) return "—";
    var d = new Date(iso);
    if (isNaN(d.getTime())) return "—";
    return d.toLocaleString("en-US", {
      month: "short", day: "numeric", year: "numeric",
      hour: "numeric", minute: "2-digit",
      timeZone: "America/Phoenix", timeZoneName: "short"
    });
  }
  /* A date, and how long ago it was, in one line: "Jun 12, 2026 · 79 days".
     Never invents a date. No timestamp is a dash, and an unreadable one is a
     dash too — "today" would be the worst possible guess here, because the
     whole point of the line is to show that something has been sitting. */
  function ageOf(iso) {
    if (!iso) return "—";
    var d = new Date(iso);
    if (isNaN(d.getTime())) return "—";
    var on = d.toLocaleDateString("en-US", {
      month: "short", day: "numeric", year: "numeric", timeZone: "America/Phoenix"
    });
    var days = Math.floor((Date.now() - d.getTime()) / 86400000);
    if (!isFinite(days) || days < 0) return on;
    if (days === 0) return on + " · today";
    return on + " · " + days + (days === 1 ? " day" : " days");
  }

  function scoreLine(tm) {
    tm = tm || {};
    function one(k, v) { return k + " " + (v == null || v === "" ? "—" : String(v)); }
    return one("EX", tm.experian) + " · " + one("EQ", tm.equifax) + " · " + one("TU", tm.transunion);
  }

  /* cardUse — how much of this client's revolving credit is in use.
   *
   * NOT MEASURED IS NOT ZERO, and this is the whole reason the function exists
   * rather than a setText() call. The endpoint returns { percent, band, asOf }
   * (src/http/client-detail.mjs:112-122) and `percent` is null whenever no
   * stored report carried a utilisation figure. A real bureau pull does not
   * write one today, so null is the ordinary answer for a live file — and "0%"
   * would tell a closer this person's cards are clear when in fact nobody has
   * looked. Only null reads "not measured"; a genuine 0 still reads "0%".
   */
  function cardUse(u) {
    var pct = u && u.percent;
    if (pct == null || pct === "") return "not measured";
    var n = Number(pct);
    if (!isFinite(n)) return "not measured";
    return Math.round(n) + "%" + (u.band ? " · " + u.band : "");
  }

  /* ── THE INQUIRIES ON THE CREDIT FILE ─────────────────────────────────────
   *
   * OWNER-SET 2026-09-06, TODO §8. The tile above used to print
   * inquiry_removal_cases.open_inquiry_count. That column counts rows in
   * inquiry_log, and inquiry_log is only written once the removal desk stages a
   * case, so on a file nobody has worked it is empty and the tile read 0 or 1
   * while the credit report itself listed four — Capital One, SYNCB/PayPal,
   * Navy Federal and Citibank on Walk1 Funding. Two screens, one word, two
   * numbers, and neither said which it meant.
   *
   * THE NAMES ARE ALREADY ON THIS PAGE. GET /api/dashboard/client returns
   * crs_results with the whole stored report in `result`, so no new read is
   * needed — this walks it.
   *
   * THE FIELD NAMES ARE COPIED, NOT INVENTED. They are exactly the ones
   * src/inquiry-ops/extract-disputables.mjs reads (collectInquiries), so this
   * screen and the removal desk cannot disagree about what an inquiry is.
   * THAT DUPLICATION IS A DEBT, and it is written down rather than hidden: the
   * right home for this is one field on the client endpoint, and when that
   * lands this function should be deleted rather than kept beside it.
   *
   * SANDBOX PULLS ARE SKIPPED, the same rule triMerge() and incomeEstimates()
   * already apply — a vendor test fixture is not this person's credit file.
   *
   * NEVER A ZERO STANDING IN FOR UNKNOWN. Three answers:
   *   { known:false }                 no usable stored report — say so
   *   { known:true, rows:[] }         a report with no inquiry list on it
   *   { known:true, rows:[{name,bureau}] }
   * `asOf` is the created_at of the report the rows came off, so the paint
   * can ask FHCP.isSampleReport() about THAT report (live hole N12).
   */
  function fileInquiries(crsResults) {
    var out = { known: false, rows: [], asOf: null };
    var list = Array.isArray(crsResults) ? crsResults.slice() : [];
    list.sort(function (a, b) {
      return new Date((b && b.created_at) || 0) - new Date((a && a.created_at) || 0);
    });
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var row = list[i] || {};
      var result = row.result;
      if (typeof result === "string") {
        try { result = JSON.parse(result); } catch (e) { result = null; }
      }
      if (!result || typeof result !== "object") continue;
      var env = "";
      try { env = String(result.environment || "").toLowerCase(); } catch (e) { env = ""; }
      if (env === "sandbox") continue;

      out.known = true;
      out.asOf = row.created_at || null;
      var seen = {};
      var rows = [];
      function take(items) {
        for (var j = 0; j < (Array.isArray(items) ? items.length : 0); j++) {
          var inq = items[j];
          if (!inq || typeof inq !== "object") continue;
          var name = inq.creditorName || inq.inquiry || inq.inquiry_name || inq.name || inq.furnisher;
          name = String(name == null ? "" : name).trim();
          if (!name) continue;
          var bureau = inq.source || inq.bureau || inq.bureauCode;
          bureau = String(bureau == null ? "" : bureau).trim().toUpperCase();
          var key = name.toLowerCase() + "|" + bureau;
          if (seen[key]) continue;
          seen[key] = true;
          rows.push({ name: name, bureau: bureau });
        }
      }
      var normalized = (result.normalized && typeof result.normalized === "object") ? result.normalized : result;
      take(normalized.inquiries);
      take(result.inquiries);
      take(result.newInquiries);
      var blocks = (result.bureaus && typeof result.bureaus === "object") ? result.bureaus
        : (normalized.bureaus && typeof normalized.bureaus === "object") ? normalized.bureaus : {};
      for (var code in blocks) {
        if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(blocks, code)) continue;
        var block = blocks[code];
        if (!block || typeof block !== "object") continue;
        var items2 = Array.isArray(block.inquiries) ? block.inquiries.slice() : [];
        for (var k = 0; k < items2.length; k++) {
          if (items2[k] && typeof items2[k] === "object" && !items2[k].bureau && !items2[k].source) {
            items2[k] = { creditorName: items2[k].creditorName || items2[k].name
              || items2[k].inquiry_name || items2[k].furnisher, bureau: code };
          }
        }
        take(items2);
      }
      out.rows = rows;
      return out;
    }
    return out;
  }

  /* One line naming the banks that pulled this person's credit, so nobody has
     to open a second screen to find out which four they are. Full names — a
     bureau writes "AMERICAN EXPRESS", never "Amex" (owner rule). */
  /* THE SAME ROWS, PAINTED UNDER THE NEXT STEP.
     Record Facts keeps its one-line footnote; this puts the list itself where
     the instruction to act on it is. Built as DOM nodes with textContent, never
     an HTML string — a creditor name comes off a credit report and is not ours
     to trust. */
  function paintNextInquiries(rows, sample) {
    var box = $("ccp-next-inquiries");
    if (!box) return;
    box.textContent = "";
    if (!rows || !rows.length) { box.hidden = true; return; }
    var head = document.createElement("div");
    head.className = "na-inq-head";
    head.textContent = rows.length === 1
      ? "The 1 inquiry on this file"
      : "The " + rows.length + " inquiries on this file";
    box.appendChild(head);
    /* Straight under the head, before the names: a list off a sample report
       says so first (live hole N12). */
    if (sample) {
      var note = document.createElement("p");
      note.className = "fact-note na-inq-sample";
      note.textContent = FHCP.SAMPLE_FIGURE_NOTE;
      box.appendChild(note);
    }
    rows.forEach(function (r) {
      var row = document.createElement("div");
      row.className = "na-inq-row";
      var name = document.createElement("span");
      name.className = "na-inq-name";
      name.textContent = r.name;
      row.appendChild(name);
      if (r.bureau) {
        var b = document.createElement("span");
        b.className = "na-inq-bureau";
        b.textContent = r.bureau;
        row.appendChild(b);
      }
      /* No status word here. This list comes off the stored credit report,
         which knows who pulled the file and nothing about whether a removal
         has been sent — inquiry_log holds that and this endpoint does not
         return it. Printing "Pending Removal" from this source would be a
         claim the source cannot support. */
      box.appendChild(row);
    });
    box.hidden = false;
  }

  function paintInquiries(crsResults) {
    var found = fileInquiries(crsResults);
    var names = $("ccp-inquiry-names");
    /* The count and the list came off one report. When that report is a
       walkthrough's sample, both say so — live hole N12. */
    var sample = found.known && FHCP.isSampleReport(crsResults, found.asOf);
    var tileNote = $("ccp-inquiries-sample");
    if (tileNote) {
      tileNote.textContent = sample ? FHCP.SAMPLE_FIGURE_NOTE : "";
      tileNote.hidden = !sample;
    }
    if (!found.known) {
      setText("ccp-inquiries", "no report yet");
      if (names) { names.textContent = ""; names.hidden = true; }
      paintNextInquiries([]);
      return;
    }
    if (!found.rows.length) {
      setText("ccp-inquiries", "none listed");
      if (names) {
        names.textContent = "The stored credit report does not list any inquiries. "
          + "That is not the same as none — pull a bureau again if this file should have them.";
        names.hidden = false;
      }
      paintNextInquiries([]);
      return;
    }
    setText("ccp-inquiries", String(found.rows.length));
    /* The run-on line under Client Facts is gone. It printed
       "Who pulled this credit: CAPITAL ONE (EX) · SYNCB/PAYPAL CREDIT (EX) ·
       NAVY FEDERAL CU (TU) · CITIBANK NA (EQ)" as one wrapping sentence —
