document.getElementById('genBtn').addEventListener('click', function () {
  var msg = document.getElementById('genMsg');
  if (!canWriteCreative()) {
    msg.textContent = CF_SUITE.error
      || (CF_SUITE.loaded && !CF_SUITE.enabled
        ? 'The owner has not turned this on for this partner. It turns on in Brand Studio, owner-only.'
        : 'Need a partner first.');
    return;
  }
  var partnerId = null;
  try {
    if (typeof PARTNERS !== 'undefined' && typeof S !== 'undefined' && PARTNERS[S.partner]) {
      partnerId = PARTNERS[S.partner].id;
    }
  } catch (e) {}
  if (!partnerId && window.FHData && FHData.param) partnerId = FHData.param('partner_id');
  if (!partnerId) {
    try { partnerId = new URL(location.href).searchParams.get('partner_id'); } catch (e) {}
  }
  var kind = document.getElementById('genKind').value;
  var offer = document.getElementById('genOffer').value;
  var prompt = document.getElementById('genPrompt').value.trim();
  var idem = document.getElementById('genIdem').value.trim();
  if (!partnerId) { msg.textContent = 'Need a partner first.'; return; }
  if (!idem) { msg.textContent = 'Give this batch a name first.'; return; }
  /* Stopped here, the same way a missing batch name is. Sending it without an
     offer type is not a smaller failure — the job runs, makes the creative, and
     then the compliance check blocks every piece of it and shows the engine's
     own words. Better to ask one question now. */
  if (!offer) { msg.textContent = 'Say what is being sold first.'; return; }
  /* scriptId is OPTIONAL and is only put in the spec when one was picked. An
     empty string here would fail the uuid shape check on the endpoint
     (api/creative/generate.mjs:132) and refuse the whole job, so "none" must
     send nothing at all rather than "". */
  var scriptId = document.getElementById('genScript').value;
  /* offerType rides inside spec, not beside it. The endpoint hands body.spec
     straight to enqueue(), which stores it on the job, and the compliance
     check reads spec.offerType off that stored job — so a copy of it at the
     top level of this body would be dropped and never seen. */
  var genSpec = { prompt: prompt, formats: ['1x1'], variants: 1, assetKind: kind, offerType: offer };
  if (scriptId) genSpec.scriptId = scriptId;
  msg.textContent = 'Enqueueing…';
  var t = '';
  try { t = localStorage.getItem('fh_token') || ''; } catch (e) { t = ''; }
  fetch('/api/creative/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      accept: 'application/json',
      'content-type': 'application/json',
      ...(t && t !== 'demo' ? { authorization: 'Bearer ' + t } : {})
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      partner_id: partnerId,
      asset_kind: kind,
      idempotency_key: idem,
      prompt: prompt,
      spec: genSpec
    })
  }).then(function (r) { return r.json().catch(function () { return { ok: false }; }); })
    .then(function (res) {
      if (!res.ok) {
        msg.textContent = 'Could not add it. ' + plainCreative(res);
        return;
      }
      /* The server says whether an ad-making service is actually switched on, and
         that sentence is shown as it is. The old message promised the queue would
         "start on its own in a few minutes" whatever the state of the account —
         true of the clock, false of the outcome, because with no service switched
         on the run can only record a failure. */
      msg.textContent = res.created
        ? (res.note || 'Saved to the queue.')
        : 'That batch name was already used, so nothing new was added.';
      if (typeof wireCreative === 'function') wireCreative();
    });
});

function cfPartnerId() {
  var partnerId = null;
  try {
    if (typeof PARTNERS !== 'undefined' && typeof S !== 'undefined' && PARTNERS[S.partner]) {
      partnerId = PARTNERS[S.partner].id;
    }
  } catch (e) {}
  if (!partnerId && window.FHData && FHData.param) partnerId = FHData.param('partner_id');
  if (!partnerId) {
    try { partnerId = new URL(location.href).searchParams.get('partner_id'); } catch (e) {}
  }
  return partnerId;
}
function cfAuthHeaders() {
  var t = '';
  try { t = localStorage.getItem('fh_token') || ''; } catch (e) { t = ''; }
  var h = { accept: 'application/json', 'content-type': 'application/json' };
  if (t && t !== 'demo') h.authorization = 'Bearer ' + t;
  return h;
}
/* ══ WRITE A SCRIPT AND LABEL IT ═════════════════════════════════════════
   POST /api/scripts/write — the only way a row reaches ad_scripts, and until
   this form existed nothing under public/ called it. Every label on every ad
   starts here: script -> creative -> ad.

   WHAT THIS SENDS AND WHAT IT LEAVES OUT. Only `body` is required. A label the
   person left blank is OMITTED from the request rather than sent as "", because
   the endpoint normalises whatever it is given and an empty string is not a
   label — leaving the key out is how "we do not know" stays unknown.

   THE LABELS ARE NOT CHECKED HERE. That is deliberate and it is an owner rule
   (CLAUDE.md §3c, 2026-09-06): naming must never be a blocker. A brand-new angle
   nobody has written down saves the first time it is typed. The datalists are
   suggestions only and never restrict what may be typed — an <input list=…> in
   HTML accepts any value, unlike a <select>.

   WHERE THE SUGGESTIONS COME FROM. Nothing reads the label dictionary back —
   there is no endpoint for it — so they are seeded from what this screen has
   already saved, using the `dictionary` array the endpoint returns. No
   vocabulary is invented here; an empty list means nothing has been saved yet.
   ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */

/* The employee roles the endpoint accepts — ROLE_SETS.STAFF in
   src/http/read-api.mjs:173, verbatim. An UNKNOWN role still sees the card: the
   cache is a hint, not the session, and hiding a control from a real employee
   because the cache was cold is the worse mistake. The server is the gate. */
var SW_STAFF_ROLES = ['owner','admin','funding_advisor','closer','inquiry_specialist','setter','sales_manager','csm'];
(function swRoleGate(){
  var vrole = '';
  try { vrole = String(localStorage.getItem('fh_role') || '').trim().toLowerCase(); } catch(e){}
  var card = document.getElementById('secScriptWrite');
  if(!card) return;
  card.style.display = (vrole && SW_STAFF_ROLES.indexOf(vrole) === -1) ? 'none' : '';
})();

/* One suggestion added to one datalist, never twice, never blank. */
function swSuggest(listId, value){
  if(!value) return;
  var dl = document.getElementById(listId);
  if(!dl) return;
  for(var i = 0; i < dl.children.length; i++){
    if(dl.children[i].value === value) return;
  }
  var o = document.createElement('option');
  o.value = value;
  dl.appendChild(o);
}
var SW_LIST_FOR = { script_type:'swTypeList', angle:'swAngleList', hook:'swHookList', offer:'swOfferList' };

/* WHAT A REFUSAL SAYS. The sign-in and wrong-method answers carry no message and
   go through this screen's own plain-words helper. The rest of this endpoint's
   refusals are written for a person AND name the exact text that was typed —
   "angle_key came out as 3_second_hook after tidying" is worth more than any
   sentence this screen could invent — so those are shown exactly as they came
   back rather than reworded into something vaguer. */
function swSay(res){
  switch(String((res && res.error) || '')){
    case 'unauthorized': case 'forbidden': case 'auth_unavailable':
    case 'method_not_allowed': case 'offline':
      return plainCreative(res);
    case 'body_required':
      return 'Type or paste the words of the ad first.';
  }
  /* The endpoint's own sentence, with only its first letter raised so it does not
     read as a fragment after "Nothing was saved." NEVER when it opens with a
     field name: angle_key is a real column and Angle_key is not, so a sentence
     whose first word carries an underscore is left exactly as it came back. */
  if(res && typeof res.message === 'string' && res.message){
    var firstWord = res.message.split(' ')[0];
    return firstWord.indexOf('_') === -1
      ? res.message.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + res.message.slice(1)
      : res.message;
  }
  return plainCreative(res);
}

document.getElementById('swSaveBtn').addEventListener('click', function () {
  var btn = this;
  var msg = document.getElementById('swMsg');
  var text = document.getElementById('swBody').value;
  if(!text.trim()){ msg.textContent = 'Type or paste the words of the ad first.'; return; }

  var payload = { body: text };
  var title = document.getElementById('swTitle').value.trim();
  if(title) payload.title = title;
  [['swType','script_type'],['swAngle','angle_key'],['swHook','hook_key'],['swOffer','offer_key']]
    .forEach(function(pair){
      var v = document.getElementById(pair[0]).value.trim();
      if(v) payload[pair[1]] = v;
    });
  var lane = document.getElementById('swLane').value;
  if(lane) payload.lane = lane;
  /* The partner this screen is scoped to. Left out when there is none, and then
     the endpoint files the script under the house partner rather than failing. */
  var pid = cfPartnerId();
  if(pid) payload.partner_id = pid;

  var prev = btn.textContent;
  btn.disabled = true;
  btn.textContent = 'Saving…';
  msg.textContent = 'Saving…';
  fetch('/api/scripts/write', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: cfAuthHeaders(),
    body: JSON.stringify(payload)
  }).then(function (r) { return r.json().catch(function () { return { ok:false, error:'offline' }; }); })
    .catch(function () { return { ok:false, error:'offline' }; })
    .then(function (res) {
      btn.disabled = false;
      btn.textContent = prev;
      if(!res || !res.ok){
        msg.textContent = 'Nothing was saved. ' + swSay(res);
        return;
      }
      var s = res.script || {};
      /* THE TIDIED LABELS, NOT THE TYPED ONES. The endpoint lower-cases and
         joins words with underscores, so "Denial Angle" is stored as
         denial_angle. Showing what it BECAME is the only way the tidying is
         visible instead of a silent rename. */
      var stored = res.labels || {};
      var shown = ['script_type','lane','angle_key','hook_key','offer_key']
        .map(function(k){ return stored[k]; })
        .filter(function(v){ return !!v; });
      msg.textContent = 'Saved as version ' + (s.version == null ? '1' : s.version) +
        (shown.length ? ' · labelled ' + shown.join(', ') : ' · no labels on it') +
        '. It is now in the Script list below.';

      /* The dictionary the endpoint says it learned, fed back as suggestions. */
      (res.dictionary || []).forEach(function(d){
        if(d && SW_LIST_FOR[d.kind]) swSuggest(SW_LIST_FOR[d.kind], d.key);
      });

      /* Into the Generate form's Script list, and picked, so the very next thing
         made is tied to it. This is the middle link of the chain. */
      if(s.id){
        var sel = document.getElementById('genScript');
        /* scriptLabel() is the one formula renderScriptPicker() uses too, called
           rather than copied: two spellings of one label would make the script
           read differently before and after a reload, which looks like two
           scripts where there is one. */
        var label = scriptLabel(s.title, s.body, s.version);
        /* Into the list the picker is built from, not only into the picker, so a
           later render rebuilds this option instead of dropping it. Filed under
           the partner that was just saved to, so a partner switch replaces it
           wholesale rather than leaving it behind. */
        SCRIPTS.unshift({ id: s.id, title: s.title, body_preview: s.body, version: s.version });
        var o = document.createElement('option');
        o.value = s.id;
        o.textContent = label;
        sel.appendChild(o);
        sel.value = s.id;
      }
      document.getElementById('swBody').value = '';
    });
});

document.getElementById('runJobsBtn').addEventListener('click', function () {
  var msg = document.getElementById('genMsg');
  var partnerId = cfPartnerId();
  if (!partnerId) { msg.textContent = 'Need a partner first.'; return; }
  msg.textContent = 'Running queued jobs…';
  fetch('/api/creative/run', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: cfAuthHeaders(),
    body: JSON.stringify({ partner_id: partnerId, max_jobs: 3 })
  }).then(function (r) { return r.json().catch(function () { return { ok: false }; }); })
    .then(function (res) {
      if (!res.ok) { msg.textContent = 'Could not run it. ' + plainCreative(res); return; }
      /* "Ran 1 job." was the whole message even when that job failed and made
         nothing, which reads as success. Say how many worked and how many did
         not, then the server's plain-words reason. */
      var ran = res.ran || 0;
      var okCount = res.succeeded == null ? null : res.succeeded;
      var head = ran === 0
        ? 'Nothing ran.'
        : (okCount == null
          ? 'Tried ' + ran + (ran === 1 ? ' job.' : ' jobs.')
          : 'Tried ' + ran + (ran === 1 ? ' job: ' : ' jobs: ') + okCount + ' worked, ' + (ran - okCount) + ' did not.');
      msg.textContent = head + (res.note ? ' ' + res.note : '');
      if (typeof wireCreative === 'function') wireCreative();
    });
});

    var partnerId = cfPartnerId();
    var assetId = (document.getElementById('actAsset').value || '').trim();
    if (!partnerId) { msg.textContent = 'Need a partner first.'; return; }
    if (!assetId) { msg.textContent = 'Choose a creative first.'; return; }
    var action = btn.getAttribute('data-cact');
    var label = document.getElementById('actAsset');
    label = label.options[label.selectedIndex] ? label.options[label.selectedIndex].text : '';
    if (!window.confirm(ACTION_CONFIRM[action] + '\n\n' + label)) { msg.textContent = ''; return; }
    msg.textContent = action + '…';
    fetch('/api/creative/actions', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: cfAuthHeaders(),
      body: JSON.stringify({ partner_id: partnerId, asset_id: assetId, action: action })
    }).then(function (r) { return r.json().catch(function () { return { ok: false }; }); })
      .then(function (res) {
        if (!res.ok) { msg.textContent = 'Could not ' + action + ' it. ' + plainCreative(res); return; }
        var st = (res.asset && res.asset.compliance_state) || '';
        msg.textContent = 'Done. This creative is now ' + st +
          (res.asset && res.asset.archived_at ? ' and archived' : '') + '.';
        if (typeof wireCreative === 'function') wireCreative();
      });
  });
});

/* ══ BRAND: APPROVE / SEND BACK ══════════════════════════════════════════
   The two buttons apprDetail() draws on a brand row. Delegated on document
   because the detail row is built after this runs — the same idiom as the
   [data-open-asset] listener above. api/brand/review.mjs is the only writer of
   a brand's approval state; nothing here decides anything, it just asks.

   THE SERVER IS THE GATE. apprDetail() draws these only for owner/admin, but
   that is tidiness, not security: the handler refuses a partner before it reads
   a row, so a hand-made request gets the same 403 the hidden button would have.

   ONE RELOAD PATH, COPIED. wireCreative() is what the two other write buttons on
   this screen call when they are done. It re-reads all four panels, so the
   approved brand leaves the queue and the counts on the filter buttons follow. */
var BRAND_CONFIRM = {
  approve: 'Approve this brand? It will be marked approved for this partner.',
  reject: 'Send this brand back? It becomes a draft again and leaves the queue.'
};
document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
  var btn = e.target.closest ? e.target.closest('[data-brand-act]') : null;
  if (!btn) return;
  e.stopPropagation();
  var box = btn.closest('[data-brand-box]');
  var msg = box ? box.querySelector('[data-brand-msg]') : null;
  var noteEl = box ? box.querySelector('[data-brand-note]') : null;
  function say(t) { if (msg) msg.textContent = t; }

  var action = btn.getAttribute('data-brand-act');
  var partnerId = btn.getAttribute('data-brand-partner') || '';
  if (!partnerId) { say('No partner is selected, so nothing was changed.'); return; }

  /* The handler refuses a reject with no reason (400 note_required). Asking here
     first saves a round trip and says the same thing in the same words. */
  var note = noteEl ? String(noteEl.value || '').trim() : '';
  if (action === 'reject' && !note) {
    say('Type a reason first — it is kept with the brand.');
    if (noteEl) noteEl.focus();
    return;
  }
  if (!window.confirm(BRAND_CONFIRM[action])) { say(''); return; }

  var body = action === 'reject'
    ? { partner_id: partnerId, action: 'reject', note: note }
    : { partner_id: partnerId, action: 'approve' };

  btn.disabled = true;
  say(action === 'approve' ? 'Approving…' : 'Sending it back…');
  var status = 0;
  fetch('/api/brand/review', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: cfAuthHeaders(),
    body: JSON.stringify(body)
  }).then(function (r) { status = r.status; return r.json().catch(function () { return { ok: false }; }); })
    .then(function (res) {
      btn.disabled = false;
      if (res && res.ok) {
        say(action === 'approve'
          ? 'Approved. It has left the queue.'
          : 'Sent back. It is a draft again and has left the queue.');
        if (typeof wireCreative === 'function') wireCreative();
        return;
      }
      /* BRANCH ON THE STATUS, NEVER ECHO res.error. Two refusals carry no plain
         words at all — requirePrincipal answers 401 with {error:"unauthorized"}
         and 503 with {error:"auth_unavailable"} — and printing those codes at a
         person is what brand-studio.html was fixed for. Every other refusal from
         this endpoint carries a whole sentence written to be shown as it stands. */
      say(status === 401 ? 'Your sign-in has expired. Sign in again and try once more.'
        : status === 403 ? 'This sign-in is not allowed to approve a brand. Nothing was changed.'
        : status === 503 ? 'We could not reach the system just now. Nothing was changed.'
        : ((res && res.message) || 'Nothing was changed. Try again in a moment.'));
    })
    .catch(function () {
      btn.disabled = false;
      say('Nothing was changed — we could not reach the server. Try again in a moment.');
    });
});
</script>
</body>
</html>

/* Layout shells: content always clears the fixed rail.

   NO `display` DECLARATION HERE — ON PURPOSE. Do not put one back.
   shell.js:599 guards its runtime <link> injection on id="fh-crm-sidebar-css",
   but the copy each page links in its own <head> carries no id, so the guard
   never matches and this file is fetched and applied a SECOND time, after the
   page's own <style>. Six screens set `.app{display:flex}` inline
   (pipeline:57, command-center:67, closer-dashboard:51, messaging:43,
   staff-teams:24, finance-os:34). With a `display:block` here, that late second
   copy overrode them and flipped the whole layout flex -> block about 9ms after
   first paint — a measured 362px jump on staff-teams, on every load, on all six
   screens.
   Declaring no display at all makes the double load a no-op: `.app` is a div,
   so it is block by default, and a page that wants flex keeps flex both before
   and after the second copy lands. This fixes the jump from the stylesheet side
   without touching shell.js, which three other batches are editing today.

   padding-left transitions in step with the rail's own width transition
   (.18s ease, line ~46). Before this the rail slid over 182ms while the content
   snapped across in 7ms, so the rail visibly covered ~168px of content the

/* ── UI-STANDARDS §1: ONE WIDTH, ON EVERY SCREEN ──────────────────────────────
   NOW: full width, no cap (owner-set 2026-08-27). The history below is kept
   because it is what explains the SHAPE of this rule — why it lives on the
   rail, why .main is in the selector, and why every declaration is !important.
   All three reasons still hold; only the value changed. Read it before you
   touch this.

   WAS: "Max content width 1800px, centered." (owner-set 2026-08-17, --fh-maxw in
   fundhub-brand.css). It was opt-in per screen — a hand-added .fh-maxw class —
   and measured live on 2026-08-18 only 18 of 31 CRM screens had it. At a 2560px
   monitor the other 13 painted 2332px full-bleed (Calendar, Closer Dashboard,
   Company Brain, Contract templates, Finance OS, Galaxy, Lenders, Messaging,
   Ops & Admin, Specialist, partner Home), while Sales Floor and
   My Numbers hardcoded their own 1280px and 1240px and sat narrow in the middle
   of the screen. Screens that should look like one product looked like five.

   Making the cap a property of the RAIL rather than of each screen is what
   stops it drifting again: every screen that links this file gets it, and a new
   screen gets it for free.

   .main IS IN THE SELECTOR ON PURPOSE. On Staff & Teams (and Documents, and
   Campaigns) the cap sat on .content while the sticky top bar was a SIBLING
   inside an uncapped .main — so the bar ran the full width and the screen read
   full-bleed even though its content was capped. Capping .main puts the bar
   inside the same box as everything under it.

   !important IS ALSO ON PURPOSE, and it is the only thing that works from here.
   Every screen's own <style> block sits AFTER this file's <link> in <head>, so
   at equal specificity the page wins on source order — a normal declaration
   here would lose to Sales Floor's 1280px. Importance is settled before
   specificity and before order, which is why this reaches them. The cost: a
   screen that later wants true full-bleed has to say so with its own
   !important. That is the trade, stated rather than discovered.

   2026-08-27 — THE CAP IS REMOVED, AND THAT IS WHY THIS RULE STAYS.
   Deleting the rule would NOT give full width. It would hand two screens back
   their own hardcoded caps, which are the very thing the paragraph above says
   this rule exists to beat: sales-floor.html:40 `.shell{max-width:1280px;
   margin:0 auto}` and my-numbers.html:40 `.shell{max-width:1240px;margin:0
   auto}`. Both would sit narrow and centred on a 3440px monitor while every
   other screen filled it. So the rule is kept and its value inverted — from
   "cap everything at 1800" to "uncap everything" — and the !important is now
   carrying MORE weight than before, not less.

   margin-inline goes to 0, not away. Those same two screens set `margin:0
   auto`, and an auto cross-axis margin on a flex item cancels the stretch
   (the trap written up at length in fundhub-brand.css). Removing the cap
   without also pinning the margin lets them shrink-wrap to their widest child
   instead of filling the column.

   The phone rule further down (@media max-width:860px) still pins these same
   selectors to max-width:100%. That is UI-STANDARDS §11, no sideways scroll,
   and it is untouched by this — 100% is not a cap, it is the viewport. */
/* THE SESSION CHIP MUST BE ABLE TO SHRINK, AT EVERY WIDTH.
   shell.js mountChip builds the chip with its geometry as an INLINE style,
   including flex-shrink:0 and no max-width, and placeInHeader drops it into
   whatever .topbar the screen already has. Measured 558px wide. On a screen
   whose top bar is already full, a 558px unshrinkable child does not just
   overflow the bar — it pushes the whole PAGE sideways, against UI-STANDARDS
   §11 ("No sideways page scroll").
   Measured live at 1440 on 2026-08-27: campaign-manager scrolled 381px and
   social-studio 195px, and in both cases the element setting the page's
   scrollWidth was this chip, sitting in .topbar with nothing clipping it.
   These four declarations already existed for phones, inside the 860px block
   below. Nothing about the problem is specific to a phone — it is specific to
   a full top bar — so they are hoisted here and apply everywhere. The phone
   block keeps only what is genuinely phone-shaped (its margin reset).
   !important is required and not decorative: an inline style beats any
   external sheet that is not important, and the width comes from one. */
#fh-shell-chip {
  flex-wrap: wrap !important;
  max-width: 100% !important;
  min-width: 0 !important;
  flex-shrink: 1 !important;
}

/* ...and the bar it landed in must be allowed to WRAP, so the chip can drop to
   its own row instead of being squeezed to nothing.
   Letting the chip shrink (above) fixes most screens outright, but shrinking
   alone has a floor it cannot see: the chip's own children — the role span, the
   source label, the Sign out button — keep their intrinsic widths. Measured at
   1280 on campaign-manager 2026-08-27: the chip obediently shrank to 26px and
   its 106px child then hung 101px off the side of the page, so the page still
   scrolled AND the chip had become unreadable. Squeezing harder makes both
   worse.
   Wrapping fixes the cause instead. When the rest of the bar fills the row the
   chip moves to the next one, at a readable width, and nothing overflows.
   :has() keeps this to bars that ACTUALLY hold the chip — shell.js decides that
   at runtime, differently per screen — so no other top bar's layout is touched.
   .topbar-right is in the list because placeInHeader PREFERS it and 11 screens
   have one (pipeline, lenders, messaging, closer-dashboard and the rest), so the
   chip's parent is one of two different elements depending on the screen. Those
   eleven measure clean today; covering only the container that happens to be
   broken right now is the half-fix that leaves the other half as a landmine. */
:is(.topbar, .top, .page-hd, header, .topbar-right):has(> #fh-shell-chip) {
  flex-wrap: wrap;
}

:is(.app, .app-shell) :is(.shell, .content, .main),
.app main,
.app-shell main {
  max-width: none !important;
  margin-inline: 0 !important;
  width: 100%;
}

/* THE MARKETING SECTION IS NOT HIDDEN HERE ANY MORE, AND THAT IS THE POINT.
   A rule used to sit right here that said:

     .navgroup[data-fh-section="marketing"] { display: none !important; }

   It hid the whole Marketing box — the heading and all four rows inside it —
   no matter what any other rule said. That made it the trap this note exists
   to stop you falling into: someone would take a row off the hidden list in
   shell.js, take the matching address off the list above, reload, see nothing
   change, and assume they had got it wrong. They had not. The section around
   the row was still gone.
   Two reasons this rule beat everything else. It hid the PARENT, so the row
   never had a chance to paint. And `!important` in a stylesheet beats the
   plain `style="display:"` that shell.js gateLinks() writes on a group it has
   decided to show, so the runtime could not put it back either.
   Nothing needs to replace it. gateLinks() already hides any group whose rows
   are all gated for the person looking, so a staff role sees no lonely
   Marketing heading — it disappears with its rows, on its own. */

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   MOBILE — added 2026-08-05, workflow 1 of the mobile-CRM batch.
   See ops/workflows/mobile-crm.md.

   Two breakpoints for the whole app. Do not invent others.
     860px — sidebar goes off-canvas, content takes the full width
     640px — phone: single column, tables become cards

   The old rule here shrank the rail to a 60px icon strip below 860px and left
   it there, permanently eating 60px of a 390px phone and showing nav as
   unlabelled glyphs. Off-canvas instead: hidden until asked for, full width for
   the content, which is what a phone needs.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

@media (max-width: 860px) {
  /* NOTE ON WHERE THESE RULES REALLY LIVE.
     The width and the content padding-left are set by the lock stylesheet that
     shell.js injects, NOT here — that sheet is appended to <head> at runtime,
     so at equal specificity it beats this file on source order. Declaring the
     width here as well only produced a stylesheet that disagreed with the
     rendered page. What stays here is everything the lock does not touch:
     the transition, the shadow, and the label/padding restoration. */
  aside.side,
  .side {
    transform: translateX(-100%);
    transition: transform .22s ease;
    box-shadow: none;
    will-change: transform;
  }
  aside.side.open,
  .side.open {
    transform: translateX(0);
    box-shadow: 12px 0 34px rgba(0, 0, 0, .45);
  }
  /* Labels always show on mobile — a 60px glyph rail is not navigation. */
  .side.mini .side-top .logo,
  .side.mini .navitem .lbl,
  .side.mini .side-foot .who { display: initial; }
  .side.mini .side-top .logo { display: inline-block; }
  .side.mini .navitem { justify-content: flex-start; padding: 7px 18px; }
  .side.mini .navhead { justify-content: flex-start; padding: 9px 18px 6px; font-size: var(--fs-caption, 11px); letter-spacing: .18em; }
  .side.mini .navhead::after { display: none; }
  .side.mini .navhead .chev { display: initial; }
  .side.mini .side-foot { justify-content: flex-start; padding: 10px 16px; }

  /* Content owns the full width, mini state or not. */
  .app,
  .app-shell,
  html.fh-side-mini .app,
  html.fh-side-mini .app-shell {
    padding-left: 0 !important;
  }

  /* Deliberately NOT setting overflow-x:hidden on html/body here.
     It was tried and removed the same day: it stops the page scrolling
     sideways, but it does that by CLIPPING whatever is too wide, so a 577px
     table in a 390px viewport silently loses 187px and the layout check
     reports the screen as passing. Hiding the symptom would have made the
     remaining four workflows untestable. Overflow stays visible so
     ops/workflows/mobile-check.mjs can fail on it and someone fixes the
     element that is actually too wide. */

  /* UI-STANDARDS §11: "No sideways page scroll." The cap above is a MAXIMUM,
     not a width, so it is already harmless on a phone — but a screen that
     carries its own `margin:0 auto` rather than .fh-maxw hits the same
     cancelled-stretch trap described in fundhub-brand.css, and grows to its
     widest child. Measured at 390px on 2026-08-18: Sales Floor painted 488px
     and Lenders 765px that way. Pinning the wrapper to the viewport fixes it
     without clipping anything — the note above about never using
     overflow-x:hidden still stands, and this is the alternative it asks for. */
  :is(.app, .app-shell) :is(.shell, .content, .main),
  .app main,
  .app-shell main {
    max-width: 100% !important;
  }

  /* The session chip shell.js injects into the top bar carries its geometry as
     an INLINE style (shell.js mountChip), including flex-shrink:0 and no
     max-width. Measured 400px wide inside a 390px row, which pushed 14 screens
     sideways on a phone all by itself. An inline style beats any external
     sheet unless the external one is important, which is why these are.
     Nothing is hidden: the chip is allowed to shrink and wrap onto a second
     line, which shell.js's own lock sheet already permits for the bar. */
  /* (the four chip declarations that were here now apply at every width —
     see the #fh-shell-chip rule higher up in this file) */
  .fh-shell-account-row #fh-shell-chip {
    margin-left: 0 !important;
  }
  .topbar,
  .topbar-right,
  .top,
  .page-hd {
    flex-wrap: wrap !important;
    max-width: 100% !important;
    min-width: 0 !important;
  }
  /* Any named header that receives the shared account controls must own their
     full height. Fixed-height bars used to let the chip paint over the page. */
  :is(.topbar, .top, .page-hd, body > header, .app > header, .app-shell > header):has(#fh-shell-chip) {
    height: auto !important;
    min-height: 57px;
    flex: 0 0 auto !important;
    overflow: visible !important;
    row-gap: 8px;
    padding-top: 8px !important;
    padding-bottom: 8px !important;
  }
  .topbar-right:has(#fh-shell-chip) {
    width: 100%;
    flex-basis: 100%;
    flex-wrap: wrap !important;
  }

  /* Bigger touch targets for the nav itself. */
  .navitem { padding-top: 11px; padding-bottom: 11px; }
}

.q-shift .dot{ width:9px; height:9px; border-radius:50%; background:var(--text-faint); flex:0 0 9px; }
.q-shift.on .dot{ background:var(--green); }
.q-shift .who{ font-weight:600; color:var(--text); }
.q-shift .when{ display:block; color:var(--text-dim); margin-top:2px; }
.q-shift .cta{ margin-top:10px; }

.q-banner{ border-radius:8px; padding:12px 14px; margin-bottom:16px; border:1px solid transparent; display:none; }
.q-banner.show{ display:block; }
.q-banner.err{ color:var(--red); background:var(--red-bg); border-color:rgba(110,42,34,.22); }
.q-banner.ok{ color:var(--green); background:var(--green-bg); border-color:rgba(44,81,56,.22); }

/* ONE ROW PER CALL. .card is on the brand file's shadow list, so it gets
   --panel-shadow for free and this screen never writes a shadow value
   (UI-STANDARDS §12.2). */
.q-list{ display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:12px; }
.card{ background:var(--surface); border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:10px; padding:16px; }
.q-row{ display:flex; align-items:flex-start; gap:16px; flex-wrap:wrap; }
.q-who{ flex:1 1 260px; min-width:0; }
.q-name{ font-weight:600; color:var(--text); display:inline-block; max-width:100%; overflow:hidden;
         text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap; vertical-align:bottom; }
.q-name:hover{ text-decoration:underline; }
.q-what{ color:var(--text-dim); margin-top:2px; }
.q-facts{ display:flex; gap:8px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-top:8px; align-items:center; }
.q-acts{ display:flex; gap:8px; align-items:center; flex-wrap:wrap; }

/* STATUS IS NEVER COLOUR ALONE (UI-STANDARDS §12.6) — every chip says its word.
   A white-label tenant with one hue paints --alert and --ok the same colour. */
.chip{ border:1px solid var(--soft); border-radius:999px; padding:4px 10px; color:var(--text-dim);
       background:var(--paper); white-space:nowrap; }
.chip.late{ color:var(--red); background:var(--red-bg); border-color:rgba(110,42,34,.28); }
.chip.owed{ color:var(--amber); background:var(--amber-bg); border-color:rgba(107,74,18,.28); }
.chip.mine{ color:var(--green); background:var(--green-bg); border-color:rgba(44,81,56,.28); }
.chip.num{ font-family:var(--mono); font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; }
/* Capital Blueprint rows say so in words and carry a solid border, so the mark survives a one-hue brand. */
.chip.bp{ color:var(--text); border-color:var(--ink2); font-weight:600; }

.btn{ border:1px solid var(--ink2); background:var(--ink2); color:var(--paper); border-radius:7px;
      padding:10px 16px; font-weight:600; cursor:pointer; min-height:40px; }
.btn:hover{ opacity:.9; }
.btn[disabled]{ opacity:.45; cursor:not-allowed; }
.btn.ghost{ background:transparent; color:var(--text); border-color:var(--soft); }
.btn.ghost:hover{ border-color:var(--gray2); }

/* THE ANSWER FORM (GAP 38). Collapsed until the CSM opens the row —
   UI-STANDARDS §9, the daily 20% is the list, the form is one click deeper. */
.q-form{ border-top:1px solid var(--line); margin-top:14px; padding-top:14px; display:none; }
.q-form.open{ display:block; }
.q-field{ margin-top:12px; }
.q-field label{ display:block; color:var(--text); font-weight:600; margin-bottom:5px; }
.q-input, .q-area, .q-select{ width:100%; border:1px solid var(--soft); border-radius:6px; padding:9px 11px;
                              background:var(--surface); }
.q-area{ min-height:64px; resize:vertical; }
.q-notes{ max-width:78ch; }
.q-save{ display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:center; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-top:14px; }
.q-say{ display:none; border-radius:6px; padding:8px 11px; }
.q-say.show{ display:inline-block; }
.q-say.ok{ color:var(--green); background:var(--green-bg); }
.q-say.err{ color:var(--red); background:var(--red-bg); }

.q-empty{ color:var(--text-dim); }
.q-foot-note{ margin-top:20px; }
.q-link{ text-decoration:underline; }
.q-empty .btn{ margin-top:12px; }

/* LOADING — skeletons in the real layout, never a full-page spinner (§6.1). */
.q-skel{ height:74px; border-radius:10px; border:1px solid var(--line); background:var(--paper);
         opacity:.6; animation:qpulse 1.2s ease-in-out infinite; }
@keyframes qpulse{ 0%,100%{opacity:.35} 50%{opacity:.7} }

  .q-head{ gap:16px; }
  .q-shift{ min-width:0; width:100%; }
  .q-acts{ width:100%; }
}

      <div class="q-head">

<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";

  /* THE CSM'S DAY, IN ONE SCREEN.
   *
   * GET /api/read/csm-queue has returned the right rows since the day it
   * shipped, and until 2026-09-17 nothing in public/ had ever asked it for
   * them: a grep of the whole app for "csm-queue" returned nothing. The CSM's
   * home was the pick-a-client Client Control Panel, so the first thing the
   * role saw was a chooser, not a call list (live walk 2026-09-17, GAP 34).
   *
   * Three jobs, one screen: who to call, get on shift and take the row, write
   * down what they said.
   */

  function $(id) { return document.getElementById(id); }

  function esc(s) {
    return String(s == null ? "" : s)
      .replace(/&/g, "&amp;").replace(/</g, "&lt;").replace(/>/g, "&gt;")
      .replace(/"/g, "&quot;").replace(/'/g, "&#39;");
  }

  /* The session token is a Bearer header when the screen has one and a
     same-origin cookie otherwise — src/http/middleware/requireAuth.mjs accepts
     either, and calendar.html and consent-capture.html each use one of them. */
  function api(path, options) {
    var init = options || {};
    init.headers = init.headers || {};
    init.headers.accept = "application/json";
    try {
      var t = localStorage.getItem("fh_token") || "";
      if (t && t !== "demo" && t !== "demo-token") init.headers.authorization = "Bearer " + t;
    } catch (e) {}
    if (init.body !== undefined) {
      init.headers["content-type"] = "application/json";
      init.body = JSON.stringify(init.body);
    }
    init.credentials = "same-origin";
    return fetch(path, init).then(
      function (r) {
        return r.json().then(
          function (b) { return { status: r.status, body: b }; },
          function () { return { status: r.status, body: null }; }
        );
      },
      function (e) { return { status: 0, body: null, transport: (e && e.message) || "network error" }; }
    );
  }

  /* WHAT WENT WRONG, IN THE WORDS OF THE PERSON IT HAPPENED TO — never a raw
     status code (UI-STANDARDS §6.3). The two shift-shaped refusals reuse
     calendar.html's existing sentences rather than inventing a second set of
     words for the same two facts. */
  function problem(res) {
    var err = String((res.body && res.body.error) || "");
    if (res.transport || res.status === 0) return "Could not reach the server. Check your connection and try again.";
    if (res.status === 401) return "You are signed out. Sign in and open this page again.";
    if (err === "no_active_shift") return "Clock in first. Work can only be claimed or closed on a shift.";
    if (err === "already_claimed") return "Somebody else took this one first.";
    if (err === "shift_already_open") return "You are already on a shift.";
    if (err === "no_open_shift") return "You are not on a shift right now.";
    if (res.status === 403) return "Your account is not allowed to do that.";
    if (res.status === 404) return "That is gone. Reload the page.";
    if (res.status === 503) return "The database is not reachable right now. Try again in a moment.";
    if (res.body && res.body.message) return String(res.body.message);
    return "That did not work. Try again in a moment.";
  }

  function banner(tone, text) {
    var el = $("qBanner");
    el.className = "q-banner show " + tone;
    el.textContent = text;
  }
  function clearBanner() { $("qBanner").className = "q-banner"; }

  /* Relative under a day, absolute after, exact time always in the tooltip
     (UI-STANDARDS §7). "No date" is said out loud rather than left blank. */
  function whenText(iso) {
    if (!iso) return { text: "No date set", title: "" };
    var d = new Date(iso);
    if (isNaN(d.getTime())) return { text: "No date set", title: "" };
    var diff = d.getTime() - Date.now();
    var hours = Math.round(Math.abs(diff) / 3600000);
    var title = d.toLocaleString();
    if (hours < 24) {
      if (hours < 1) return { text: diff >= 0 ? "Due now" : "Due now", title: title };
      return { text: diff >= 0 ? "Due in " + hours + "h" : hours + "h ago", title: title };
    }
    return {
      text: d.toLocaleDateString(undefined, { month: "short", day: "numeric", year: "numeric" }),
      title: title
    };
  }

  /* HOW LATE THE CALL IS, in whole days, from the call's OWN due date.
     Nothing else on this row measures the call. The money chip measures the
     BILL, and the two are different facts about the same client — a 30-day-old
     invoice says nothing about whether today's call is late. Returns null when
     there is no date, the date is unreadable, or the call is not late yet. */
  function callLateDays(iso) {
    if (!iso) return null;
    var d = new Date(iso);
    if (isNaN(d.getTime())) return null;
    var ms = Date.now() - d.getTime();
    if (ms <= 0) return null;
    return Math.floor(ms / 86400000);
  }

  /* MID or POST, read off the row's own source_workflow. Anything else is a CSM
     task from another workflow and simply has no interview form. */
  function stageOf(row) {
    if (row.source_workflow === "customer-insights-mid") return "mid";
    if (row.source_workflow === "customer-insights-post") return "post";
    return null;
  }

  /* CAPITAL BLUEPRINT EXCEPTION TASKS. They are ordinary CSM tasks, told apart
     by the source_workflow the backend stamps on them (src/blueprint/
     coach-exception.mjs and closer-ready.mjs). Nothing here asks the queue for
     anything new: the read already carries source_workflow and
     assignee_staff_id. */
  var BLUEPRINT_KIND = {
    "blueprint-coach": "Exception: client stopped coach texts",
    "blueprint-csm-prep": "Closing prep call before the closer"
  };
  function blueprintKind(row) { return BLUEPRINT_KIND[row.source_workflow] || null; }

  var state = {
    rows: [],
    shift: null,          // the open shift row, or null
    myStaffId: null,      // read off the shift; it is the only id this screen gets
    questions: null,      // { mid: [...], post: [...] } from the read endpoint
    open: null            // task_id whose answer form is showing
  };

  /* ── the shift ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

  function paintShift() {
    var box = $("qShift");
    var btn = $("qClock");
    btn.disabled = false;
    if (state.shift) {
      box.className = "q-shift on";
      $("qShiftWho").textContent = "You are on shift";
      var started = state.shift.started_at ? new Date(state.shift.started_at) : null;
      $("qShiftWhen").textContent = started && !isNaN(started.getTime())
        ? "Since " + started.toLocaleTimeString("en-US", { hour: "numeric", minute: "2-digit", timeZone: "America/Phoenix" })
        : "";
      btn.textContent = "End shift";
    } else {
      box.className = "q-shift";
      $("qShiftWho").textContent = "You are not clocked in";
      $("qShiftWhen").textContent = "Start a shift before you claim a call.";
      btn.textContent = "Start shift";
    }
  }

  function loadShift() {
    return api("/api/shifts").then(function (res) {
      if (res.status !== 200 || !res.body || !res.body.ok) {
        $("qShiftWho").textContent = "Cannot read your shift";
        $("qShiftWhen").textContent = problem(res);
        $("qClock").disabled = true;
        return;
      }
      state.shift = res.body.shift || null;
      state.myStaffId = state.shift ? (state.shift.staff_id || null) : state.myStaffId;
      paintShift();
    });
  }

  function toggleClock() {
    var btn = $("qClock");
    var goingOn = !state.shift;
    btn.disabled = true;
    btn.textContent = goingOn ? "Starting…" : "Ending…";
    clearBanner();
    // staff_id and org_id are deliberately NOT sent: api/shifts.mjs refuses a
    // body that carries either, and takes both off the session instead.
    api("/api/shifts", { method: "POST", body: { action: goingOn ? "clock_in" : "clock_out" } })
      .then(function (res) {
        if (res.status !== 200 || !res.body || !res.body.ok) {
          banner("err", problem(res));
          return loadShift();
        }
        state.shift = goingOn ? (res.body.shift || null) : null;
        if (state.shift && state.shift.staff_id) state.myStaffId = state.shift.staff_id;
        paintShift();
        banner("ok", goingOn ? "You are on shift. You can claim calls now." : "Shift ended.");
      });
  }

  /* ── the queue ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

  function moneyChip(row) {
    /* NULL SURVIVES. The endpoint returns null when the client has no invoice
       at all, which means "unknown until you look", not zero. A dash is the
       honest render; a "$0.00" here would be a number nobody measured
       (CLAUDE.md §12). */
    if (row.balance_due === null || row.balance_due === undefined) {
      return '<span class="chip num" title="No invoice on file for this client">Owes —</span>';
    }
    var n = row.open_invoices === 1 ? "1 invoice" : row.open_invoices + " invoices";
    /* bill_days_overdue is the OLDEST UNPAID INVOICE's lateness, so it belongs
       inside the money chip and nowhere near the call. It used to be printed on
       its own as "30 days overdue" right beside the call time, which read as a
       late call and is not one. */
    var billLate = "";
    if (row.bill_days_overdue !== null && row.bill_days_overdue !== undefined &&
        row.bill_days_overdue > 0) {
      billLate = " · bill " + (row.bill_days_overdue === 1
        ? "1 day late" : row.bill_days_overdue + " days late");
    }
    return '<span class="chip owed num" title="What this client still owes. This is ' +
      'about their bill, not about this call.">Owes $' + esc(row.balance_due) +
      " · " + esc(n) + esc(billLate) + "</span>";
  }

  function rowHtml(row) {
    var name = row.client_name || row.client_code || "Unnamed client";
    var when = whenText(row.due_at);
    var lateDays = callLateDays(row.due_at);
    var mine = state.myStaffId && row.assignee_staff_id === state.myStaffId;
    var taken = row.assignee_staff_id && !mine;

    var chips = '<span class="chip" title="' + esc(when.title) + '">' + esc(when.text) + "</span>";
    if (lateDays !== null) {
      chips += '<span class="chip late num" title="This call was due ' + esc(when.title) +
        ' and has not been done.">Call ' +
        (lateDays < 1 ? "late today" : esc(lateDays) + (lateDays === 1 ? " day late" : " days late")) +
        "</span>";
    }
    chips += moneyChip(row);
    for (var i = 0; i < row.owned_codes.length; i++) {
      chips += '<span class="chip">Has ' + esc(row.owned_codes[i]) + "</span>";
    }
    var bpKind = blueprintKind(row);
    if (bpKind) chips = '<span class="chip bp" title="' + esc(bpKind) + '">Capital Blueprint</span>' + chips;
    if (row.source_workflow === "blueprint-csm-prep") {
      /* The prep task is created for the CSM assigned to the client when there
         is one (createBlueprintCsmPrepCallTask), so a holder here is that
         CSM. Nobody holding it means no CSM was assigned yet. */
      /* assigned_csm_name is the CSM on the client's file (api/read/csm-queue),
         which is not always the holder of the task. Use the name when there is
         one; fall back to the holder wording when the read has none. */
      var csmName = row.assigned_csm_name ? String(row.assigned_csm_name) : "";
      if (csmName) chips += '<span class="chip' + (mine ? " mine" : "") + '" title="The CSM assigned to this client\'s file.">Assigned CSM: ' + esc(csmName) + "</span>";
      else if (mine) chips += '<span class="chip mine" title="This prep call sits with the CSM on this client\'s file.">Assigned CSM: you</span>';
      else if (taken) chips += '<span class="chip" title="This prep call sits with the CSM on this client\'s file.">Assigned CSM: a teammate</span>';
      else chips += '<span class="chip" title="No CSM holds this prep call yet.">No CSM assigned yet</span>';
    } else if (mine) chips += '<span class="chip mine">Claimed by you</span>';
    else if (taken) chips += '<span class="chip">Claimed by a teammate</span>';

    var acts = "";
    if (!row.assignee_staff_id) {
      acts += '<button class="btn ghost" type="button" data-claim="' + esc(row.task_id) + '">Claim this call</button>';
    }
    if (stageOf(row)) {
      acts += '<button class="btn ghost" type="button" data-open="' + esc(row.task_id) + '">' +
              (state.open === row.task_id ? "Hide answers" : "Write down their answers") + "</button>";
    }
    if (row.meeting_url) {
      acts += '<a class="btn ghost" href="' + esc(row.meeting_url) + '" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Booking link</a>';
    }

    return '<div class="card" data-row="' + esc(row.task_id) + '">' +
      '<div class="q-row">' +
        '<div class="q-who">' +
          '<a class="q-name" href="client-control-panel.html?client_id=' + esc(row.client_id) + '">' + esc(name) + "</a>" +
          '<div class="q-what">' + esc(row.title) + "</div>" +
          '<div class="q-facts">' + chips + "</div>" +
        "</div>" +
        '<div class="q-acts">' + acts + "</div>" +
      "</div>" +
      (state.open === row.task_id ? formHtml(row) : "") +
      "</div>";
  }

  /* THE ANSWER FORM (GAP 38). There were 0 rows in customer_insights because no
     screen had ever posted to /api/customer-insights, and the task body told
     the CSM to call the API by hand. The questions come from the read endpoint,
     which already serves the one question bank (src/insights/questions.mjs) —
     this screen never keeps a second copy of them. */
  function formHtml(row) {
    var stage = stageOf(row);
    var list = (state.questions && state.questions[stage]) || [];
    if (!list.length) {
      return '<div class="q-form open"><p class="q-empty">The question list did not load. ' +
             "Reload the page and open this row again.</p></div>";
    }
    var channel = stage === "post" ? "google_meet" : "call";
    var h = '<div class="q-form open">' +
      '<div class="q-field">' +
        '<label for="qChan">How did you speak to them?</label>' +
        '<select class="q-select" id="qChan">' +
          '<option value="call"' + (channel === "call" ? " selected" : "") + ">Phone call</option>" +
          '<option value="google_meet"' + (channel === "google_meet" ? " selected" : "") + ">Google Meet</option>" +
          '<option value="ai_reachout">AI reach-out</option>' +
        "</select>" +
      "</div>";
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      h += '<div class="q-field">' +
             '<label for="qa-' + esc(list[i].id) + '">' + esc(list[i].prompt) + "</label>" +
             '<textarea class="q-area" id="qa-' + esc(list[i].id) + '" data-answer="' + esc(list[i].id) + '"></textarea>' +
           "</div>";
    }
    h += '<div class="q-field q-notes">' +
           '<label for="qNotes">Anything else worth keeping</label>' +
           '<textarea class="q-area" id="qNotes" placeholder="Optional."></textarea>' +
         "</div>" +
         '<div class="q-save">' +
           '<button class="btn" type="button" data-save="' + esc(row.task_id) + '">Save these answers</button>' +
           '<span class="q-say" id="qSay"></span>' +
         "</div>" +
       "</div>";
    return h;
  }

  function paintQueue() {
    var list = $("qList");
    if (!state.rows.length) {
      $("qCount").textContent = "0";
      $("qCountLabel").textContent = "calls waiting";
      $("qOverdue").textContent = "Nothing is due.";
      list.innerHTML = '<div class="card q-empty">' +
        "<p>No calls are waiting for you.</p>" +
        "<p>A call appears here when a client pays (the halfway check-in) or when a " +
        "funding round lands (the results call).</p>" +
        '<a class="btn ghost" href="client-control-panel.html">Open a client instead</a>' +
        "</div>";
      return;
    }
    /* COUNTS LATE CALLS, not late bills. The headline sits above a list of
       calls, so the only number that belongs in it is how many of those calls
       are past their own due time. */
    var late = 0;
    for (var i = 0; i < state.rows.length; i++) {
      if (callLateDays(state.rows[i].due_at) !== null) late++;
    }
    $("qCount").textContent = String(state.rows.length);
    $("qCountLabel").textContent = state.rows.length === 1 ? "call waiting" : "calls waiting";
    $("qOverdue").textContent = late
      ? (late === 1 ? "1 call past due" : late + " calls past due")
      : "No calls past due";
    var bpCount = 0;
    for (var b = 0; b < state.rows.length; b++) if (blueprintKind(state.rows[b])) bpCount++;
    if (bpCount) {
      $("qOverdue").textContent += " · " + bpCount +
        (bpCount === 1 ? " Capital Blueprint exception" : " Capital Blueprint exceptions");
    }

    var html = "";
    for (var j = 0; j < state.rows.length; j++) html += rowHtml(state.rows[j]);
    list.innerHTML = html;
  }

  function loadQueue() {
    return api("/api/read/csm-queue").then(function (res) {
      if (res.status !== 200 || !res.body || !res.body.ok) {
        $("qCount").textContent = "—";
        $("qCountLabel").textContent = "queue did not load";
        $("qOverdue").textContent = "";
        $("qList").innerHTML = '<div class="card q-empty">' + esc(problem(res)) +
          ' <a class="q-link" href="client-control-panel.html">Open the Client Control Panel</a>' +
          " while this is down.</div>";
        return;
      }
      state.rows = (res.body.items || []).slice();
      paintQueue();
      $("qStamp").textContent = "read " + new Date().toLocaleTimeString("en-US", { timeZone: "America/Phoenix" });
    });
  }

  /* The question bank rides along on the interview READ endpoint, which returns
     it on every response. limit=1 because the rows are not what this is for. */
  function loadQuestions() {
    return api("/api/read/customer-insights?limit=1").then(function (res) {
      if (res.status === 200 && res.body && res.body.questions) state.questions = res.body.questions;
    });
  }

  /* ── the two writes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

  function claim(taskId, btn) {
    clearBanner();
    btn.disabled = true;
    btn.textContent = "Claiming…";
    api("/api/tasks", { method: "PATCH", body: { id: taskId, claim: true } }).then(function (res) {
      if (res.status !== 200 || !res.body || !res.body.ok) {
        banner("err", problem(res));
        return loadQueue();
      }
      /* The claim is what tells this screen who the signed-in person is: the
         queue read carries assignee_staff_id but never "you". */
      var task = res.body.task || {};
      if (task.assignee_staff_id) state.myStaffId = task.assignee_staff_id;
      banner("ok", "This call is yours.");
      return loadQueue();
    });
  }

  function save(taskId, btn) {
    var row = null;
    for (var i = 0; i < state.rows.length; i++) {
      if (state.rows[i].task_id === taskId) row = state.rows[i];
    }
    if (!row) return;

    var answers = {};
    var boxes = document.querySelectorAll("[data-answer]");
    for (var j = 0; j < boxes.length; j++) {
      var v = boxes[j].value.trim();
      if (v) answers[boxes[j].getAttribute("data-answer")] = v;
    }
    var say = $("qSay");
    if (!Object.keys(answers).length) {
      say.className = "q-say show err";
      say.textContent = "Write down at least one answer before saving.";
      return;
    }

    btn.disabled = true;
    btn.textContent = "Saving…";
    say.className = "q-say";
    api("/api/customer-insights", {
      method: "POST",
      body: {
        client_id: row.client_id,
        task_id: row.task_id,
        stage: stageOf(row),
        channel: $("qChan").value,
        answers: answers,
        notes: $("qNotes").value.trim() || null
      }
    }).then(function (res) {
      btn.disabled = false;
      btn.textContent = "Save these answers";
      if (res.status !== 201 || !res.body || !res.body.ok) {
        say.className = "q-say show err";
        // The store writes a readable sentence on every InsightError; show that
        // rather than the code beside it.
        say.textContent = problem(res);
        return;
      }
      state.open = null;
      banner("ok", "Answers saved for " + (row.client_name || row.client_code || "this client") + ".");
      paintQueue();
    });
  }

  /* One delegated listener: the rows are repainted on every read, so a listener
     per button would have to be rebound each time. */
  $("qList").addEventListener("click", function (e) {
    var t = e.target;
    while (t && t !== this) {
      if (t.getAttribute) {
        if (t.getAttribute("data-claim")) { claim(t.getAttribute("data-claim"), t); return; }
        if (t.getAttribute("data-save")) { save(t.getAttribute("data-save"), t); return; }
        if (t.getAttribute("data-open")) {
          var id = t.getAttribute("data-open");
          state.open = state.open === id ? null : id;
          paintQueue();
          return;
        }
      }
      t = t.parentNode;
    }
  });

  $("qClock").addEventListener("click", toggleClock);

  loadQuestions();
  loadShift();
  loadQueue();
})();
</script>
</body>
</html>
