<script>
/* ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   FHInquiryView — the screen's decision logic.

   THIS BLOCK IS A VERBATIM COPY of src/http/inquiry-remover-view.mjs, from its
   first `export` onward, with the word `export ` stripped, wrapped in an IIFE
   that returns VIEW. DO NOT EDIT IT HERE. Edit the module, then paste it back:
   src/http/inquiry-remover-view.test.mjs compares the two character for
   character and fails the build if they differ.

   Why a copy at all: npm test globs src/** and scripts/** only, so anything
   that lives solely inside this file is untestable by construction — and this
   screen's logic decides whether a consumer's credit-report action is shown as
   having happened. public/ is the static publish root and cannot import from
   src/, so the choice is a copy with a drift test or logic nobody can test.
   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
window.FHInquiryView = (function () {
"use strict";
/* ==FHVIEW-BEGIN== */
const ATTEMPT_KINDS = ["call", "letter", "portal", "note"];

// Mirrors COUNTING_KINDS in src/inquiries/work.mjs: a working note is logged in
// the same timeline but does not count toward call_attempts, because a desk that
// inflates its attempt count is lying to a bureau, slowly.
const COUNTING_KINDS = ["call", "letter", "portal"];

const UUID_RE = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i;

class ViewError extends Error {
  constructor(message) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "ViewError";
  }
}

function isUuid(v) {
  return typeof v === "string" && UUID_RE.test(v.trim());
}

/* blankToNull — "the user typed nothing" is not a value. Whitespace-only input
   collapses to null so it is omitted from a body rather than stored as text
   nobody wrote. */
function blankToNull(v) {
  if (v === null || v === undefined) return null;
  const s = String(v).trim();
  return s === "" ? null : s;
}

/* pill — status text → the pill class the screen renders.
   Mapped ONLY where the wording is unambiguous. inquiry_log.status is free text
   written by several producers (the external spreadsheet runtime among them), so an
   unrecognised value keeps its real text on a neutral pill and is counted into
   the banner as unmapped. A complete mapping would be an invention, and 055
   deliberately declined to constrain the column for the same reason. */
function pill(status, outcome) {
  const s = String(status || outcome || "").trim();
  const k = s.toLowerCase();
  if (!s) return { cls: "new", text: "No status recorded", known: false, done: false };
  if (/removed|confirmed|deleted|cleared/.test(k)) return { cls: "confirmed", text: s, known: true, done: true };
  if (/no answer|unreachable/.test(k)) return { cls: "noanswer", text: s, known: true, done: false };
  if (/filed|sent|progress|pending/.test(k)) return { cls: "progress", text: s, known: true, done: false };
  if (/new|queued/.test(k)) return { cls: "new", text: s, known: true, done: false };
  return { cls: "", text: s, known: false, done: false };
}

/* ── REQUEST SHAPING ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Every builder returns { method, path, body? } and throws rather than
   producing a request that cannot succeed. The ids come from data- attributes
   the wiring block copies off the read response; a row rendered from the sample
   markup has none, and firing a POST at a missing or malformed id would be a
   write aimed at nothing.                                                     */

function requireInquiryId(id) {
  if (!isUuid(id)) throw new ViewError("inquiry_id must be a uuid — this row is not a database row");
}

function requireClientId(id) {
  if (!isUuid(id)) throw new ViewError("client_id must be a uuid — this row is not a database row");
}

function buildAttemptRequest(opts) {
  const o = opts || {};
  requireInquiryId(o.inquiryId);
  const kind = o.kind === undefined || o.kind === null ? "call" : String(o.kind);
  if (ATTEMPT_KINDS.indexOf(kind) === -1) {
    throw new ViewError("unknown attempt kind: " + kind);
  }
  const body = { inquiry_id: o.inquiryId, action: "attempt", kind: kind };
  const outcome = blankToNull(o.outcome);
  const note = blankToNull(o.note);
  if (outcome !== null) body.outcome = outcome;
  if (note !== null) body.note = note;
  return { method: "POST", path: "/api/inquiries", body: body };
}

/* confirmRemoval defaults to status "Removed" server-side, chosen there to match
   wording already present in the live data. Restating it here would fork the
   default across two files; the screen sends a status only when a human typed
   one. */
function buildConfirmRequest(opts) {
  const o = opts || {};
  requireInquiryId(o.inquiryId);
  const body = { inquiry_id: o.inquiryId, action: "confirm" };
  const status = blankToNull(o.status);
  if (status !== null) body.status = status;
  return { method: "POST", path: "/api/inquiries", body: body };
}

function buildStatusRequest(opts) {
  const o = opts || {};
  requireInquiryId(o.inquiryId);
  const status = blankToNull(o.status);
  if (status === null) throw new ViewError("a status is required");
  return {
    method: "POST",
    path: "/api/inquiries",
    body: { inquiry_id: o.inquiryId, action: "status", status: status }
  };
}

function buildExpectedRequest(opts) {
  const o = opts || {};
  requireInquiryId(o.inquiryId);
  const expected = blankToNull(o.expectedName);
  if (expected === null) throw new ViewError("an expected name is required");
  return {
    method: "POST",
    path: "/api/inquiries",
    body: { inquiry_id: o.inquiryId, action: "expected", expected_name: expected }
  };
}

function buildAttemptsRequest(opts) {
  const o = opts || {};
  requireInquiryId(o.inquiryId);
  return { method: "GET", path: "/api/inquiries?inquiry_id=" + encodeURIComponent(o.inquiryId) };
}

function buildIdentityRequest(opts) {
  const o = opts || {};
  requireClientId(o.clientId);
  return { method: "GET", path: "/api/pii?client_id=" + encodeURIComponent(o.clientId) };
}

/* buildRevealRequest — the only call in this file that discloses a protected
   value, and the only one that refuses to run on missing input rather than
   defaulting it.

   THE REASON IS NOT OPTIONAL HERE. src/pii/index.mjs states it as rule 4 — "A
   REASON IS REQUIRED. Every reveal records who, what field, and when" — and
   api/pii.mjs now rejects a reveal with no reason with a 400, so this check is
   the screen agreeing with the server rather than substituting for it. Keep
   both: failing here means the user gets told before a request is sent, and
   failing there means curl gets told too. What this must NEVER do is satisfy
   the parameter with filler, which would fill the audit log with a sentence
   nobody wrote and make every entry equally worthless.

   The reason and the client id travel in the BODY. Nothing here goes in a URL:
   query strings are logged, cached and forwarded by things nobody audits. */
function buildRevealRequest(opts) {
  const o = opts || {};
  requireClientId(o.clientId);
  const reason = blankToNull(o.reason);
  if (reason === null) {
    throw new ViewError("a reason is required — every reveal is written to pii_access_log");
  }
  return {
    method: "POST",
    path: "/api/pii",
    body: { client_id: o.clientId, action: "reveal", reason: reason }
  };
}

/* ── FAILURE → BANNER COPY ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   `res` is what the HTML's send() produces and never a thrown error:
     { transport: true, detail }        the request never got an answer
     { status, body }                   an answer, body possibly null
   Returns { code, tone, text, status, scope, saved } where `saved` is "no" when
   the request is known to have been rejected before any write, and "unknown"
   when it might have landed.                                                  */

const ENDPOINT = { inquiry: "/api/inquiries", identity: "/api/pii" };

function failure(code, text, extra) {
  return Object.assign({ code: code, tone: "error", text: text, status: null, saved: "no" }, extra || {});
}

function describeFailure(res, opts) {
  const scope = (opts && opts.scope) === "identity" ? "identity" : "inquiry";
  const endpoint = ENDPOINT[scope];
  const body = res && res.body && typeof res.body === "object" ? res.body : null;
  const detail = body && typeof body.error === "string" ? body.error : null;
  const suffix = detail ? " (" + detail + ")" : "";

  // No answer at all. The request may have reached the server and committed
  // before the connection dropped, so this is the one case that must not tell
  // the user their click did nothing.
  if (!res || res.transport) {
    return failure("offline",
      "could not reach " + endpoint + " — reload before assuming this did not save" +
      (res && res.detail ? " (" + res.detail + ")" : ""),
      { scope: scope, saved: "unknown" });
  }

  const status = Number(res.status) || 0;
  const base = { status: status, scope: scope };

  // TWO DIFFERENT 404s. The router's fallthrough answers {error:"not_found",
  // path:"..."} for a path nothing serves — the endpoint is in the repo and not
  // deployed, which is an ops problem. A 404 from the handler itself means the
  // row is gone, which is a data problem. Telling a closer the backend is down
  // when it is up and answering honestly sends someone hunting a fault that
  // does not exist.
  if (status === 404 && body && body.error === "not_found" && typeof body.path === "string") {
    return failure("unrouted",
      endpoint + " is not deployed — the handler exists but no route serves it. Nothing was saved.",
      base);
  }
  if (status === 404) {
    return failure("not_found",
      scope === "identity"
        ? "no identity on file for this client" + suffix
        : "that inquiry is no longer in the database" + suffix,
      base);
  }
  if (status === 401) {
    return failure("unauthorized", "your session has expired — sign in again. Nothing was saved.", base);
  }
  if (status === 403) {
    return failure("forbidden",
      scope === "identity"
        ? "your role cannot see identity data — /api/pii is limited to owner, admin, inquiry specialist and funding advisor"
        : "your role cannot write to the inquiry queue. Nothing was saved.",
      base);
  }
  if (status === 400) {
    return failure("bad_request", "the request was rejected" + suffix + ". Nothing was saved.", base);
  }
  if (status === 405) {
    return failure("method_not_allowed", endpoint + " refused the method. Nothing was saved.", base);
  }
  // requirePrincipal answers 503 {error:"auth_unavailable", db:"down"} when the
  // session lookup itself could not run — the write never started.
  if (status === 503 && body && (body.error === "auth_unavailable" || body.db === "down")) {
    return failure("db_down", "the database is unreachable — nothing was saved", base);
  }
  // The other 503 on this screen is PiiError's: the encryption key is not set,
  // so the server is refusing to handle identity data at all.
  if (status === 503) {
    return failure("unavailable",
      (detail || "the endpoint is unavailable") + " — nothing was saved", base);
  }
  if (status >= 500) {
    return failure("server_error",
      "the server failed" + suffix + " — reload before assuming this did not save",
      Object.assign({ saved: "unknown" }, base));
  }
  return failure("unexpected", "unexpected response " + status + suffix, Object.assign({ saved: "unknown" }, base));
}

/* interpretWrite — the single place a POST /api/inquiries response becomes
   either a row to render or a banner to show. A 200 whose body is not
   {ok:true} is a failure however friendly its status code was. */
function interpretWrite(res) {
  if (res && !res.transport && Number(res.status) === 200 &&
      res.body && res.body.ok === true) {
    return { ok: true, inquiry: res.body.inquiry || null };
  }
  return { ok: false, failure: describeFailure(res, { scope: "inquiry" }) };
}

/* interpretAttempts — GET /api/inquiries?inquiry_id=. An empty list is an
   answer: a row nobody has worked yet has no attempts, which is different from
   a history we could not fetch. */
function interpretAttempts(res) {
  if (res && !res.transport && Number(res.status) === 200 &&
      res.body && res.body.ok === true && Array.isArray(res.body.attempts)) {
    return { ok: true, attempts: res.body.attempts };
  }
  return { ok: false, failure: describeFailure(res, { scope: "inquiry" }) };
}

function interpretIdentity(res) {
  if (res && !res.transport && Number(res.status) === 200 &&
      res.body && res.body.ok === true) {
    // A client with no identity row is a 200 with identity:null. That is an
    // answer, not a failure — "we have nothing on file" is a fact the screen
    // should state plainly.
    return { ok: true, identity: res.body.identity || null };
  }
  return { ok: false, failure: describeFailure(res, { scope: "identity" }) };
}

function interpretReveal(res) {
  if (res && !res.transport && Number(res.status) === 200 &&
      res.body && res.body.ok === true && typeof res.body.ssn === "string") {
    return { ok: true, ssn: res.body.ssn };
  }
  return { ok: false, failure: describeFailure(res, { scope: "identity" }) };
}

/* ── IDENTITY DISPLAY ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Masked is the default and the only thing rendered without a deliberate act.
   Three states, none of them guessed:
     no row at all           → nothing is on file for this person
     row without an SSN      → we hold a DOB/addresses but no number
     row whose key is missing→ readIdentity() returns ssn_last4:null when the
                               ciphertext cannot be opened. That is "unavailable",
                               NOT "this client has no SSN", and the difference
                               decides whether someone goes looking for a key. */
function maskedSsnLabel(identity) {
  if (!identity) return { text: "no identity record on file", present: false, degraded: false };
  if (!identity.ssn_present) return { text: "no SSN on file", present: false, degraded: false };
  if (!identity.ssn_last4) {
    return { text: "SSN on file · last four unavailable", present: true, degraded: true };
  }
  return { text: "SSN ***-**-" + String(identity.ssn_last4), present: true, degraded: false };
}

function canReveal(identity) {
  return !!(identity && identity.ssn_present);
}

/* formatRevealed — group nine digits for reading. Anything that is not nine
   digits is returned untouched: reshaping a value we do not recognise would be
   asserting something about it. */
function formatRevealed(ssn) {
  const raw = ssn === null || ssn === undefined ? "" : String(ssn);
  const d = raw.replace(/\D/g, "");
  if (d.length !== 9) return raw;
  return d.slice(0, 3) + "-" + d.slice(3, 5) + "-" + d.slice(5);
}

/* ── THE ROW STATE MACHINE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   idle → pending → idle. Three transitions, no fourth, and the displayed state
   changes on exactly one of them.

   `done` is the flag that decides whether a row reads as Removed, so it has two
   sources and takes either: confirmed_at is the unambiguous one 055 added, and
   the free-text status is what the external runtime writes. Requiring both
   would un-confirm rows that were confirmed before 055 existed.               */

function createRowState(row) {
  const r = row || {};
  const p = pill(r.status, r.outcome);
  return {
    phase: "idle",
    status: r.status === undefined ? null : r.status,
    outcome: r.outcome === undefined ? null : r.outcome,
    attempts: r.call_attempts === undefined || r.call_attempts === null
      ? null : Number(r.call_attempts),
    done: r.confirmed_at ? true : p.done,
    pending: null,
    error: null,
    refused: null,
    snapshot: null,
    stale: false
  };
}

function idleFrom(base) {
  return {
    phase: "idle",
    status: base.status,
    outcome: base.outcome,
    attempts: base.attempts,
    done: base.done,
    pending: null,
    error: null,
    refused: null,
    snapshot: null,
    stale: false
  };
}

/* beginWrite — arm the write. NOTE WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it does not change
   status, done or attempts. The row goes on looking exactly as it did until the
   server answers. A second click while one is in flight is refused rather than
   sent, because two attempt POSTs for one human action is a double-count on a
   dispute record. */
function beginWrite(state, action) {
  if (state.phase === "pending") {
    return Object.assign({}, state, { refused: "busy" });
  }
  return Object.assign({}, state, {
    phase: "pending",
    pending: action || null,
    error: null,
    refused: null,
    stale: false,
    snapshot: {
      status: state.status,
      outcome: state.outcome,
      attempts: state.attempts,
      done: state.done
    }
  });
}

/* settleWrite — adopt the row the server returned. Fields the response did not
   carry keep the value they had; a response is not a statement that everything
   it omitted is now empty. */
function settleWrite(state, inquiry) {
  const base = state.snapshot || state;
  if (!inquiry || typeof inquiry !== "object") {
    // The write succeeded and we cannot show what it produced. Say so rather
    // than painting a state nobody sent.
    return Object.assign(idleFrom(base), { stale: true });
  }
  const status = inquiry.status === undefined ? base.status : inquiry.status;
  const outcome = inquiry.outcome === undefined ? base.outcome : inquiry.outcome;
  const attempts = inquiry.call_attempts === undefined || inquiry.call_attempts === null
    ? base.attempts
    : Number(inquiry.call_attempts);
  const done = !!inquiry.confirmed_at || pill(status, outcome).done;
  return {
    phase: "idle",
    status: status,
    outcome: outcome,
    attempts: attempts,
    done: done,
    pending: null,
    error: null,
    refused: null,
    snapshot: null,
    stale: false
  };
}

/* failWrite — put the row back exactly as it was and hang the failure off it.
   The restore is from the snapshot beginWrite took, not from re-reading the
   DOM, so a half-applied render cannot survive as the new truth. */
function failWrite(state, fail) {
  const base = state.snapshot || state;
  return Object.assign(idleFrom(base), { error: fail || null });
}

/* attemptsDelta — how far the Calls tile should move. Derived from the two
   counts rather than assumed to be +1, because the server recomputes the
   counter and a retry can legitimately produce no change at all. Unknown on
   either side means no movement: a tile must not drift on a guess. */
function attemptsDelta(before, after) {
  if (typeof before !== "number" || typeof after !== "number") return 0;
  if (!isFinite(before) || !isFinite(after)) return 0;
  return after - before;
}

/* ── THE ATTEMPT HISTORY ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   The work strip's log used to hold this session's clicks and nothing else, so
   it emptied on reload. listAttempts() serves the real dated trail — which is
   the thing migration 055 added the table for: "a counter cannot answer what
   happened on the second call, and a bureau dispute wants a dated trail".

   attemptLine renders ONLY what the query selected. An attempt with no outcome
   and no note is a kind and a date, and that is what it renders — the blank is
   the record, and filling it with "no outcome recorded" would put words into an
   append-only log of what a human did to a consumer's credit file. */
function attemptLine(attempt) {
  const a = attempt || {};
  const parts = [String(a.kind || "attempt")];
  // outcome first, note second: an outcome is what happened, a note is colour.
  const detail = blankToNull(a.outcome) || blankToNull(a.note);
  if (detail) parts.push(detail);
  const who = blankToNull(a.staff_name);
  if (who) parts.push(who);
  const when = formatWhen(a.created_at);
  if (when) parts.push(when);
  return parts.join(" · ");
}

/* formatWhen — a timestamp the desk can read, or null. A date that will not
   parse renders as nothing rather than as "Invalid Date". */
function formatWhen(ts) {
  if (!ts) return null;
  const d = new Date(ts);
  if (isNaN(d.getTime())) return null;
  return d.toLocaleString("en-US", { month: "short", day: "numeric", hour: "numeric", minute: "2-digit" });
}

function pendingLabel(action) {
  if (action === "attempt") return "logging attempt...";
  if (action === "confirm") return "confirming removal...";
  if (action === "status") return "saving status...";
  return "saving...";
}

/* ── CASE QUEUE (inquiry gate) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
   Expanding-row helpers for inquiry_removal_cases. Send is human-only. */

function caseUiStatus(row) {
  const r = row || {};
  const st = String(r.case_status || "");
  if (st === "Blocked") return { label: "Blocked (docs)", cls: "noanswer" };
  if (st === "Completed") return { label: "Complete", cls: "confirmed" };
  if (r.call_fired_at) return { label: "Awaiting Call", cls: "progress" };
  if (r.call_due_at || r.first_delivery_at || r.letter_provider_id || r.portal_confirmation) {
    return { label: "Sent", cls: "progress" };
  }
  if (st === "Queued" || st === "Scheduled") return { label: "Ready for Review", cls: "new" };
  if (st === "In Progress") return { label: "Sent", cls: "progress" };
  return { label: st || "Unknown", cls: "" };
}

function caseCallState(row, now) {
  const r = row || {};
  if (r.call_fired_at) return "done";
  if (!r.call_due_at) return "not due";
  const due = new Date(r.call_due_at).getTime();
  const t = (now || new Date()).getTime();
  if (Number.isFinite(due) && due <= t) return "due";
  return "not due";
}

function buildCaseSendRequest(opts) {
  const o = opts || {};
  if (!isUuid(o.caseId)) throw new ViewError("case id must be a uuid");
  const mail = o.mail === true;
  const portal = o.portal === true;
  if (!mail && !portal) throw new ViewError("select mail and/or portal");
  const body = { id: o.caseId, action: "send", mail: mail, portal: portal };
  if (portal) {
    const ref = blankToNull(o.portalConfirmation);
    if (ref === null) {
      throw new ViewError("Experian portal reference number is required");
    }
    body.portal_confirmation = ref;
    const uploaded = blankToNull(o.portalUploadedAt);
    if (uploaded !== null) body.portal_uploaded_at = uploaded;
  }
  const note = blankToNull(o.note);
  if (note !== null) body.note = note;
  const serviceLevel = blankToNull(o.mailServiceLevel || o.mail_service_level);
  if (serviceLevel !== null) body.mail_service_level = serviceLevel;
  return { method: "POST", path: "/api/inquiry-cases", body: body };
}

function buildInquiryGenerateRequest(opts) {
  const o = opts || {};
  if (!isUuid(o.caseId)) throw new ViewError("case id must be a uuid");
  return { method: "POST", path: "/api/inquiry-cases", body: { id: o.caseId, action: "generate" } };
}

/* ── REPAIR PANE ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Same desk, other toggle. Send is human-only. No letter without an id. */

const BUREAU_NAMES = Object.freeze({ EX: "Experian", EQ: "Equifax", TU: "TransUnion" });

/* ONE BUREAU, WRITTEN TWO WAYS, COUNTED AS TWO BUREAUS.

   inquiry_removal_cases.selected_bureaus_raw is called "raw" because it is: it
   carries whatever the source handed us. src/inquiry-ops/send.mjs copies it
   straight onto inquiry_log.bureau, and inquiry_log.bureau is plain `text` with
   no CHECK (db/schema/001_init.sql:173). Today's writers put the two-letter code
   there — EX / EQ / TU, per the ai_bureau_config seed in migration 155 — while
   rows that arrived from the old spreadsheet runtime hold the full name.

   The screen's three bureau chips compared against the full name only. Against
   code rows every chip read 0 and "none in queue" while the queue was full, and
   pressing one emptied the table under the words "all done for today". Against a
   MIX the counts would have been quietly short, which is worse than obviously
   zero.

   So nothing on this screen compares one bureau string to another. Both sides go
   through bureauKey first, and an unrecognised value keeps its own uppercase
   form rather than being folded into one of the three — an unknown bureau is its
   own thing, not a silent member of somebody else's count. */
const BUREAU_KEYS = Object.freeze({
  EX: "EX", EXPERIAN: "EX",
  EQ: "EQ", EQUIFAX: "EQ",
  TU: "TU", TRANSUNION: "TU", "TRANS UNION": "TU"
});

function bureauKey(raw) {
  const s = String(raw == null ? "" : raw).trim().toUpperCase();
  if (!s) return "";
  return BUREAU_KEYS[s] || s;
}

function bureauLabel(code) {
  const k = bureauKey(code);
  return BUREAU_NAMES[k] || k || "—";
}

/** countByBureau — the chip counts, keyed the one way the chips are keyed. */
function countByBureau(rows, pick) {
  const out = {};
  const list = Array.isArray(rows) ? rows : [];
  for (const row of list) {
    const key = bureauKey(typeof pick === "function" ? pick(row) : (row && row.bureau));
    if (!key) continue;
    out[key] = (out[key] || 0) + 1;
  }
  return out;
}

/* ── THE QUEUE YOU EMPTY ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Inquiry removal is an errand with an end: check the papers, read the draft,
   press Send. The only cases that need a PERSON are the ones nothing has been
   sent on yet. Everything else is in the mail, or the sweeper is phoning the
   bureau on its own clock, and neither of those is hers to move. A headline that
   counts them all is a number that does not go down when she works. */

function caseIsReadyToSend(row) {
  return caseUiStatus(row).label === "Ready for Review";
}

/* THE CASES THE HEADLINE DOES NOT COUNT, COUNTED SEPARATELY.
   "Ready to send" is the right number and it is honestly derived, but the
   sentence under it used to be "nothing is waiting on you" whenever that number
   was zero — including when every open case was Blocked or Escalated.

   Blocked is written by src/inquiry-ops/send.mjs when the identity packet is
   short: the send was REFUSED, nothing left the building, and the fix is a
   person chasing documents. It is not ready and it is not sent, so a screen that
   answers zero and says "go home" is the same untruth this desk was rebuilt to
   remove. Blocked is counted however far the case got, because caseUiStatus
   reads that status before it looks at any timestamp.

   WHAT THIS DOES NOT COUNT, deliberately: Escalated, and the `st || "Unknown"`
   fallback for a status nobody has taught this screen, are only counted while
   NOTHING HAS GONE OUT YET. caseUiStatus checks call_fired_at, then call_due_at
   / first_delivery_at / letter_provider_id / portal_confirmation, before it ever
   falls through to the raw status — so an Escalated case whose bureau call
   already fired reads "Awaiting Call", and one whose letter already landed reads
   "Sent". Both leave this count at zero. That is the intended answer: an
   Escalated case that HAS been sent is out of her hands, and
   inquiry-remover-view.test.mjs pins it. Do not read this as "Escalated is
   caught" — measured, an Escalated row with call_fired_at set returns 0 here.

   These four labels are the settled ones — counted by the headline, or out of
   her hands. */
const SETTLED_CASE_LABELS = new Set(["Ready for Review", "Sent", "Awaiting Call", "Complete"]);

function casesNeedingAPerson(rows) {
  const list = Array.isArray(rows) ? rows : [];
  return list.filter((row) => !SETTLED_CASE_LABELS.has(caseUiStatus(row).label));
}

/** Whole days since a timestamp, or null when there is no usable timestamp. */
function waitingDays(since, now) {
  if (!since) return null;
  const then = new Date(since).getTime();
  if (!Number.isFinite(then)) return null;
  const asOf = now instanceof Date ? now : (now ? new Date(now) : new Date());
  const n = asOf.getTime();
  if (!Number.isFinite(n)) return null;
  const days = Math.floor((n - then) / 86400000);
  return days < 0 ? 0 : days;
}

/** Words for waitingDays(). null renders as an em-dash — unknown, never zero. */
function waitingLabel(days) {
  if (days == null) return "—";
  if (days <= 0) return "today";
  return days + (days === 1 ? " day" : " days");
}

/* Oldest first, and the cases already out of her hands sink.

   api/read/inquiries.mjs orders by updated_at DESC and src/inquiry-ops/cases.mjs
   by requested_at DESC, so the row she just worked jumped to the top and the one
   nobody has touched sank out of sight — the exact opposite of a worklist. A
   case with no date sorts to the bottom of its own group rather than being given
   a date it does not have. */
function sortCasesOldestFirst(rows) {
  const list = Array.isArray(rows) ? rows.slice() : [];
  const age = (c) => {
    const v = c && (c.requested_at || c.created_at);
    const t = v ? new Date(v).getTime() : NaN;
    return Number.isFinite(t) ? t : Infinity;
  };
  const rank = (c) => (caseIsReadyToSend(c) ? 0 : 1);
  return list.sort((a, b) => (rank(a) - rank(b)) || (age(a) - age(b)));
}

/** The next action, said once: the oldest case that is waiting on a person. */
function nextInquiryAction(rows, opts) {
  const o = opts || {};
  const list = Array.isArray(rows) ? rows : [];
  let best = null;
  let bestAge = Infinity;
  for (const row of list) {
    if (!caseIsReadyToSend(row)) continue;
    const v = row && row.requested_at;
    const t = v ? new Date(v).getTime() : NaN;
    const age = Number.isFinite(t) ? t : Infinity;
    if (best === null || age < bestAge) { best = row; bestAge = age; }
  }
  if (!best) return null;
  const who = blankToNull(best.client_name) || blankToNull(best.client_email)
    || blankToNull(best.case_id) || "this case";
  const parts = [who];
  const bureau = bureauLabel(best.selected_bureaus_raw);
  if (bureau && bureau !== "—") parts.push(bureau);
  const days = waitingDays(best.requested_at, o.now);
  if (days != null) parts.push("waiting " + waitingLabel(days));
  return { caseId: best.id || null, text: "Send the oldest — " + parts.join(", ") };
}

/* THE DOC PACKET, WITHOUT INVENTING AN ANSWER.

   The screen used to print "complete" for every case that was not already
   Blocked, and Blocked is only ever set at send time (src/inquiry-ops/send.mjs
   :166-170). So a packet nobody had looked at read "complete" on the one screen
   whose whole job is deciding whether to press Send.

   There are three states here, not two, and the third is the honest word for
   "nobody has checked yet". */
function docsPacketLabel(row) {
  const r = row || {};
  if (r.docs_complete === true) return "complete";
  if (r.docs_complete === false) return "chasing";
  if (String(r.case_status || "") === "Blocked") return "chasing";
  return "not checked";
}

const DOC_WORDS = Object.freeze({
  id_document: "photo ID",
  proof_of_address: "proof of address",
  authorization: "signed authorization",
  ssn_card: "Social Security card"
});

/** Names what is missing, in plain words. "" when nothing is known to be. */
function docsMissingWords(missing) {
  const list = Array.isArray(missing) ? missing.filter(Boolean).map(String) : [];
  if (!list.length) return "";
  return list.map((m) => DOC_WORDS[m] || m.replace(/_/g, " ")).join(", ");
}

/* ── THE ONE NUMBER, TOP LEFT ────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Both panes fill one slot, and both say where the number came from.

   `total` is the reader's COUNT(*) over the whole caseload. When it is bigger
   than the page that was actually fetched, the line underneath says so, because
   a page count standing in for a caseload count is a headline that silently
   under-reports the day it matters. A missing total is unknown, not zero.

   AND IT SAYS WHAT IT DID NOT COUNT. The number is "ready to send" and Blocked
   and Escalated cases are not ready to send, so folding them in would be a lie
   in the other direction. What was wrong was the sentence underneath: with three
   blocked cases and nothing ready, this said "nothing is waiting on you" — a
   zero standing in for work the screen had decided not to count. It names them
   now, in both branches. */
function inquiryHeadline(rows, opts) {
  const o = opts || {};
  const list = Array.isArray(rows) ? rows : [];
  const ready = list.filter(caseIsReadyToSend);
  const waiting = casesNeedingAPerson(list).length;
  const waitingWords = waiting === 1
    ? "1 case needs a person before it can be sent"
    : waiting + " cases need a person before they can be sent";
  const total = Number(o.total);
  const capped = Number.isFinite(total) && total > list.length;
  let sub;
  if (!ready.length) {
    if (waiting) sub = waitingWords;
    else sub = list.length ? "nothing is waiting on you" : "no active cases";
  } else {
    let oldest = null;
    for (const row of ready) {
      const d = waitingDays(row.requested_at, o.now);
      if (d != null && (oldest === null || d > oldest)) oldest = d;
    }
    sub = oldest === null
      ? "oldest waiting — no request date on file"
      : "oldest waiting " + waitingLabel(oldest);
    if (waiting) sub += " · " + waitingWords;
  }
  if (capped) sub += " · counted over the first " + list.length + " of " + total;
  return { value: String(ready.length), label: "Ready to send", sub: sub };
}

function repairHeadline(payload) {
  const p = payload || {};
  const files = Array.isArray(p.files) ? p.files : [];
  const total = Number(p.total);
  const capped = Number.isFinite(total) && total > files.length;
  const open = Number.isFinite(total) ? total : files.length;
  return {
    value: p.need_me == null ? "—" : String(p.need_me),
    label: "Need me",
    sub: capped
      ? "counted over the first " + files.length + " of " + open + " open"
      : "of " + open + " open"
  };
}

/* The repair pane's next action: the first file the rows themselves say needs
   her. The caller passes in the chip label its own lens derived, so the sentence
   and the row can never disagree about which file is first. */
function nextRepairAction(files, needLabelOf) {
  const list = Array.isArray(files) ? files : [];
  if (typeof needLabelOf !== "function") return null;
  for (const f of list) {
    const need = blankToNull(needLabelOf(f));
    if (!need) continue;
    const who = blankToNull(f && f.name) || "this file";
    return { clientId: (f && f.client_id) || null, text: who + " — " + need };
  }
  return null;
}

/* The line under the repair headline when no row needs her. Built from the
   same tile counts the pane paints, so it cannot say every file is waiting on
   a bureau while the Waiting tile says 0 and the Stuck tile says 2. "Every
   file" is only said when the waiting count covers the whole open queue. */
function repairQuietLine(payload) {
  const p = payload || {};
  const stuck = Number(p.stalled);
  const waiting = Number(p.waiting);
  const total = Number(p.total);
  const open = Number.isFinite(total) ? total : (Array.isArray(p.files) ? p.files.length : 0);
  const parts = [];
  if (Number.isFinite(stuck) && stuck > 0) {
    parts.push(stuck + (stuck === 1 ? " file is stuck" : " files are stuck"));
  }
  if (Number.isFinite(waiting) && waiting > 0) {
    if (!parts.length && waiting === open) return "Nothing needs you — every file is waiting on a bureau.";
    parts.push(waiting + (waiting === 1 ? " file is" : " files are") + " waiting on a bureau");
  }
  if (!parts.length) return "Nothing needs you right now.";
  return "Nothing needs you — " + parts.join(", ") + ".";
}

function repairStagePill(stageKey) {
  const k = String(stageKey || "");
  if (k === "stalled") return { cls: "noanswer", text: "Stuck" };
  if (k === "ready_to_send" || k === "letters_generated") return { cls: "new", text: "Ready" };
  if (k === "program_complete") return { cls: "confirmed", text: "Done" };
  if (k === "in_transit" || k === "awaiting_response") return { cls: "progress", text: "Waiting" };
  if (k === "response_received") return { cls: "progress", text: "Answer in" };
  if (k === "cancelled") return { cls: "", text: "Cancelled" };
  return { cls: "", text: k ? k.replace(/_/g, " ") : "Unknown" };
}

function buildRepairSendRequest(opts) {
  const o = opts || {};
  requireClientId(o.clientId);
  if (o.mail !== true) throw new ViewError("mail required — a person has to press send");
  const letters = Array.isArray(o.letters) ? o.letters : [];
  if (!letters.length) throw new ViewError("no letters ready to send");
  const bodyLetters = [];
  for (const letter of letters) {
    if (!letter || !letter.bureau) throw new ViewError("each letter needs a bureau");
    const html = letter.html || letter.body_text || "";
    if (!html) throw new ViewError("a letter with no body cannot be mailed");
    const row = {
      bureau: String(letter.bureau).toUpperCase(),
      html: html
    };
    if (letter.id && isUuid(letter.id)) row.letter_id = letter.id;
    bodyLetters.push(row);
  }
  return {
    method: "POST",
    path: "/api/repair/send",
    body: {
      mail: true,
      client_id: o.clientId,
      letters: bodyLetters
    }
  };
}

function buildRepairConfirmParseRequest(opts) {
  const o = opts || {};
  if (!isUuid(o.responseId)) throw new ViewError("response id must be a uuid");
  return {
    method: "POST",
    path: "/api/repair/exceptions",
    body: { action: "confirm_parse", responseId: o.responseId }
  };
}

const VIEW = {
  ATTEMPT_KINDS: ATTEMPT_KINDS,
  COUNTING_KINDS: COUNTING_KINDS,
  ViewError: ViewError,
  isUuid: isUuid,
  blankToNull: blankToNull,
  pill: pill,
  buildAttemptRequest: buildAttemptRequest,
  buildConfirmRequest: buildConfirmRequest,
  buildStatusRequest: buildStatusRequest,
  buildExpectedRequest: buildExpectedRequest,
  buildAttemptsRequest: buildAttemptsRequest,
  buildIdentityRequest: buildIdentityRequest,
  buildRevealRequest: buildRevealRequest,
  describeFailure: describeFailure,
  interpretWrite: interpretWrite,
  interpretIdentity: interpretIdentity,
  interpretReveal: interpretReveal,
  maskedSsnLabel: maskedSsnLabel,
  canReveal: canReveal,
  formatRevealed: formatRevealed,
  createRowState: createRowState,
  beginWrite: beginWrite,
  settleWrite: settleWrite,
  failWrite: failWrite,
  attemptsDelta: attemptsDelta,
  attemptLine: attemptLine,
  formatWhen: formatWhen,
  interpretAttempts: interpretAttempts,
  pendingLabel: pendingLabel,
  caseUiStatus: caseUiStatus,
  caseCallState: caseCallState,
  buildCaseSendRequest: buildCaseSendRequest,
  buildInquiryGenerateRequest: buildInquiryGenerateRequest,
  bureauKey: bureauKey,
  bureauLabel: bureauLabel,
  countByBureau: countByBureau,
  caseIsReadyToSend: caseIsReadyToSend,
  casesNeedingAPerson: casesNeedingAPerson,
  waitingDays: waitingDays,
  waitingLabel: waitingLabel,
  sortCasesOldestFirst: sortCasesOldestFirst,
  nextInquiryAction: nextInquiryAction,
  docsPacketLabel: docsPacketLabel,
  docsMissingWords: docsMissingWords,
  inquiryHeadline: inquiryHeadline,

  buildRepairConfirmParseRequest: buildRepairConfirmParseRequest
};

return VIEW;
})();

<script defer src="data.js"></script>
<script>
/* ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   WIRING — replaces the sample queue with inquiry_log, then hands the rebuilt
   table to the screen's own init so every interaction binds to real rows.

   Runs BEFORE the behaviour block and publishes __fhQueueReady, which that
   block waits on. On any failure it resolves anyway and keeps the empty status
   row with a banner — rule: fall back, don't invent people.
   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
window.__fhQueueReady = (function () {
  /* data.js carries `defer` (see its tag above), so window.FHData does not exist
     yet while THIS script is being parsed. The guard used to sit here and read it,
     so the whole block quit before doing anything: the Work Queue kept its
     "Loading inquiry queue…" row forever, the four tiles kept their "—", and the
     three bureau chips kept their hardcoded 0. Every deferred script runs before
     DOMContentLoaded, so the first read waits for that event — the same pattern
     client-control-panel.html and messaging.html already use.

     __fhQueueReady is still ASSIGNED synchronously here, because the behaviour
     block further down tests for it while IT is being parsed. Only the READ moved. */
  var domReady = new Promise(function (resolve) {
    if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
      document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { resolve(); });
    } else {
      resolve();
    }
  });
  /* Three tables on this page carry class="queue" — #caseQueueTable, the Work
     Queue, and #repairTable — and querySelector returns the FIRST in document
     order, so every lookup here used to land on the cases table: rows were
     appended under the wrong header and #queue-status-row was never found to be
     removed. Ask for the one we mean. */
  function queueTable() { return document.getElementById('workQueueTable'); }
  var table = null;
  function showQueueStatus(msg) {
    var table = queueTable();
    if (!table) return;
    [].slice.call(table.querySelectorAll('tr[data-row], #queue-status-row')).forEach(function (r) { r.remove(); });
    var tr = document.createElement('tr');
    tr.id = 'queue-status-row';
    var td = document.createElement('td');
    td.colSpan = 7;
    td.style.cssText = 'text-align:center;padding:28px 16px;color:var(--text-dim)';
    td.textContent = msg;
    tr.appendChild(td);
    table.appendChild(tr);
  }
  function setStat(name, n) {
    var el = document.querySelector('[data-stat="' + name + '"]');
    if (el) el.textContent = String(n);
  }
  /* Both sides of every bureau comparison go through FHInquiryView.bureauKey.
     The chips used to carry data-bureau="Equifax" and the rows carry whatever
     inquiry_log.bureau holds, which today is the two-letter code — so the keys
     could never match, all three chips read 0 while thirty inquiries were open,
     and pressing one emptied the table under the words "all done for today". */
  function paintBureaus(byBureau) {
    byBureau = byBureau || {};
    var total = Object.keys(byBureau).reduce(function (sum, key) {
      return sum + Number(byBureau[key] || 0);
    }, 0);
    var bureauRow = document.getElementById('bureau-row');
    var emptyState = document.getElementById('no-open-inquiries');
    if (bureauRow) bureauRow.hidden = total === 0;
    if (emptyState) emptyState.hidden = total !== 0;
    [].slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('.bureau-chip[data-bureau]')).forEach(function (c) {
      var bc = c.querySelector('.bc');
      var bs = c.querySelector('.bs');
      var n = byBureau[VIEW.bureauKey(c.dataset.bureau)] || 0;
      c.classList.remove('blocked');
      if (bc) {
        bc.textContent = String(n);
        bc.classList.toggle('zero', n === 0);
        bc.classList.remove('blocked');
      }
      if (bs) bs.textContent = n === 0 ? 'none in queue' : (n + ' left');
    });
  }


  var VIEW = window.FHInquiryView;
  var pill = VIEW.pill;

  function cell(html) { var td = document.createElement('td'); td.innerHTML = html; return td; }
  function esc(v) {
    return String(v == null ? '' : v)
      .replace(/&/g, '&amp;').replace(/</g, '&lt;').replace(/>/g, '&gt;')
      .replace(/"/g, '&quot;');
  }
  function callStateLabel(s) {
    if (!s) return '—';
    return String(s).replace(/_/g, ' ');
  }
  function callStateClass(s) {
    if (s === 'holding') return 'holding';
    if (s === 'live_agent_reached') return 'live';
    if (s === 'transferred_to_rep') return 'transferred';
    return '';
  }

  return domReady.then(function () {
    table = queueTable();
    if (!table || !window.FHData) return;
    return runLoad();
  });

  function runLoad() {
  return FHData.inquiries({ limit: 200 }).then(function (res) {
    if (!res.ok) { showQueueStatus('Could not load the inquiry queue.'); FHData.explain(res, 'inquiry queue'); return; }
    var items = (res.data && res.data.items) || [];
    if (!items.length) {
      showQueueStatus('No inquiries in the database yet.');
      FHData.banner('sample', 'No inquiries in the database yet.', 'inquiries');
      setStat('left', 0);
      setStat('worked', 0);
      setStat('calls', 0);
      setStat('confirmed', 0);
      paintBureaus({});
      return;
    }

    /* The static "Loading inquiry queue…" row (#queue-status-row) is only cleared
       by showQueueStatus, which the success path never calls — so on a good load
       it used to sit above the real rows forever. Purge it here with them. */
    [].slice.call(table.querySelectorAll('tr[data-row], #queue-status-row'))
      .forEach(function (r) { r.remove(); });

    var unknown = 0, calls = 0, left = 0, confirmed = 0, worked = 0, byBureau = {};
    items.forEach(function (it) {
      var p = pill(it.status, it.outcome);
      if (!p.known) unknown++;
      calls += Number(it.call_attempts) || 0;
      if (p.done || Number(it.call_attempts) > 0) worked++;
      if (p.done) confirmed++; else {
        left++;
        var bkey = VIEW.bureauKey(it.bureau);
        if (bkey) byBureau[bkey] = (byBureau[bkey] || 0) + 1;
      }

      var tr = document.createElement('tr');
      tr.setAttribute('data-row', '');
      /* data-bureau holds the NORMALISED key, because it is what the chips,
         the filter and bumpChip() all compare against. The raw value is kept
         beside it so the cell can still show what the record actually says. */
      if (it.bureau) {
        tr.dataset.bureau = VIEW.bureauKey(it.bureau);
        tr.dataset.bureauRaw = it.bureau;
      }
      if (p.done) tr.dataset.done = '1';
      if (it.id) tr.dataset.id = it.id;
      if (it.client_id) tr.dataset.clientId = it.client_id;
      if (it.case_id) tr.dataset.caseId = it.case_id;
      tr._row = { status: it.status, outcome: it.outcome, call_attempts: it.call_attempts, expected_name: it.expected_name || "" };
      tr.tabIndex = 0;
      tr.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
      tr.appendChild(cell('<span class="rowchev">&#9656;</span>' +
        esc(it.client_name || '(unnamed client)')));
      tr.appendChild(cell(esc(VIEW.bureauLabel(it.bureau))));
      tr.appendChild(cell(esc(it.inquiry_name || it.inquiry || '—')));
      tr.appendChild(cell(esc(it.expected_name || '—')));
      tr.appendChild(cell('<span class="call-state ' + callStateClass(it.call_state) + '">' +
        esc(callStateLabel(it.call_state)) + '</span>'));
      var holdCell = '—';
      if (it.call_state === 'holding') holdCell = '<span class="hold-time">live</span>';
      tr.appendChild(cell(holdCell));
      var att = cell(esc(it.call_attempts == null ? 0 : it.call_attempts));
      att.className = 'mono';
      tr.appendChild(att);
      tr.appendChild(cell('<span class="status-pill ' + p.cls + '">' + esc(p.text) + '</span>'));
      table.appendChild(tr);
    });

    setStat('left', left);
    setStat('worked', worked);
    setStat('calls', calls);
    setStat('confirmed', confirmed);
    paintBureaus(byBureau);

    FHData.banner('real', 'live queue · ' + items.length + ' inquiries · ' +
      left + ' open' +
      (unknown ? ' · ' + unknown + ' with an unmapped status' : ''), 'inquiries');
  }).catch(function () {
    FHData.banner('error', 'sample queue — the inquiry read failed', 'inquiries');
  });
  }
})();
</script>

<script>
/* ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Inquiry Remover — queue behaviour. The filtering and expand/collapse below
   are UNCHANGED from the wireframe: they read the table out of the DOM at init
   and bind every interaction to whatever rows they find. That is why the wiring
   block above rewrites the rows FIRST and then calls this — real rows get the
   same behaviour the sample rows had.

   WHAT CHANGED: the work strip now WRITES. "Log an attempt", "Mark confirmed"
   and "Set status" POST to /api/inquiries (src/inquiries/work.mjs), and the
   identity line reads and reveals through /api/pii (src/pii/index.mjs). HANDOFF
   still says there is no write endpoint for inquiry_log; that stopped being
   true at migration 055.

   THERE IS NO OPTIMISTIC UI ON THIS SCREEN, DELIBERATELY. A click arms a
   pending state and changes NOTHING the row claims. Only the row the server
   sends back moves a status, an attempt count or a tile, and a failure puts the
   row back exactly as it was and says why. A credit-report action that appears
   to have happened and did not is the worst thing this page could do to
   somebody, and it costs one round trip to never do it.

   The decisions — what a request body looks like, when a row may read as
   Removed, what a failure means — are all in FHInquiryView above, which is a
   copy of a module with tests. What is left here is DOM plumbing.
   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
window.__fhInitQueue = function(){
  var V      = window.FHInquiryView,
      table  = document.getElementById('workQueueTable'),
      rows   = [].slice.call(table.querySelectorAll('tr[data-row]')),
      chips  = [].slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('.bureau-chip[data-bureau]')),
      note   = document.getElementById('filter-note'),
      filter = null;

  /* ── WHICH CELL IS WHICH ───────────────────────────────────────────────
     The Work Queue header declares eight columns, in this order:

       0 Client · 1 Bureau · 2 Actual · 3 Expected
       4 Call State · 5 Hold · 6 Attempts · 7 Status

     and the wiring block above appends exactly those eight, in that order.
     These two constants were 3 and 4, left over from a five-column table
     that no longer exists — so every write put the attempt count in the
     EXPECTED column and the status pill in CALL STATE, while the real
     Attempts and Status columns never moved at all. Press "Mark confirmed"
     and the row read "Removed" under Call State with Status still open:
     precisely the credit-report action that appears to have happened and
     did not, which the header of the next block says is the worst thing
     this page can do to somebody.

     Named rather than inlined so the two places that index a row cannot
     drift apart again, and pinned against the header itself by
     src/http/inquiry-remover-view.test.mjs. */
  var COL_ATTEMPTS = 6, COL_STATUS = 7;

  function esc(v){
    return String(v == null ? '' : v)
      .replace(/&/g,'&amp;').replace(/</g,'&lt;').replace(/>/g,'&gt;').replace(/"/g,'&quot;');
  }

  /* A demo session must not write, for the same reason data.js will not read on
     one: the sentinel token is not a credential and presenting it as one gets a
     401 that reads like a real session expiry. */
  function isDemo(){
    try { return localStorage.getItem('fh_demo') === '1'; } catch(e){ return false; }
  }

  /* send — one request, and it NEVER rejects. Callers branch on the shape
     FHInquiryView.interpret*() expects: {transport:true,detail} for "no answer
     at all", {status,body} for an answer. A screen-level .catch that forgot a
     case is how a failed write becomes a silent one. */
  function send(spec){
    var headers = { accept: 'application/json' };
    var init = { method: spec.method, headers: headers };
    if (spec.body){ headers['content-type'] = 'application/json'; init.body = JSON.stringify(spec.body); }
    var t = ''; try { t = localStorage.getItem('fh_token') || ''; } catch(e){}
    if (t) headers.authorization = 'Bearer ' + t;
    var started;
    try { started = fetch(spec.path, init); }
    catch (e) { return Promise.resolve({ transport:true, detail:(e && e.message) || 'fetch unavailable' }); }
    return Promise.resolve(started).then(function(r){
      return r.json().then(
        function(b){ return { status:r.status, body:b }; },
        function(){ return { status:r.status, body:null }; }
      );
    }, function(e){
      return Promise.resolve({ transport:true, detail:(e && e.message) || 'network error' });
    });
  }

  /* Two banner keys, so a failed write cannot hide behind a successful read and
     the identity line cannot overwrite the queue's own line. FHData.banner
     keeps each part and shows the worst tone across all of them. */
  function banner(tone, text, key){
    if (window.FHData) FHData.banner(tone, text, key || 'inquiry writes');
  }

  function clock(){
    return new Date().toLocaleTimeString('en-US',{hour:'numeric',minute:'2-digit',timeZone:'America/Phoenix'});
  }
  function stat(name){ return document.querySelector('[data-stat="'+name+'"]'); }
  function bump(name, delta){
    var el = stat(name); if(!el) return;
    el.textContent = String(Math.max(0, parseInt(el.textContent,10) + delta));
    el.classList.add('bumped');
    setTimeout(function(){ el.classList.remove('bumped'); }, 600);
  }
  function chipFor(bureau){ return chips.filter(function(c){ return c.dataset.bureau===bureau; })[0]; }
  function bumpChip(bureau, delta){
    var c = chipFor(bureau); if(!c) return;
    var bc = c.querySelector('.bc'), n = Math.max(0, parseInt(bc.textContent,10) + delta);
    bc.textContent = String(n);
    bc.classList.toggle('zero', n === 0);
  }

  /* ── FILTER BY BUREAU ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  var emptyRow = null;
  function applyFilter(){
    var shown = 0;
    rows.forEach(function(r){
      var hit = !filter || r.dataset.bureau === filter;
      r.hidden = !hit;
      if(hit) shown++;
      /* a hidden row must not leave its expanded strip behind */
      if(!hit) collapse(r);
    });
    chips.forEach(function(c){
      c.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(c.dataset.bureau === filter));
    });
    note.textContent = filter
      ? 'filtered · ' + V.bureauLabel(filter) + ' · ' + shown + ' of ' + rows.length + ' rows'
      : '';
    if(emptyRow){ emptyRow.remove(); emptyRow = null; }
    if(shown === 0){
      emptyRow = document.createElement('tr');
      emptyRow.className = 'queue-empty';
      var td = document.createElement('td');
      td.colSpan = 8;
      /* reuse the chip's own wording rather than inventing new copy */
      td.textContent = 'all done for today';
      emptyRow.appendChild(td);
      table.appendChild(emptyRow);
    }
  }
  chips.forEach(function(c){
    c.addEventListener('click', function(){
      filter = (filter === c.dataset.bureau) ? null : c.dataset.bureau;
      applyFilter();
    });
  });

  /* ── EXPAND A ROW INTO ITS WORK STRIP ─────────────────────────────────── */
  function collapse(r){
    r.setAttribute('aria-expanded','false');
    if(r._strip){ r._strip.remove(); r._strip = null; }
  }

  function logLine(r, txt, cls){
    var log = r._strip.querySelector('.worklog'),
        line = document.createElement('div');
    if(cls) line.className = cls;
    line.textContent = txt;
    log.insertBefore(line, log.firstChild);
  }

  /* rowState — one state object per row, kept ON the row so it survives a
     collapse. Seeded from the raw database row the wiring block stashed, and
     only from the DOM when there was none (the sample markup). */
  function rowState(r){
    if (r._state) return r._state;
    var raw = r._row;
    if (!raw){
      var txt = r.cells[COL_ATTEMPTS].textContent.trim();
      raw = {
        status: r.cells[COL_STATUS].textContent.trim(),
        call_attempts: /^\d+$/.test(txt) ? Number(txt) : null,
        confirmed_at: r.dataset.done === '1' ? true : null
      };
    }
    r._state = V.createRowState(raw);
    return r._state;
  }

  function expand(r){
    var locked = r.dataset.locked,
        bureau = r.dataset.bureau,
        attemptsCell = r.cells[COL_ATTEMPTS],
        statusCell   = r.cells[COL_STATUS],
        inquiryId    = r.dataset.id || null,
        clientId     = r.dataset.clientId || null,
        /* "live" means this row exists in the database. Sample markup has no
           data-id, and a POST at an invented uuid is worse than a disabled
           button that says why. */
        live         = V.isUuid(inquiryId);

    rowState(r);

    var tr = document.createElement('tr');
    tr.className = 'workrow';
    var td = document.createElement('td');
    td.colSpan = 8;

    var strip = document.createElement('div');
    strip.className = 'workstrip';

    /* The four kinds are the four the CHECK constraint in migration 055 allows,
       read from the module rather than typed out again here — a fifth option
       would be a constraint violation at the end of a click. */
    var kind = document.createElement('select');
    kind.className = 'qbtn';
    kind.title = 'What to log: call, letter, portal or note. A note does not count as an attempt.';
    /* aria-label rather than a visible <label>: the strip is a single row of
       controls in the approved design and a label element would add a line to
       it. A control with no accessible name at all is not an option. */
    kind.setAttribute('aria-label', 'attempt kind');
    V.ATTEMPT_KINDS.forEach(function(k){
      var o = document.createElement('option');
      o.value = k; o.textContent = k;
      kind.appendChild(o);
    });

    var call = document.createElement('button');
    call.type = 'button'; call.className = 'qbtn';
    call.textContent = 'Log an attempt';

    var conf = document.createElement('button');
    conf.type = 'button'; conf.className = 'qbtn primary';
    conf.textContent = 'Mark confirmed';

    /* Free text, because inquiry_log.status IS free text — 055 declined to add
       an enum on the grounds that the status vocabulary is a business decision.
       A dropdown here would invent that vocabulary in the least visible place. */
    var statusIn = document.createElement('input');
    statusIn.type = 'text'; statusIn.className = 'qbtn qinput';
    statusIn.placeholder = 'new status';
    statusIn.title = 'inquiry_log.status is free text — type what the desk actually uses.';
    statusIn.setAttribute('aria-label', 'new status for this inquiry');

    var setSt = document.createElement('button');
    setSt.type = 'button'; setSt.className = 'qbtn';
    setSt.textContent = 'Set status';

    var expectedIn = document.createElement('input');
    expectedIn.type = 'text'; expectedIn.className = 'qbtn qinput';
    expectedIn.placeholder = 'expected name';
    expectedIn.title = 'Name you expected to see. Actual stays the bureau string.';
    expectedIn.setAttribute('aria-label', 'expected creditor name');
    if (r._row && r._row.expected_name) expectedIn.value = r._row.expected_name;

    var saveExpected = document.createElement('button');
    saveExpected.type = 'button'; saveExpected.className = 'qbtn';
    saveExpected.textContent = 'Save expected';

    var log = document.createElement('div');
    log.className = 'worklog';

    strip.appendChild(kind); strip.appendChild(call); strip.appendChild(conf);
    strip.appendChild(statusIn); strip.appendChild(setSt);
    strip.appendChild(expectedIn); strip.appendChild(saveExpected); strip.appendChild(log);

    /* ── the identity line ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
       Masked by default and never fetched for a row that is not in the
       database. api/pii.mjs gates on IDENTITY_ROLES — owner, admin, inquiry
       specialist, funding advisor — because disputing an inquiry with a bureau
       means identifying the consumer, and a setter or a closer has no such
       need. A 403 here is a role answer, not an outage. */
    var pii = document.createElement('div');
    pii.className = 'workstrip';

    var ssnEl = document.createElement('span');
    ssnEl.className = 'pii-ssn';
    ssnEl.textContent = 'SSN —';

    var reasonIn = document.createElement('input');
    reasonIn.type = 'text'; reasonIn.className = 'qbtn qinput';
    reasonIn.placeholder = 'reason for reveal';
    reasonIn.setAttribute('aria-label', 'reason for revealing this SSN — written to the access log');

    var reveal = document.createElement('button');
    reveal.type = 'button'; reveal.className = 'qbtn';
    reveal.textContent = 'Reveal SSN';
    reveal.disabled = true;

    /* Said BEFORE the click, in one line, because an audit trail the user does
       not know about is a dark pattern. */
    var pnote = document.createElement('span');
    pnote.className = 'pii-note';
    pnote.textContent = 'Revealing writes your name and this reason to the access log.';

    pii.appendChild(ssnEl); pii.appendChild(reasonIn); pii.appendChild(reveal); pii.appendChild(pnote);

    td.appendChild(strip); td.appendChild(pii); tr.appendChild(td);
    r.parentNode.insertBefore(tr, r.nextSibling);
    r._strip = tr;
    r.setAttribute('aria-expanded','true');

    /* ── rendering ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
       syncButtons runs on every state change. paintRow runs ONLY after a write
       has been armed or answered, so opening a row and closing it again leaves
       the Attempts and Status cells exactly as the wiring block painted them.

       (This used to say the cell held a "2d 14h" stuck age. It does not: that
       column, and the sample rows that carried it, were deleted when the table
       went to eight columns. The sentence outlived the markup and pointed the
       next reader at the wrong two cells.) */
    function syncButtons(){
      var s = r._state, busy = s.phase === 'pending', off = busy || !live || !!locked;
      kind.disabled = call.disabled = off;
      statusIn.disabled = setSt.disabled = off;
      conf.disabled = off || s.done;
      if (s.done && !off) conf.title = 'Already confirmed and removed.';
    }

    function paintRow(){
      var s = r._state, p = V.pill(s.status, s.outcome);
      attemptsCell.textContent = s.attempts === null ? '—' : String(s.attempts);
      statusCell.innerHTML =
        '<span class="status-pill ' + p.cls + '">' + esc(p.text) + '</span>' +
        (s.phase === 'pending'
          ? ' <span class="status-pending">' + esc(V.pendingLabel(s.pending)) + '</span>'
          : '');
      if (s.done){ r.dataset.done = '1'; r.classList.remove('stuck'); }
      else { delete r.dataset.done; }
      syncButtons();
    }

    /* The strip can be gone by the time a response lands — the user is allowed
       to collapse a row mid-write. The row cells still update; the log line is
       simply dropped. */
    function note_(txt, cls){ if (r._strip) logLine(r, txt, cls); }

    var LABEL = { attempt: 'attempt logged', confirm: 'confirmed removed', status: 'status saved' };

    /* run — arm, send, settle or restore. The whole no-optimistic-UI rule is
       these twenty lines: beginWrite touches nothing the row claims, and only
       out.inquiry (the row Postgres returned) is allowed to change it. */
    function run(action, build){
      /* The double-submit guard is the module's, not a second one written here:
         two attempt POSTs for one human click is a double-count on a dispute
         record, and that rule has a test. */
      var armed = V.beginWrite(r._state, action);
      if (armed.refused) return;

      var spec;
      try { spec = build(); }
      catch (e){ note_(LABEL[action] + ' NOT SENT · ' + e.message, 'wl-fail'); return; }

      if (isDemo()){
        note_(LABEL[action] + ' NOT SENT · demo session — nothing is written', 'wl-fail');
        return;
      }

      r._state = armed;
      paintRow();
      note_(V.pendingLabel(action), 'wl-pend');

      send(spec).then(function(res){
        var before = r._state.snapshot || r._state;
        var wasAttempts = before.attempts, wasDone = before.done;
        var out = V.interpretWrite(res);

        if (!out.ok){
          r._state = V.failWrite(r._state, out.failure);
          paintRow();
          note_(LABEL[action] + ' FAILED · ' + out.failure.text, 'wl-fail');
          banner('error', 'inquiry write failed — ' + out.failure.text);
          return;
        }

        r._state = V.settleWrite(r._state, out.inquiry);
        paintRow();

        /* Tiles move by the difference between two server-known counts, not by
           a hardcoded +1: work.mjs RECOMPUTES call_attempts from the attempt
           log inside the write transaction, so a retry can legitimately leave
           it unchanged. */
        var d = V.attemptsDelta(wasAttempts, r._state.attempts);
        if (d) bump('calls', d);
        if (r._state.done && !wasDone){
          bump('confirmed', 1); bump('worked', 1); bump('left', -1);
          bumpChip(bureau, -1);
        } else if (!r._state.done && wasDone){
          bump('confirmed', -1); bump('left', 1);
          bumpChip(bureau, 1);
        }

        note_(LABEL[action] + ' · ' + clock() +
          (r._state.stale ? ' (saved — the server sent no row, reload to see it)' : ''));
        banner('real', 'inquiry writes are saving to the database');
      });
    }

    call.addEventListener('click', function(){
      run('attempt', function(){
        return V.buildAttemptRequest({ inquiryId: inquiryId, kind: kind.value });
      });
    });
    conf.addEventListener('click', function(){
      /* No status argument: confirmRemoval's own default is "Removed", chosen
         there to match wording already in the live data. */
      run('confirm', function(){ return V.buildConfirmRequest({ inquiryId: inquiryId }); });
    });
    setSt.addEventListener('click', function(){
      run('status', function(){
        return V.buildStatusRequest({ inquiryId: inquiryId, status: statusIn.value });
      });
    });
    saveExpected.addEventListener('click', function(){
      run('expected', function(){
        return V.buildExpectedRequest({ inquiryId: inquiryId, expectedName: expectedIn.value });
      });
    });

    /* ── identity ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
       maskedText holds the MASKED label only. The revealed number is written
       straight into the DOM from inside the response callback and is never
       assigned to anything that outlives it, so hiding and re-revealing makes a
       fresh request — and a fresh, correct, log entry. */
    var maskedText = 'SSN —', identityReady = false;

    /* Reveal stays disabled until there is something to reveal AND a reason to
       put in the log. Once revealed the button is the Hide control, so it is
       enabled regardless of what the reason box now says. */
    function syncReveal(){
      if (reveal.dataset.shown === '1'){ reveal.disabled = false; return; }
      reveal.disabled = !identityReady || !reasonIn.value.trim();
    }
    reasonIn.addEventListener('input', syncReveal);

    function noIdentity(text){
      ssnEl.textContent = text;
      maskedText = text;
      identityReady = false;
      reasonIn.disabled = true;
      syncReveal();
    }

    function loadIdentity(){
      if (locked){ noIdentity('SSN not read — this file is frozen'); pnote.textContent = locked; return; }
      if (!live || !V.isUuid(clientId)){ noIdentity('SSN — sample row, no client on file'); pnote.textContent = ''; return; }
      if (isDemo()){ noIdentity('SSN — demo session, identity not read'); pnote.textContent = ''; return; }

      ssnEl.textContent = 'SSN — checking';
      send(V.buildIdentityRequest({ clientId: clientId })).then(function(res){
        var out = V.interpretIdentity(res);
        if (!out.ok){
          noIdentity(out.failure.code === 'forbidden' ? 'SSN — hidden from your role' : 'SSN — unavailable');
          pnote.textContent = out.failure.text;
          return;
        }
        var m = V.maskedSsnLabel(out.identity);
        ssnEl.textContent = m.text;
        maskedText = m.text;
        identityReady = V.canReveal(out.identity) && !m.degraded;
        reasonIn.disabled = !identityReady;
        if (!identityReady) pnote.textContent = m.degraded
          ? 'the stored number could not be opened — a key is missing or wrong'
          : '';
        syncReveal();
      });
    }

    reveal.addEventListener('click', function(){
      if (reveal.dataset.shown === '1'){
        ssnEl.textContent = maskedText;
        reveal.textContent = 'Reveal SSN';
        reveal.dataset.shown = '';
        pnote.textContent = 'Revealing writes your name and this reason to the access log.';
        syncReveal();
        return;
      }
      var spec;
      try { spec = V.buildRevealRequest({ clientId: clientId, reason: reasonIn.value }); }
      catch (e){ pnote.textContent = e.message; return; }

      reveal.disabled = true; reveal.textContent = 'revealing...';
      send(spec).then(function(res){
        reveal.textContent = 'Reveal SSN';
        var out = V.interpretReveal(res);
        if (!out.ok){
          pnote.textContent = out.failure.text;
          banner('error', 'identity — ' + out.failure.text, 'identity');
          syncReveal();
          return;
        }
        ssnEl.textContent = V.formatRevealed(out.ssn);
        reveal.textContent = 'Hide';
        reveal.dataset.shown = '1';
        reveal.disabled = false;
        pnote.textContent = 'recorded in the access log · ' + clock();
      });
    });

    if (locked){
      kind.disabled = call.disabled = conf.disabled = true;
      statusIn.disabled = setSt.disabled = true;
      kind.title = call.title = conf.title = statusIn.title = setSt.title = locked;
      logLine(r, locked, 'wl-lock');
      loadIdentity();
      return;
    }

    /* ── the real attempt history ──────────────────────────────────────────
       The log used to hold this session's clicks and empty on reload. 055 added
       inquiry_attempts precisely so a dated trail exists; listAttempts serves
       it. Oldest first into logLine, which inserts at the top, so the newest
       ends up on top and this session's lines land above the history. */
    function loadHistory(){
      if (!live || isDemo()) return;
      send(V.buildAttemptsRequest({ inquiryId: inquiryId })).then(function(res){
        if (!r._strip) return;
        var out = V.interpretAttempts(res);
        if (!out.ok){ logLine(r, 'history unavailable · ' + out.failure.text, 'wl-fail'); return; }
        if (!out.attempts.length){ logLine(r, 'no attempts logged yet', 'wl-pend'); return; }
        out.attempts.slice().reverse().forEach(function(a){ logLine(r, V.attemptLine(a)); });
      });
    }

    syncButtons();
    if (!live){
      logLine(r, 'sample row — not in the database, nothing here will save', 'wl-lock');
    }
    loadHistory();
    loadIdentity();
  }

  rows.forEach(function(r){
    function toggle(){
      if(r.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true') collapse(r); else expand(r);
    }
    r.addEventListener('click', toggle);
    r.addEventListener('keydown', function(e){
      if(e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' '){ e.preventDefault(); toggle(); }
    });
  });
};

/* Hand off to the wiring block if it is still fetching; otherwise start now, so
   the screen still works with the script above removed. */
if (window.__fhQueueReady && typeof window.__fhQueueReady.then === 'function') {
  window.__fhQueueReady.then(window.__fhInitQueue, window.__fhInitQueue);
} else {
  window.__fhInitQueue();
}

/* ── THE HEADLINE SLOT ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   UI-STANDARDS §12 rules 1 and 2: one number top-left, and the next action said
   once directly under it. There is one slot and two desks, so each pane hands
   its answer in here and the toggle decides which one is showing. A pane that
   has not loaded yet, or whose read failed, puts an em-dash in — never a zero.
   NULL means unknown and unknown must survive all the way to the screen. */
window.FHDeskHead = (function () {
  var store = {};
  var active = "inquiries";
  function paint() {
    var s = store[active] || {};
    var head = s.head || {};
    var l = document.getElementById("deskLabel");
    var v = document.getElementById("deskValue");
    var sub = document.getElementById("deskSub");
    var btn = document.getElementById("deskNext");
    var none = document.getElementById("deskNextNone");
    if (l) l.textContent = head.label || "—";
    if (v) v.textContent = head.value == null ? "—" : head.value;
    if (sub) sub.textContent = head.sub || "";
    if (!btn || !none) return;
    if (s.action && s.action.text) {
      btn.textContent = s.action.text;
      btn.hidden = false;
      /* onclick, not addEventListener: this button is reused every reload, so
         assignment REPLACES the previous handler instead of stacking one. */
      btn.onclick = s.action.onClick || null;
      none.hidden = true;
    } else {
      btn.hidden = true;
      btn.onclick = null;
      none.hidden = false;
      none.textContent = s.quiet || "";
    }
  }
  return {
    put: function (pane, head, action, quiet) {
      store[pane] = { head: head, action: action, quiet: quiet };
      if (pane === active) paint();
    },
    show: function (pane) { active = pane; paint(); }
  };
})();

/* Inquiry removal case queue — expanding rows on this same page (no new route). */
(function loadCaseQueue() {
  var EXPANDED = null;
  function token() {
    try { return localStorage.getItem("fh_token") || ""; } catch (e) { return ""; }
  }
  function headers(json) {
    var h = { accept: "application/json" };
    var t = token();
    if (t) h.authorization = "Bearer " + t;
    if (json) h["content-type"] = "application/json";
    return h;
  }
  function esc(s) {
    return String(s == null ? "" : s)
      .replace(/&/g,"&amp;").replace(/</g,"&lt;").replace(/>/g,"&gt;");
  }
  function uiStatus(C) {
    if (window.FHInquiryView && window.FHInquiryView.caseUiStatus) return window.FHInquiryView.caseUiStatus(C);
    return { label: C.case_status || "—", cls: "" };
  }
  function callState(C) {
    if (window.FHInquiryView && window.FHInquiryView.caseCallState) return window.FHInquiryView.caseCallState(C);
    return "—";
  }
  function deliveryChips(C) {
    var mail = C.letter_provider_id
      ? (C.first_delivery_channel === "mail" || C.first_delivery_at ? "delivered" : "sent")
      : "empty";
    var portal = C.portal_confirmation
      ? (C.first_delivery_channel === "portal" || C.first_delivery_at ? "delivered" : "sent")
      : "empty";
    function chip(label, state) {
      var cls = state === "delivered" ? "chip done" : state === "sent" ? "chip on" : "chip";
      return '<span class="' + cls + '">' + label + (state === "empty" ? "" : " · " + state) + "</span>";
    }
    var bureau = window.FHInquiryView.bureauKey(C.selected_bureaus_raw);
    var html = chip("Letter", mail);
    if (bureau === "EX") html += chip("Portal", portal);
    return html;
  }
  /* docsLabel used to return "complete" for every case that was not already
     Blocked — and Blocked is only ever set at send time, so a packet nobody had
     looked at read "complete" on the screen that decides whether to send. The
     real answer now rides in on the case row (api/read/inquiry-cases.mjs asks
     src/inquiry-ops/doc-gate.mjs for it); the third state, "not checked", is
     what an unread or failed packet honestly says. */
  function docsLabel(C) {
    return window.FHInquiryView.docsPacketLabel(C);
  }
  /* ── WHAT DISABLES SEND IS THE PACKET, NOT LAST WEEK'S STATUS ────────────
     This used to read `C.case_status === "Blocked"` and nothing else, and
     Blocked was a one-way door: it is written when a send is refused for short
     paperwork, and until 2026-09-06 nothing in the send path ever wrote it back
     down. An agent watched the "still needed" list fall from three items to one
     as the client uploaded, and Send stayed grey the whole time. It would have
     stayed grey forever.

     The packet answer rides in on the case row now (api/read/inquiry-cases.mjs
     asks src/inquiry-ops/doc-gate.mjs, which since today also counts a
     signature filed as a consent rather than as a document — that is where the
     walkthrough client's dispute authorization actually lives). Three states,
     and the third is not "no":

       docs_complete === false  → papers really are short. Send is off, and the
                                  screen names WHICH papers.
       docs_complete === true   → send is on, even on a case still marked
                                  Blocked. Pressing it clears the block, which
                                  src/inquiry-ops/send.mjs now does.
       undefined                → nobody could check. Send stays available and
                                  the server gate decides; a screen that refuses
                                  on "we could not look" is guessing.

     A case with no bureau on it is a separate, harder no: there is no address
     to send to. It is off regardless of paperwork. */
  function sendBlock(C) {
    var noBureau = !window.FHInquiryView.bureauKey(C.selected_bureaus_raw);
    var packetShort = C.docs_complete === false;
    var missingWords = window.FHInquiryView.docsMissingWords(C.docs_missing);
    var note = "";
    if (noBureau) {
      note = '<p style="font-size:var(--fs-body);color:var(--red)">'
        + 'Send is off — this case has no credit bureau on it, so there is nowhere to send it. '
        + 'Set the bureau on the case first.</p>';
    } else if (packetShort) {
      note = '<p style="font-size:var(--fs-body);color:var(--red)">'
        + 'Send is off — this client still needs to send us '
        + (missingWords || 'part of their identity packet') + '.</p>';
    } else if (C.case_status === "Blocked") {
      /* Words, not colour. shell.js paintBrand() repaints --warn off the
         tenant's ramp, so a one-hue brand paints every state the same
         (docs/rules/UI-STANDARDS.md §12.6). The sentence has to carry it alone. */
      note = '<p style="font-size:var(--fs-body);color:var(--text-dim)">'
        + 'This case was blocked earlier for missing paperwork. Everything needed is on file now, '
        + 'so pressing Send will clear the block.</p>';
    } else if (C.docs_complete !== true) {
      note = '<p style="font-size:var(--fs-body);color:var(--text-dim)">'
        + 'The identity packet has not been checked. Send will check it before anything leaves.</p>';
    }
    return { off: noBureau || packetShort, note: note };
  }

  function detailHtml(C) {
    var bureau = window.FHInquiryView.bureauKey(C.selected_bureaus_raw);
    var send = sendBlock(C);
    var blocked = send.off;
    var missingWords = window.FHInquiryView.docsMissingWords(C.docs_missing);
    var letter = C.letter_draft_html || "<p><em>No draft letter yet.</em></p>";
    var portalBlock = bureau === "EX"
      ? '<label style="display:block;font-size:var(--fs-body);margin:8px 0 4px">Experian portal reference (required if uploading)</label>' +
        '<input type="text" class="portal-ref" placeholder="Reference from Experian confirmation" style="width:100%;padding:6px 8px;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:6px">' +
        '<label style="display:flex;gap:6px;align-items:center;margin-top:8px;font-size:var(--fs-body)">' +
        '<input type="checkbox" class="want-portal"> Upload to Experian portal</label>' +
        '<a class="qbtn" style="display:inline-block;margin-top:6px;text-decoration:none" target="_blank" rel="noopener" href="https://www.experian.com/consumer/upload/">Open Experian upload ↗</a>'
      : '<p style="font-size:var(--fs-body);color:var(--text-dim)">Portal upload is Experian-only. Mail only for this bureau.</p>';
    return (
      '<div class="case-expand" data-case-id="' + esc(C.id) + '">' +
        '<div class="case-col">' +
          '<h4>Disputable items</h4>' +
          '<div class="cd-meta">Open count: ' + esc(C.open_inquiry_count || 0) +
            (C.funding_round_id ? ' · Round <span class="mono">' + esc(String(C.funding_round_id).slice(0, 8)) + '</span>' : '') +
          '</div>' +
