<script>
  (function () {
    "use strict";

    var BOOK = "https://apply.fundhub.ai/schedule/phonecall";

    var intake = document.getElementById("intake");
    var err = document.getElementById("err");
    var book = document.getElementById("book");
    var again = document.getElementById("again");

    /* Whatever they already typed on /optimize. remember() there writes this, so
       a person arriving from the sign-up does not type their name twice. Private
       mode throws on read — an empty form is the correct fallback, never a crash. */
    (function prefill() {
      try {
        var saved = JSON.parse(sessionStorage.getItem("fh_opt") || "{}");
        if (saved.first_name) document.getElementById("first").value = saved.first_name;
        if (saved.last_name) document.getElementById("last").value = saved.last_name;
        if (saved.email) document.getElementById("email").value = saved.email;
      } catch (e) { /* nothing saved, or storage is off */ }
    })();

    /* The booking address comes from the server, same as on /optimize. */
    fetch("/api/public/optimize", { headers: { accept: "application/json" } })
      .then(function (r) { return r.json(); })
      .then(function (cfg) {
        if (cfg && cfg.bookUrl) { BOOK = cfg.bookUrl; book.setAttribute("href", BOOK); }
      })
      .catch(function () { /* the hardcoded address above still works */ });

    book.addEventListener("click", function (e) {
      e.preventDefault();
      location.assign(BOOK);
    });

    again.addEventListener("click", function (e) {
      e.preventDefault();
      location.reload();
    });

    intake.addEventListener("submit", function (e) {
      e.preventDefault();
      var first = document.getElementById("first").value.trim();
      if (!first) {
        err.textContent = "Please put in your first name so we can put it on your plan.";
        err.hidden = false;
        document.getElementById("first").focus();
        return;
      }
      err.hidden = true;
      remember();
      load(first, document.getElementById("goal").value.trim());
    });

    function remember() {
      try {
        sessionStorage.setItem("fh_opt", JSON.stringify({
          first_name: document.getElementById("first").value,
          last_name: document.getElementById("last").value,
          email: document.getElementById("email").value,
          goal: document.getElementById("goal").value
        }));
      } catch (e) { /* private mode — the page still works */ }
    }

    function load(first, goal) {
      var btn = document.getElementById("build");
      btn.textContent = "Building your roadmap…";
      btn.disabled = true;
      fetch("/api/public/optimize?view=roadmap", { headers: { accept: "application/json" } })
        .then(function (r) { return r.json(); })
        .then(function (data) {
          if (!data || data.ok !== true) throw new Error("bad shape");
          draw(data, first, goal);
        })
        .catch(function () {
          btn.textContent = "Build my roadmap";
          btn.disabled = false;
          err.textContent = "We could not build your roadmap just now. Please try again, " +
            "or book a call and we will go through it with you.";
          err.hidden = false;
        });
    }

    function el(tag, cls, text) {
      var n = document.createElement(tag);
      if (cls) n.className = cls;
      if (text != null) n.textContent = text;
      return n;
    }

    function dollars(n) {
      return "$" + Number(n).toLocaleString("en-US");
    }

    /* `observed` is a plain value on a tradeline finding and an object on an
       inquiry one. Printing the object gives "[object Object]", so each key is
       spelled out instead. Never show a person a shape. */
    function readable(v) {
      if (v == null || v === "") return "";
      if (typeof v !== "object") return String(v);
      var out = [];
      for (var k in v) {
        if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(v, k)) out.push(k + ": " + String(v[k]));
      }
      return out.join(" · ");
    }

    function draw(data, first, goal) {
      document.getElementById("intro").hidden = true;
      intake.hidden = true;

      document.getElementById("plantitle").textContent = first + "'s Plan";
      var goalLine = document.getElementById("plangoal");
      goalLine.textContent = goal
        ? "What you told us you want: " + goal.toLowerCase() + "."
        : "Here is what we go through together on your call.";
      document.getElementById("planhead").hidden = false;

      /* NEVER let an example read as their own file. The server says which it is
         and the notice is keyed off that, so it disappears by itself the day a
         real pull exists — no code change needed. */
      if (data.source !== "file") {
        document.getElementById("sampletext").textContent =
          "This plan is built on an example credit file, not on yours. We cannot read " +
          "your report until you have pulled it and we have gone through it with you. " +
          "It shows you the shape of the work and the order we do it in. The names, " +
          "balances and dates below are not yours.";
        document.getElementById("sample").hidden = false;
      }

      drawStats(data);
      drawAccounts(data.accounts || []);
      drawFindings(data.findings || []);
      drawLawbook(data.findings || []);
      drawSteps(data.rounds || [], data.findings || []);

      document.getElementById("plan").hidden = false;
      document.getElementById("close").hidden = false;
      window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: "smooth" });
    }

    function stat(key, value, unknown) {
      var box = el("div", "stat");
      box.appendChild(el("span", "k", key));
      box.appendChild(el("div", unknown ? "v unknown" : "v", value));
      return box;
    }

    /* A preapproval of 0 can mean "we never had the credit limit", NOT "you
       qualify for nothing". The server sends preapprovalKnown so the page can
       tell those apart. An unknown figure is SAID to be unknown, never drawn
       as a zero. */
    function drawStats(data) {
      var box = document.getElementById("stats");
      var today = data.today || {};
      var later = data.later || {};
      var known = today.preapprovalKnown === true;

      box.appendChild(stat("Where you are now",
        known ? dollars(today.preapproval) : "Not known yet", !known));
      box.appendChild(stat("After the work",
        known && later.preapproval ? dollars(later.preapproval) : "We size this on the call",
        !(known && later.preapproval)));
      box.appendChild(stat("Card use",
        today.util ? String(today.util) : "Not known yet", !today.util));
    }

    function drawAccounts(accounts) {
      if (!accounts.length) return;
      var box = document.getElementById("accounts");
      accounts.forEach(function (a) {
        var row = el("div", "row");
        var top = el("div", "top");
        top.appendChild(el("span", "name", a.name || "Account"));
        var limit = a.limit != null ? dollars(a.limit) : "limit not reported";
        top.appendChild(el("span", "meta",
          (a.balance != null ? dollars(a.balance) : "balance unknown") + " of " + limit));
        row.appendChild(top);
        if (a.target) row.appendChild(el("p", "why", "Where we aim it: " + a.target));
        box.appendChild(row);
      });
      document.getElementById("acctpanel").hidden = false;
    }

    function drawFindings(findings) {
      if (!findings.length) return;
      var box = document.getElementById("findings");
      findings.forEach(function (f) {
        var row = el("div", "row");
        var top = el("div", "top");
        var who = f.creditor || "This item";
        if (f.account_last4) who += " · ending " + f.account_last4;
        top.appendChild(el("span", "name", who));
        var meta = [f.bureau, f.severity].filter(Boolean).join(" · ");
        if (meta) top.appendChild(el("span", "meta", meta));
        row.appendChild(top);

        if (f.reason) row.appendChild(el("p", "why", f.reason));

        var observed = readable(f.observed);
        var expected = readable(f.expected);
        if (observed || expected) {
          var pair = el("div", "pair");
          if (observed) pair.appendChild(el("div", null, "What the report says: " + observed));
          if (expected) pair.appendChild(el("div", null, "What it should say: " + expected));
          row.appendChild(pair);
        }

        /* THE POINT OF THIS PAGE. Every finding the engine returns carries the
           rule that was broken. Showing the section number next to the item is
           what separates "something looks wrong" from "here is the law that
           says it is wrong". Printed exactly as the engine wrote it — nothing
           here paraphrases a statute. */
        var cites = (f.citations || []).slice();
        if (cites.length || f.metro2Ref) {
          var law = el("div", "law");
          law.appendChild(el("span", "h", "The rule this breaks"));
          var ul = document.createElement("ul");
          cites.forEach(function (c) { ul.appendChild(el("li", null, c)); });
          if (f.metro2Ref) ul.appendChild(el("li", "field", f.metro2Ref));
          law.appendChild(ul);
          row.appendChild(law);
        }

        box.appendChild(row);
      });
      document.getElementById("findpanel").hidden = false;
    }

    /* Every distinct rule cited across the whole file, once each. The engine
       writes its citations as "FCRA § 1681e(b) (maximum possible accuracy)" —
       the part in brackets is its own plain-words gloss, authored in the repo.
       It is split out and shown as the explanation. NOTHING here writes its own
       description of a law. */
    function drawLawbook(findings) {
      var seen = {};
      var order = [];
      findings.forEach(function (f) {
        (f.citations || []).forEach(function (c) {
          if (seen[c]) return;
          seen[c] = true;
          order.push(c);
        });
      });
      if (!order.length) return;

      var box = document.getElementById("lawbook");
      order.forEach(function (c) {
        var item = el("div", "item");
        var open = c.indexOf(" (");
        var head = open > -1 ? c.slice(0, open) : c;
        var gloss = open > -1 ? c.slice(open + 2).replace(/\)$/, "") : "";
        item.appendChild(el("div", "cite", head));
        /* A statute's bracket says what it covers. A court case's bracket is the
           court and the year ("M.D. Pa. 2021") — printing that as "what it
           covers" is nonsense, so a case is labelled as a case. */
        var isCase = / v\. /.test(head);
        if (gloss) {
          item.appendChild(el("div", "plain",
            isCase ? "A court case that ruled on this. Decided by " + gloss + "."
                   : "What it covers: " + gloss + "."));
        }
        box.appendChild(item);
      });
      document.getElementById("lawpanel").hidden = false;
    }

    /* The engine's `when` is written for staff — internal operating shorthand
       about which letter pack to send and on what condition. It is not something
       to put in front of a person who is deciding whether to trust us. These are
       the same six steps in plain words.

       A step id that is NOT in here shows no timing line at all rather than
       leaking the staff wording. src/http/roadmap-html.test.mjs fails if the
       engine ever returns a step this map does not cover, so a new round is
       caught in the suite instead of on someone's screen.

       NO DURATION IS INVENTED HERE. Nothing says how many months anything takes,
       because nothing in the engine knows that. The only number below is the
       30-day answer window, and it is printed ONLY when the findings actually
       cite the section that grants it. */
    var STEP_WORDS = {
      R1: "We challenge every item listed above, in writing, with the bureau.",
      R2: "If they say an item is correct, or never write back, we make them show " +
          "how they checked it.",
      R3: "If the item still stands, we send a final written notice.",
      R4: "If that does not work, we file a complaint with the Consumer Financial " +
          "Protection Bureau, the federal agency that oversees them.",
      R5: "We file with your state attorney general as well.",
      R6: "We send the final notice again."
    };

    function drawSteps(rounds, findings) {
      if (!rounds.length) return;

      /* Grounded, not assumed: only say "30 days" when the file actually cites
         the section that gives them 30 days. */
      var grants30 = (findings || []).some(function (f) {
        return (f.citations || []).some(function (c) { return /1681i\(a\)\(1\)/.test(c); });
      });

      var box = document.getElementById("steps");
      rounds.forEach(function (r) {
        var now = r.status === "current";
        var step = el("div", now ? "step now" : "step");
        step.appendChild(el("span", "no", r.step || ""));
        step.appendChild(el("h3", null, r.title || ""));
        var words = STEP_WORDS[r.step];
        if (words) {
          if (r.step === "R1" && grants30) {
            words += " By law they have 30 days to answer.";
          }
          step.appendChild(el("p", "when", words));
        }
        if (now) {
          var tag = el("span", "tag now", "We start here");
          step.appendChild(tag);
        }
        if (r.attacks && r.attacks.length) {
          var ul = document.createElement("ul");
          r.attacks.forEach(function (a) { ul.appendChild(el("li", null, a)); });
          step.appendChild(ul);
        }
        box.appendChild(step);
      });
      document.getElementById("stepspanel").hidden = false;
    }
  })();
</script>
<script src="/funnel/fh-attribution.js"></script>

<script>
/* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   THIS PAGE IS BOTH ENDS OF THE FLOW: the form that asks for a link, and the
   landing spot the emailed link points at.

   WHY THE EMAIL POINTS HERE AND NOT AT THE API. A magic link works exactly
   once, so whatever opens it first spends it — and mailbox providers and
   corporate mail gateways routinely fetch every URL in a message to scan it. An
   emailed link pointing straight at the verification endpoint therefore gets
   burned before the human ever clicks, and the client is told, correctly, that
   their link no longer works.

   A scanner fetching THIS url consumes nothing: it is a static HTML file. Only
   a real browser runs the script below, and only the script POSTs the token to
   /api/auth/magic-link-verify. That POST is the single use.

   THE TOKEN IS TAKEN OUT OF THE ADDRESS BAR IMMEDIATELY. history.replaceState
   runs before the network call, so the credential is not left in the URL for a
   screenshot, a shared tab, a bookmark or the next page's Referer header.
   ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */

/* esc — same helper every screen in this repo defines (public/app/shell.js,
   public/login.html). Everything that reaches innerHTML goes through it. The
   text below is our own, but the habit is the point: the day one of these
   strings starts arriving over the wire, an escaped page shows the tag and an
   unescaped one runs it. */
function esc(v) {
  return String(v == null ? "" : v)
    .replace(/&/g, "&amp;").replace(/</g, "&lt;").replace(/>/g, "&gt;")
    .replace(/"/g, "&quot;").replace(/'/g, "&#39;");
}

var elErr  = document.getElementById("err");
var elOk   = document.getElementById("ok-box");
var elBusy = document.getElementById("busy");
var elForm = document.getElementById("f");
var elLede = document.getElementById("lede");
var elGo   = document.getElementById("go");
var elEmail = document.getElementById("email");

/* Prefill from ?email= on the funding-delivery CTA (and any portal deep link). */
(function prefillEmailFromQuery() {
  try {
    var q = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get("email") || "";
    if (q && elEmail && !elEmail.value) elEmail.value = q;
  } catch (_e) { /* ignore */ }
})();

function showError(msg) {
  elErr.innerHTML = esc(msg);
  elErr.style.display = "block";
}
function clearError() { elErr.style.display = "none"; elErr.innerHTML = ""; }

/* ── LANDING: a link was clicked ─────────────────────────────────────────── */

function tokenFromUrl() {
  try { return new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get("t") || ""; }
  catch (e) { return ""; }
}

function stripTokenFromUrl() {
  try { window.history.replaceState({}, document.title, window.location.pathname); }
  catch (e) { /* an old browser keeps the token in the bar; the link is still spent */ }
}

async function exchange(token) {
  elForm.style.display = "none";
  elLede.style.display = "none";
  elBusy.style.display = "block";

  var data = null;
  try {
    var r = await fetch("/api/auth/magic-link-verify", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "content-type": "application/json", accept: "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({ token: token })
    });
    data = await r.json();
  } catch (e) {
    /* fetch itself failed — no API deployed, or no network. Say that, rather
       than "your link is bad", which would send somebody to request a second
       link that will fail in exactly the same way. */
    elBusy.style.display = "none";
    elForm.style.display = "";
    elLede.style.display = "";
    showError("We could not reach Fundhub to check your link. Check your connection and try the link again.");
    return;
  }

  elBusy.style.display = "none";

  if (data && data.ok && data.token) {
    /* The app reads its token from localStorage (public/app/shell.js), and the
       endpoint also set an HttpOnly cookie. Storing it here is what makes the
       portal's own fetches work; the cookie is what makes a cold reload work.
       Same two transports the password login already uses. */
    try { localStorage.setItem("fh_token", data.token); } catch (e) {}
    /* THE ACCOUNT, NOT JUST THE TOKEN. The endpoint answers with `account` —
       the principal built in src/auth/magic-link.mjs — and that object carries
       clientId, which is the only thing /app/client-portal.html has to find
       this person's own file with. There is no ?id= in the address bar on a
       link landing, so dropping it here is why clicking the emailed link
       arrived at "We could not load your file." public/login.html already
       stores it for the password path, comment and all; this is that same
       line, not a new idea, and the API shape is untouched.

       A MISSING ACCOUNT IS REMOVED, NOT LEFT BEHIND. Signing out does not clear
       this key, so a previous person's id can still be sitting in it — and
       adopting it would put one client's id on another client's screen. */
    try {
      if (data.account) localStorage.setItem("fh_account", JSON.stringify(data.account));
      else localStorage.removeItem("fh_account");
      /* The role hint public/app/shell.js reads before the session answers, for
         the same reason public/login.html writes it: a stale "owner" left by an
         earlier staff sign-in on this browser makes the portal take its STAFF
         branches, which call two staff-only routes and paint a failure at a
         client who is signed in perfectly well. It grants nothing — every
         endpoint gates server-side, and shell.js replaces this with the real
         session's answer a moment later. */
      var kind = data.principal || (data.account && data.account.kind) || "";
      if (kind) localStorage.setItem("fh_role", String(kind).trim().toLowerCase());
      else localStorage.removeItem("fh_role");
    } catch (e) { /* private mode — the token above already failed the same way */ }
    /* A browser that fell back to fh.js's offline mock at some point has
       fh_demo set, and while it is set NOTHING in the app contacts the real
       backend again (see the note in public/login.html). A real session must
       clear it or the portal will draw sample data over a live sign-in. */
    try {
      localStorage.removeItem("fh_demo");
      localStorage.removeItem("fh_demo_staff");
    } catch (e) {}
    window.location.replace(data.next || "/app/client-portal.html");
    return;
  }

  elForm.style.display = "";
  elLede.style.display = "";
  showError(
    (data && data.message) ||
    "That sign-in link did not work. Ask for a new one below."
  );
  /* Pre-fill nothing. We do not know whose link it was — the endpoint
     deliberately does not say — and guessing an address here would put one
     person's email on another person's screen. */
}

/* ── FORM: ask for a link ────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

elForm.addEventListener("submit", async function (ev) {
  ev.preventDefault();
  clearError();
  elOk.style.display = "none";

  var email = String(elEmail.value || "").trim();
  if (!email) return;

  elGo.disabled = true;
  elGo.textContent = "Sending…";

  var data = null;
  try {
    var r = await fetch("/api/auth/magic-link", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "content-type": "application/json", accept: "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({ email: email })
    });
    data = await r.json();
  } catch (e) {
    elGo.disabled = false;
    elGo.textContent = "Email me a sign-in link";
    showError("We could not reach Fundhub. Check your connection and try again.");
    return;
  }

  elGo.disabled = false;
  elGo.textContent = "Email me a sign-in link";

  if (data && data.ok) {
    /* THE SAME PANEL FOR EVERY ADDRESS. The server answers identically whether
       or not the address has a portal — that is deliberate, so this form cannot
       be used to find out who is a Fundhub client — and this page must not
       undo it by rendering two different states. There is one success state and
       the server's own sentence goes in it. */
    elOk.innerHTML = esc(data.message || "If that email address has a Fundhub portal, a sign-in link is on its way.");
    elOk.style.display = "block";
    elForm.style.display = "none";
    elLede.style.display = "none";
    return;
  }

  showError(
    (data && data.message) ||
    (data && data.error === "email_required"
      ? "That does not look like an email address."
      : "Something went wrong. Try again in a moment.")
  );
});

/* ── BOOT ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

(function boot() {
  var t = tokenFromUrl();
  if (!t) return;              // ordinary visit: just show the form
  stripTokenFromUrl();         // before the network call, not after
  exchange(t);
})();
</script>
</body></html>

<!--
  THE CLIENT PROGRESS PAGE.

  IT LIVES AT THE SITE ROOT AND NOT UNDER /app/, FOR THE REASON public/contract.html
  GIVES AT ITS OWN :14-24. Every file in public/app/ loads shell.js, and shell.js
  grants a `client` principal exactly one screen — ROLE_TABS.client is
  ["client-portal.html"] (public/app/shell.js:356). A second client screen under
  /app/ would therefore have to widen that list for everybody. It also loads
  data.js, which attaches a STAFF bearer token to every request. Neither belongs
  on a page a customer opens.

  THE SERVER DECIDES WHO IS SIGNED IN. Every read sends the `fh_token` from
  localStorage as an Authorization header when there is one (a client's magic
  link writes it, public/portal-login.html:147), and always sends the
  fundhub_session cookie (credentials: same-origin). Staff signed in by cookie
  have no fh_token, and page code cannot read that httpOnly cookie, so this page
  never checks for a sign-in itself. A 401 from the server, and only that, sends
  the visitor to /portal-login.html. It never guesses a client id from the
  address bar: the server pins a client principal to itself.

  IT HOLDS NO SERVER-RENDERED HTML AND NEVER WILL. Everything below the fold is
  built here, in the browser, from the JSON facts described in
  ops/workflows/portal-progress-contract.md. Storing generated markup would put
  a second copy of the truth on disk and would reopen the stored-HTML hole that
  api/documents/[id].mjs:33-70 was hardened to close. There is exactly ONE
  escape function on this page, esc(), and every value that reaches innerHTML
  goes through it.

  IT ANSWERS THREE QUESTIONS, IN THIS ORDER, EVERY VISIT:
    1. Where am I?              — the stage card
    2. What moved?              — the score panels and the movement line
    3. What is next, and whose  — exactly ONE item, labelled "us" or "you"
       job is it?

  WHAT IT MUST NEVER SAY, and the guards that hold each one:
    - A score that was never pulled reads "not pulled yet". Never 0, never a
      blank a client could mistake for a low number. See scoreText().
    - A complaint to a federal regulator or a state attorney general is NEVER
      described as lodged or accepted. Nothing in this system records whether one
      was actually submitted (src/metro2/letters/catalog.mjs:57-65). See
      roundNote().
    - A paid alternative that is null is not free. It is simply absent.
      See waypointCard().
    - The banned industry term for this service does not appear anywhere in this
      file, comments included, so a grep over the shipped page is clean without
      anyone having to judge what counts as copy. Owner-set: client-facing words
      are funding-optimisation and capital-readiness language.

  NO NEW DEPENDENCY. No framework, no chart library, no date library. The one
  chart on this page is a hand-written SVG polyline, which is the same technique
  scripts/black-reports/fundhub_gen.py already uses for all nine of its charts.
-->
